@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:355

The AI SDK reactor extracts prompt, completion, total, cached, and uncached token usage.

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:395

The AI SDK reactor writes `context.llm` trace events containing model and token usage.

### Key architectural tension

`expandEvents` is useful, but it is too broad to be the only compaction abstraction.

It can:

- expand document references;
- normalize event forms;
- attach derived snippets;
- perform pure deterministic transformations;
- call durable steps when configured by a builder.

But a production context compaction feature needs additional semantics:

- explicit token budget;
- explicit model context limit;
- raw versus compacted segment manifest;
- source links back to raw events and parts;
- cost/latency accounting for the compaction call itself;
- replay policy;
- rollback/audit policy;
- authority classes for rules, user instructions, memories, retrieved sources, and old transcript text;
- threshold decisions that explain why compaction happened.

If compaction is only an `expandEvents` implementation, those semantics are likely to become hidden application code. That would make compaction hard to audit and hard to standardize across Ekairos consumers.

### Proposed breaking abstraction: context projection

The proposed central abstraction is a first-class projection step between raw event loading and reactor invocation.

Current conceptual flow:

```text
raw events
-> expandEvents
-> reactor
-> store.itemsToModelMessages
-> model call
-> event_parts
-> trace
```

Proposed conceptual flow:

```text
raw events
-> expandEvents for source expansion only
-> buildContextProjection
-> optional compaction/retrieval/rule activation
-> projection manifest
-> model messages
-> reactor model call
-> event_parts
-> trace events including projection/compaction ids
```

The breaking part is intentional: the reactor should not be responsible for deciding how an event transcript fits into a model window. The reactor should execute model I/O against a projection that has already been selected, budgeted, and traced.

### Projection object shape

This is a design sketch, not code.

```text
ContextProjection
  id
  contextId
  executionId
  stepId
  iteration
  modelProvider
  modelName
  modelContextWindowTokens
  promptBudgetTokens
  outputReserveTokens
  inputTokenEstimate
  inputTokenActual
  strategy
  createdAt
  segments[]
  decisions[]
  sourceLinks[]
  warnings[]
```

Each segment should explain what it is and why it was included:

```text
ContextProjectionSegment
  id
  kind
  authorityClass
  role
  inclusionMode
  tokenEstimate
  sourceStart
  sourceEnd
  sourceLinks[]
  contentMode
  content
```

Suggested `kind` values:

```text
system_instructions
developer_instructions
project_rules
context_state
current_user_request
explicit_user_reference
recent_event_window
tool_schema
retrieved_source
migration_artifact
compacted_history
summary_of_tool_noise
omitted_source_notice
reserve
```

Suggested `contentMode` values:

```text
raw
provider_native_reference
summary
citation_only
redacted
omitted
```

Suggested `inclusionMode` values:

```text
always
scope_match
explicit_reference
retrieval_score
recency_window
compaction_output
budget_reserve
manual_operator_selection
```

### Decision records

Every projection should record decisions separately from the text sent to the model.

```text
ContextCompactionDecision
  id
  projectionId
  decisionType
  reason
  threshold
  observedValue
  selectedStrategy
  rejectedStrategies[]
  createdAt
```

Important decision types:

```text
budget_check
compaction_triggered
compaction_skipped
provider_native_compaction_selected
local_llm_summary_selected
retrieval_selected
retrieval_rejected
rule_activated
rule_rejected
source_omitted
source_redacted
reserve_allocated
```

For example:

```text
decisionType: compaction_triggered
reason: estimated input tokens exceeded prompt budget after preserving stable instructions, current request, and recent event window
threshold: 110000
observedValue: 147500
selectedStrategy: local_llm_hierarchical_summary
rejectedStrategies:
  - provider_native_compaction: not available for configured provider
  - tail_prune: violates migration audit policy
```

This is the opposite of a silent summarization heuristic. A reviewer can inspect why the projection changed.

### Source links

Source links are mandatory because compaction must be reversible by replay and auditable by humans.

```text
ContextProjectionSourceLink
  projectionId
  segmentId
  sourceEntity
  sourceId
  sourcePartKey
  sourceTraceKey
  sourcePath
  sourceOffset
  sourceHash
  relation
```

Suggested `sourceEntity` values:

```text
event_context
event_item
event_execution
event_step
event_part
event_trace_event
document_document
code_file
migration_report
schema_plan
external_provider_compaction
```

Suggested `relation` values:

```text
contains_raw
summarizes
cites
retrieved_from
redacts
omits
supersedes
```

The compactor should not be allowed to emit a summary segment with no source links. That would break migration-grade auditability.

### Trigger policy

The trigger should be based on estimated prompt pressure, not only message count.

Inputs:

```text
modelContextWindowTokens
configuredPromptBudgetRatio
configuredOutputReserveTokens
estimatedStableInstructionTokens
estimatedCurrentRequestTokens
estimatedRecentWindowTokens
estimatedToolSchemaTokens
estimatedRetrievedContextTokens
estimatedHistoricalTranscriptTokens
cachedPromptTokensFromPreviousCalls
lastActualPromptTokens
lastActualUncachedPromptTokens
```

Basic trigger formula:

```text
promptBudgetTokens =
  floor(modelContextWindowTokens * promptBudgetRatio) - outputReserveTokens

mustKeepTokens =
  stableInstructions
  + currentUserRequest
  + explicitReferences
  + recentWindow
  + requiredToolSchemas

compressibleTokens =
  totalEstimatedInputTokens - mustKeepTokens

triggerCompaction when:
  totalEstimatedInputTokens > promptBudgetTokens
  or
  compressibleTokens > configuredCompressibleHistoryLimit
  or
  lastActualPromptTokens > highWatermark
```

Recommended first defaults for design discussion:

```text
promptBudgetRatio: 0.78
outputReserveTokens: max(12000, modelContextWindowTokens * 0.08)
recentWindowMinTurns: 2
recentWindowMinTokens: 20000
stableInstructionMaxTokens: 10000
toolSchemaMaxTokens: 12000
retrievalMaxTokens: 30000
compactedHistoryTargetTokens: 18000
```

These numbers are intentionally proposed as first-pass defaults for review, not implementation constants.

### Why actual usage metrics matter

The AI SDK step already records prompt, completion, cached, uncached, and total token usage in the LLM trace path. That means the compaction strategy can be calibrated against real usage after the first model call.

Useful feedback loop:

```text
step N projection token estimate
-> step N actual prompt tokens from provider usage
-> estimate error ratio
-> step N+1 budget adjustment
-> trace projected versus actual
```

Example trace payload fields:

```text
projectionId
estimatedPromptTokens
actualPromptTokens
estimateErrorRatio
cachedPromptTokens
uncachedPromptTokens
compactionStrategy
compactionInputTokens
compactionOutputTokens
compactionLatencyMs
```

This should not wait until a separate observability product exists. It can piggyback on the existing trace event model as a source of operational truth.

### Where not to put responsibilities

Do not put source authority policy in the summarization prompt only.

Reason:

- the prompt can ask the model to preserve authority boundaries, but the data model must also preserve them.

Do not put projection budget selection inside provider-specific reactors.

Reason:

- compaction is an engine-level concern that should work across AI SDK, scripted, OpenAI-native, Anthropic-native, and future reactors.

Do not mutate `event_items.content.parts` to store compressed replacements.

Reason:

- the package already treats `event_parts` as source of truth for replay, and migration audit requires raw history.

Do not make auto-memory equivalent to rules.

Reason:

- current agent systems distinguish durable rules from retrieved memories; Ekairos should carry that distinction because org/project policy must outrank auto-generated session facts.

Do not hide compaction inside `expandEvents` as application-specific text rewriting.

Reason:

- `expandEvents` is currently useful as a source expansion hook, but the projection manifest, trigger decision, and trace records need standard engine-level semantics.

### Integration proposal A: conservative projection wrapper

This proposal adds a projection wrapper while leaving most existing flow intact conceptually.

Flow:

```text
rawEvents = store.getItems(context)
expandedEvents = story.expandEvents(rawEvents, context, env, runtime)
projection = buildProjectionFromEvents(expandedEvents, budget, strategy)
reactor receives projection.events and projection.manifest
AI SDK reactor still uses itemsToModelMessages initially
trace receives projection summary
```

Advantages:

- smaller conceptual move from the current loop;
- easier to test against existing `context.output-parts` replay behavior;
- can start with projection manifest and no LLM summarizer;
- can emit trace events without changing all reactors at once.

Disadvantages:

- still lets reactors convert items to model messages;
- projection and provider message conversion remain split;
- harder to enforce model-message budget exactly before reactor call.

Best fit:

- first implementation after technical approval if the team wants minimal package blast radius.

### Integration proposal B: reactor receives model messages

This proposal moves provider-facing message construction before reactor invocation.

Flow:

```text
rawEvents = store.getItems(context)
expandedEvents = story.expandEvents(rawEvents, context, env, runtime)
projection = buildContextProjection(expandedEvents, all sources, budget, strategy)
messagesForModel = projection.toModelMessages()
reactor receives messagesForModel plus projection manifest
reactor only executes provider call and maps output/tool calls
```

Advantages:

- clean separation between context selection and model execution;
- prompt budget can be enforced before model call;
- every reactor sees the same projection contract;
- easier to compare providers and compactors.

Disadvantages:

- breaking reactor contract;
- more tests need updates;
- scripted reactors and fixtures need an explicit projection payload;
- store/model-message conversion ownership moves.

Best fit:

- target architecture for a non-retrocompatible compaction release.

### Integration proposal C: projection as durable step

This proposal makes projection construction itself a durable step.

Flow:

```text
rawEvents = store.getItems(context)
expandedEvents = story.expandEvents(rawEvents, context, env, runtime)
projectionStep = run durable projection step
if compaction needed:
  run durable compaction model call
  persist compaction artifact and source links
messagesForModel = projection.modelMessages
reactor executes task model call
```

Advantages:

- replay-safe;
- failed compaction can be retried independently from task model execution;
- compaction costs and latency are visible;
- deterministic projection can be separated from LLM summarization;
- aligns with durable workflow semantics.

Disadvantages:

- more operational surface;
- projection failure states need UX and trace handling;
- may require additional entities or trace conventions.

Best fit:

- production migration workloads where auditability matters more than minimal latency.

### Recommended staged design path

Stage 0: documentation and decision review

- keep writing and refining proposals;
- collect technical-leader decisions;
- do not change schema/config/code.

Stage 1: projection manifest without compaction

- build a manifest that records raw included segments;
- estimate tokens;
- emit trace events;
- do not summarize yet.

Stage 2: deterministic budget gates

- fail or warn when prompt pressure crosses thresholds;
- test recent-window preservation;
- prove raw replay still works.

Stage 3: local LLM compaction artifact

- summarize only older low-authority transcript spans;
- preserve current request, explicit references, and recent window raw;
- persist compaction artifacts with source links.

Stage 4: retrieval plane

- introduce retrieval results as separately sourced segments;
- keep retrieval provenance distinct from transcript compaction.

Stage 5: provider-native compaction adapters

- use OpenAI/Anthropic native compaction only where source identity and replay policy are understood;
- store provider compaction ids/artifacts as source links;
- keep application-level fallback explicit.

### Open decisions for the technical leader

1. Should the target architecture break reactor contracts so reactors receive model messages instead of raw/expanded events?
2. Should projection manifests be stored as first-class domain entities or as trace payloads first?
3. Should compaction be allowed inside `expandEvents` at all, or should `expandEvents` be restricted to source expansion?
4. Should the first release fail hard on over-budget prompts, or allow a deterministic tail-prune fallback for non-migration contexts?
5. Should provider-native compaction be permitted in production migration tasks before Ekairos has its own source-link ledger?
6. What is the minimum acceptable human-audit UI/report before org-scoped rollout?

### Strong recommendation

For Ekairos' migration-service identity, the safest target design is Proposal C as the end state, with Stage 1 and Stage 2 used as approval-friendly stepping stones.

The reason is simple: migration context is not normal chat context. A wrong summary can become a wrong production transaction plan. That makes traceability, source links, and rollback more important than saving a small amount of implementation surface.

## Compaction verification strategy for the current test suite

Status: proposal only, pending technical-leader approval. No tests have been added or changed.

The existing tests already contain the right primitives for compaction verification. The compaction feature should extend those primitives instead of creating a parallel test universe.

Important current anchors:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\tests\context.output-parts.test.ts:66

This test verifies that model messages are rebuilt from `event_parts` rather than stale `event_items.content.parts`.

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\tests\context.output-parts.instant.test.ts:166

The Instant-backed output-parts test verifies multipart tool output persistence and replay from `event_parts` as the source of truth.

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\tests\context.scripted-reactor.instant.test.ts:360

The scripted Instant test proves engine-expanded standard events reach provider-neutral reactors.

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\tests\context.ai-sdk-reactor.real.instant.test.ts:186

The real AI SDK Instant test reads `event_trace_events` and persisted steps/items after a model call.

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\tests\_benchmark.ts:83

The benchmark helpers already split context persistence, DSL, reactor, action execution, workflow, and network timing groups.

### Test principle

Compaction tests should prove four things independently:

1. Raw source history is preserved.
2. Projection output is bounded and deterministic enough to inspect.
3. Compaction decisions are traceable.
4. Reconstructed model messages preserve semantic behavior across replay.

The tests should not merely assert that a summary string exists. A summary string can exist while losing a migration decision, authority boundary, or tool-result artifact.

### Unit test group A: projection segment construction

Goal:

- prove that raw events become a projection manifest with stable segment classification.

Suggested fixture:

```text
input:
  system/developer/project rule segment
  current user request
  explicit file reference
  recent assistant output
  older assistant output
  older tool result
  derived document expansion

expected:
  stable instructions are prefix segments
  current user request is raw
  explicit references are raw or cited
  recent window is raw
  older compressible material is marked compactable
  tool results carry source links
  no segment lacks authorityClass
```

Assertions:

```text
projection.segments.length > 0
```

### Unit test group B: budget trigger behavior

Goal:

- prove compaction triggers on token pressure and skips when under budget.

Suggested cases:

```text

case: above budget but only must-keep material remains
expected: hard budget failure or operator gate

case: bad token estimate after provider usage feedback
expected: next projection records estimate correction
```

Assertions:

```text
decisionType is recorded

observedValue is recorded

rejectedStrategies are recorded when alternatives exist
```


### Test sequencing recommendation

Recommended order after architecture approval:

1. Unit tests for projection segment classification.
2. Unit tests for budget trigger decisions.
3. Unit tests extending replay from `event_parts`.
4. Scripted Instant integration test for projection contract.
5. Trace integration test for projection and compaction events.
6. Real-model smoke for summary fact preservation.
7. Benchmark report expansion.
8. Property/noise regression fixtures.

The important sequencing point is that replay and source-link correctness should be proven before trusting LLM summary quality.

## Selector and compactor pseudocode for Ekairos

Status: proposal only, pending technical-leader approval. No implementation has been done.

Source refresh for this section:

```text
https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/overflow.ts
https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts
https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts
https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction
https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/methods/compact
```

Relevant external mechanics:

- OpenCode reserves context headroom before declaring usable input capacity.
- OpenCode estimates selected message size by converting internal messages into model messages and estimating the serialized payload.
- OpenCode tail selection keeps recent turns according to configured tail turns and a preservation budget.
- OpenCode hides prior completed compaction message pairs when making the next compaction prompt.
- OpenCode lets plugins inject compaction context or replace the compaction prompt.
- OpenCode strips media and caps tool output when constructing the compaction model input.
- OpenCode can mark processing as needing compaction when a context overflow error occurs and then returns a `"compact"` result from the processor.
- Anthropic server-side compaction has a trigger threshold, optional pause-after-compaction behavior, custom instructions that replace the default prompt, compaction blocks that must be carried forward, and separate usage accounting for compaction iterations.
- OpenAI exposes a `/responses/compact` endpoint that returns a compacted response object and compaction items.

The Ekairos design should learn from those mechanisms but remain stricter because `@ekairos/events` is meant to support migration-grade audit.

### Pseudocode 1: top-level projection builder

```text
function buildContextProjection(input):
  rawEvents = input.rawEvents
  context = input.context
  model = input.model
  budget = resolveModelBudget(model, input.config)

  sources = collectProjectionSources({
    rawEvents,
    context,
    explicitReferences: input.explicitReferences,
    rules: input.rules,
    retrievalResults: input.retrievalResults,
    priorCompactions: input.priorCompactions,
    traceUsage: input.traceUsage
  })

  classified = classifySources(sources)

  estimates = estimateSegments(classified, {
    model,
    estimator: input.estimator,
    fallbackEstimator: "chars_to_tokens"
  })

  decision = decideProjectionStrategy({
    classified,
    estimates,
    budget,
    migrationMode: input.migrationMode
  })

  if decision.kind == "under_budget":
    return projection({
      strategy: "raw_projection",
      segments: renderRawSegments(classified, estimates, budget),
      decisions: [decision],
      sourceLinks: sourceLinksFor(classified)
    })

  if decision.kind == "over_budget_no_compressible_material":
    return failProjection({
      reason: "must_keep_material_exceeds_budget",
      decisions: [decision],
      sourceLinks: sourceLinksFor(classified)
    })

  compacted = compactCompressibleHistory({
    classified,
    estimates,
    budget,
    strategy: decision.selectedStrategy,
    priorCompactions: input.priorCompactions
  })

  validated = validateProjection({
    segments: compacted.segments,
    sourceLinks: compacted.sourceLinks,
    budget,
    invariants: input.invariants
  })

  if !validated.ok:
    return failProjection(validated.failure)

  return projection({
    strategy: decision.selectedStrategy,
    segments: compacted.segments,
    decisions: [decision, ...compacted.decisions, ...validated.decisions],
    sourceLinks: compacted.sourceLinks,
    warnings: validated.warnings
  })
```

Important difference from OpenCode:

- OpenCode can compact into a session summary and continue.
- Ekairos should also produce a projection manifest and source-link ledger.
- OpenCode can mark old tool output compacted.
- Ekairos should not destructively compact raw `event_parts`; it should render old tool output as omitted/summary/citation in the projection while preserving the raw row.

### Pseudocode 2: budget resolver

```text
function resolveModelBudget(model, config):
  contextWindow = config.overrideContextWindow ?? model.contextWindow
  maxOutput = config.overrideMaxOutput ?? model.maxOutput

  if contextWindow <= 0:
    return {
      known: false,
      policy: "require_explicit_budget"
    }

  reservedForOutput =
    config.outputReserveTokens ??
    max(12000, floor(contextWindow * 0.08), maxOutput)

  reservedForSystemDrift =
    config.systemReserveTokens ??
    min(20000, floor(contextWindow * 0.05))

  promptBudget =
    floor(contextWindow * (config.promptBudgetRatio ?? 0.78))
    - reservedForOutput
    - reservedForSystemDrift

  return {
    known: true,
    contextWindow,
    promptBudget: max(0, promptBudget),
    outputReserve: reservedForOutput,
    systemReserve: reservedForSystemDrift
  }
```

Why this is not exactly OpenCode:

- OpenCode uses a compact fixed buffer style and provider transform output max logic.
- Ekairos should expose the budget pieces in the projection manifest because migration reviewers need to see why context was compressed.

### Pseudocode 3: source classification

```text
function classifySources(sources):
  segments = []

  for source in sources:
    if source.kind in ["system", "developer", "platform_policy"]:
      segments.push(classify(source, {
        kind: "system_instructions",
        authorityClass: "platform",
        mustKeep: true,
        contentMode: "raw"
      }))
      continue

    if source.kind in ["project_rule", "AGENTS.md", "migration_policy"]:
      segments.push(classify(source, {
        kind: "project_rules",
        authorityClass: "approved_project_rule",
        mustKeep: source.activation == "always" or source.activationMatched,
        contentMode: "raw"
      }))
      continue

    if source.kind == "current_user_request":
      segments.push(classify(source, {
        kind: "current_user_request",
        authorityClass: "current_user",
        mustKeep: true,
        contentMode: "raw"
      }))
      continue

    if source.kind == "explicit_reference":
      segments.push(classify(source, {
        kind: "explicit_user_reference",
        authorityClass: "explicit_reference",
        mustKeep: true,
        contentMode: "raw_or_cited"
      }))
      continue

    if source.kind == "recent_event":
      segments.push(classify(source, {
        kind: "recent_event_window",
        authorityClass: "recent_execution",
        mustKeep: true,
        contentMode: "raw"
      }))
      continue

    if source.kind == "old_event":
      segments.push(classify(source, {
        kind: "historical_transcript",
        authorityClass: "historical",
        mustKeep: false,
        compactable: true
      }))
      continue

    if source.kind == "retrieval_result":
      segments.push(classify(source, {
        kind: "retrieved_source",
        authorityClass: source.authorityClass,
        mustKeep: false,
        selectable: true,
        contentMode: "excerpt_or_citation"
      }))
      continue

    if source.kind == "auto_memory":
      segments.push(classify(source, {
        kind: "memory",
        authorityClass: "auto_memory",
        mustKeep: false,
        selectable: true,
        contentMode: "labeled_excerpt"
      }))
      continue

  return segments
```

Rule:

```text
mustKeep beats compactable
explicit current intent beats old summary
approved rule beats auto memory
raw source authority must survive summary rendering
```

### Pseudocode 4: recent window selector

OpenCode keeps recent tail turns under a budget. Ekairos should do the same, but with stricter structural boundaries.

```text
function selectRecentWindow(events, budget):
  turns = groupIntoTurns(events)
  selected = []
  total = 0

  for turn in reverse(turns):
    estimate = estimateTurn(turn)

    if total + estimate <= budget.recentWindowBudget:
      selected.prepend(turn)
      total += estimate
      continue

    split = maybeSplitTurn(turn, budget.recentWindowBudget - total)

    if split.allowed:
      selected.prepend(split.tail)
      total += split.estimate

    break

  return {
    turns: selected,
    estimatedTokens: total,
    tailStartEventId: selected.first?.eventId
  }
```

`maybeSplitTurn` should be conservative:

```text
allow split:
  long assistant text with paragraph boundaries
  long tool log where a structured summary can cite the raw event_part

disallow split:
  current user request
  approval/rejection decision
  tool call without its paired result
  tool result without its paired tool call
  image/file/tool artifact part
  migration gate decision
  schema transaction plan
```

If a turn cannot be split safely and must-keep material exceeds budget, Ekairos should fail a projection gate instead of inventing a partial prompt.

### Pseudocode 5: compressible history selector

```text
function selectCompressibleHistory(classified, recentWindow):
  candidates = []

  for segment in classified:
    if segment.mustKeep:
      continue
    if segment.sourceId in recentWindow.sourceIds:
      continue
    if segment.kind in ["system_instructions", "project_rules", "current_user_request"]:
      continue
    if segment.kind == "retrieved_source" and segment.wasExplicitlyRequested:
      continue

    candidates.push(segment)

  grouped = groupByContiguousEventRange(candidates)

  return grouped.map(group => ({
    sourceRange: group.range,
    sourceLinks: group.sourceLinks,
    authorityClasses: unique(group.authorityClasses),
    tokenEstimate: sum(group.tokenEstimate),
    summaryTargetTokens: chooseSummaryTarget(group)
  }))
```

The grouping is important. Summarizing every old event independently wastes tokens; summarizing the entire history as one blob destroys source boundaries. Contiguous source ranges are a workable compromise.

### Pseudocode 6: compaction artifact generation

```text
function compactCompressibleHistory(input):
  priorSummary = input.priorCompactions.last?.summary
  compactableGroups = selectCompressibleHistory(input.classified, input.recentWindow)

  if compactableGroups.empty:
    return renderNoCompactionProjection(input)

  compactionPrompt = buildCompactionPrompt({
    priorSummary,
    groups: compactableGroups,
    currentTask: input.currentTask,
    authorityPolicy: input.authorityPolicy,
    requiredFacts: input.requiredFacts,
    forbiddenPromotions: input.forbiddenPromotions,
    outputSchema: "source_labeled_summary"
  })

  compactionResult = runCompactionModel({
    model: input.compactionModel,
    prompt: compactionPrompt,
    sourceMaterial: renderSourceMaterial(compactableGroups, {
      stripMedia: true,
      toolOutputMaxChars: input.toolOutputMaxChars,
      includeSourceIds: true
    })
  })

  artifact = parseAndValidateCompactionResult(compactionResult)

  if !artifact.valid:
    return failProjection({
      reason: "compaction_artifact_invalid",
      errors: artifact.errors
    })

  return mergeProjection({
    mustKeepSegments: input.mustKeepSegments,
    summarySegments: artifact.summarySegments,
    recentWindow: input.recentWindow,
    retrievalSegments: input.retrievalSegments,
    sourceLinks: artifact.sourceLinks
  })
```

OpenCode strips media and caps tool output for compaction model input. Ekairos should do the same for old compressible material, but it must write down what was stripped and where the raw source lives.

### Pseudocode 7: summary validation

```text
function parseAndValidateCompactionResult(result):
  parsed = parseStructuredSummary(result.text)

  checks = [
    hasSummaryText(parsed),
    allClaimsHaveSourceIds(parsed),
    allSourceIdsExist(parsed),
    noHighAuthoritySourceMissing(parsed),
    currentUserRequestNotSummarized(parsed),
    forbiddenPromotionsAbsent(parsed),
    requiredFactsPresent(parsed),
    migrationGateFactsPresent(parsed),
    noToolResultInvented(parsed),
    noSourceAuthorityMerged(parsed)
  ]

  if any checks fail:
    return {
      valid: false,
      errors: failedChecks(checks),
      rawResult: result
    }

  return {
    valid: true,
    summarySegments: parsed.segments,
    sourceLinks: parsed.sourceLinks,
    warnings: parsed.warnings
  }
```

Suggested required facts for migration tasks:

```text
org id
app id
schema version
schema dry-run result
admin runtime resolution
dataset extraction source
transformation script/source
transaction plan id
verification query ids
rollback constraints
manual approval/rejection decisions
```

Suggested forbidden promotions:

```text
rejected idea becomes approved plan
assistant guess becomes user instruction
auto memory becomes project rule
tool error becomes successful result
partial dry run becomes final verification
non-production test result becomes production proof
```

### Pseudocode 8: provider-native compaction adapter

Provider-native compaction should be an optional strategy, not the core source of truth.

```text
function maybeUseProviderNativeCompaction(input):
  if input.provider == "anthropic" and input.modelSupportsAnthropicCompaction:
    if input.policy.allowAnthropicCompaction:
      return runAnthropicCompaction({
        triggerTokens: input.triggerTokens,
        pauseAfterCompaction: true,
        instructions: input.customInstructions,
        messages: input.messages
      })

  if input.provider == "openai" and input.policy.allowOpenAICompactEndpoint:
    return runOpenAIResponsesCompact({
      input: input.responsesInput,
      metadata: input.metadata
    })

  return {
    used: false,
    reason: "provider_native_compaction_not_allowed_or_not_supported"
  }
```

Policy requirement:

```text
provider-native compaction result must be persisted as an external compaction artifact
provider-native compaction must have a source-link equivalent
provider-native compaction must not replace raw event history
provider-native usage accounting must include compaction iterations where the provider exposes them
```

For Anthropic specifically:

- use `pause_after_compaction` when Ekairos needs to preserve recent messages or inject additional source-labeled context after the compaction block;
- aggregate `usage.iterations` when calculating compaction cost;
- treat custom `instructions` as replacing the provider default, so Ekairos must supply a complete migration-safe summary prompt if it customizes.

For OpenAI specifically:

- store returned compaction item ids/content handles as source-linked external artifacts;
- preserve role hierarchy in input messages because developer/system roles outrank user roles;
- do not assume encrypted compaction content is human-auditable unless a readable companion artifact exists.

### Pseudocode 9: projection failure modes

```text
function failProjection(failure):
  emitTrace("context.projection.failed", {
    reason: failure.reason,
    promptBudgetTokens: failure.promptBudgetTokens,
    estimatedMustKeepTokens: failure.estimatedMustKeepTokens,
    estimatedTotalTokens: failure.estimatedTotalTokens,
    suggestedOperatorAction: failure.suggestedOperatorAction
  })

  if failure.reason in [
    "must_keep_material_exceeds_budget",
    "compaction_artifact_invalid",
    "source_link_coverage_failed",
    "forbidden_promotion_detected"
  ]:
    return {
      status: "blocked",
      safeToCallModel: false,
      operatorReviewRequired: true
    }

  return {
    status: "warn",
    safeToCallModel: failure.policy.allowsWarningContinue
  }
```

Do not route a failed compaction into the task model as if it were valid context. That creates the worst possible failure mode: a confident model call operating on silently corrupted context.

### Pseudocode 10: recursive compaction handling

Long-running sessions will compact more than once. Recursive compaction needs explicit handling.

```text
function prepareRecursiveCompaction(history):
  priorCompactions = findCompletedCompactionArtifacts(history)

  visibleHistory = history excluding:
    prior compaction prompt scaffolding
    prior compaction assistant outputs that are superseded

  previousSummary = priorCompactions.last?.summary

  sourceRanges = selectNewCompressibleRanges({
    visibleHistory,
    previousSummary
  })

  return {
    previousSummary,
    sourceRanges,
    hiddenArtifactIds: priorCompactions.supersededIds
  }
```

OpenCode hides prior completed compaction message pairs before constructing the next compaction. Ekairos should preserve that idea, but make the hidden/superseded relationship explicit in the projection source links.

### Pseudocode 11: tool noise handling

OpenCode has a prune mechanism for old tool outputs. Ekairos should treat this as projection pruning, not source mutation.

```text
function renderOldToolOutput(part, policy):
  if part.toolName in policy.protectedTools:
    return rawOrStructuredExcerpt(part)

  if part.isRecent:
    return rawOrStructuredExcerpt(part)

  if part.outputTokenEstimate <= policy.toolOutputRawLimit:
    return rawOrStructuredExcerpt(part)

  return {
    kind: "summary_of_tool_noise",
    contentMode: "summary",
    content: summarizeToolOutput(part),
    sourceLinks: [linkToEventPart(part)],
    omittedBytes: part.outputBytes,
    omittedTokensEstimate: part.outputTokenEstimate
  }
```

Protected tool classes for Ekairos:

```text
migration planner
schema dry-run
admin runtime resolver
dataset extraction
transaction application
verification query
approval gate
security/auth resolver
```

Non-protected candidates:

```text
large directory listings
repeated logs
redundant search results
long dependency install output
low-signal build output after a clearer error summary exists
```

### Pseudocode 12: projection to model messages

```text
function projectionToModelMessages(projection):
  messages = []

  appendSystemAndDeveloperSegments(messages, projection.segments)
  appendRules(messages, projection.segments)
  appendCompactedHistory(messages, projection.segments)
  appendRetrievedSources(messages, projection.segments)
  appendRecentWindow(messages, projection.segments)
  appendCurrentUserRequest(messages, projection.segments)

  validateRoleHierarchy(messages)
  validateNoDanglingToolCalls(messages)
  validateBudget(messages, projection.promptBudgetTokens)

  return messages
```

Role-order warning:

- provider APIs differ;
- the projection manifest should be provider-neutral, but the final message renderer must be provider-aware;
- tool-call pairing rules must be validated after rendering, not only before.

### Hard invariants

```text
raw event_parts are never deleted by compaction
current user request is never summarized
explicit user references are never silently omitted
project rules are never mixed into historical transcript summary
auto memory is always labeled as auto memory
summary segments always have source links
retrieval segments always have source links
projection budget is recorded
compaction trigger reason is recorded
provider usage is recorded when available
failed compaction blocks task model execution unless policy explicitly allows a warning continuation
```

### Operator-facing blocked states

Blocked state examples:

```text
projection_blocked_must_keep_too_large
projection_blocked_missing_source_links
projection_blocked_summary_validation_failed
projection_blocked_provider_compaction_uninspectable
projection_blocked_tool_pair_invalid
projection_blocked_migration_gate_conflict
```

Each blocked state should include:

```text
reason
source ids involved
suggested remediation
whether retrying with a larger model could help
whether reducing retrieved context could help
whether manual operator summary could unblock
```

The goal is not to make compaction impossible; it is to make unsafe compaction visibly impossible.

## First-class data model proposal for projections and compaction

Status: proposal only, pending technical-leader approval. No schema/config/code change has been made.

This section assumes a breaking design. It does not try to preserve the existing reactor/message conversion contract as a permanent compatibility layer.

Current schema anchors:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\schema.ts:7

The existing package already links contexts, items, executions, steps, and parts. The proposed projection model should extend that event-store structure rather than treating compaction as an untracked string stored inside a message.

### Non-retrocompatible stance

The recommended target state:

```text
reactors execute model calls
projection builder owns context selection
stores persist raw source truth
projection entities persist what the model saw
trace events persist operational timing/cost/usage
```

The recommended rejected state:

```text
reactor secretly compacts
expandEvents secretly mutates history
event_items.content.parts is reused as compressed truth
old and new projection modes coexist indefinitely
summary strings exist without source links
```

Breaking changes to expect if approved:

- reactor params change to receive projection metadata and possibly pre-rendered model messages;
- AI SDK step no longer owns message projection policy;
- `itemsToModelMessages` either becomes a lower-level renderer or moves behind projection rendering;
- compaction entities become part of the public events domain;
- tests and fixtures must assert projection semantics directly.

### Data model option 1: trace-only projection

Store projection metadata only as `event_trace_events.payload`.

Entities added:

```text
none
```

Trace event kinds:

```text
context.projection
context.compaction
context.retrieval
```

Advantages:

- no schema expansion for the first experiment;
- lower migration overhead;
- aligns with existing trace event payload flexibility;
- useful for local proof of token and latency behavior.

Disadvantages:

- projection queryability is weak;
- source links are embedded JSON rather than relationally inspectable;
- hard to enforce uniqueness and referential expectations;
- awkward for production audit reports;
- weaker fit for database migration service identity.

Use only for:

- Stage 1 local manifest experiment;
- throwaway calibration;
- benchmarks before schema approval.

Do not use for:

- production migration audit;
- provider-native compaction rollout;
- org-scoped canary with real customer data.

### Data model option 2: first-class projection entities

Add projection and source-link entities to the events domain.

Core entities:

```text
event_context_projections
event_context_projection_segments
event_context_projection_source_links
event_context_compaction_artifacts
event_context_retrieval_queries
event_context_retrieval_results
event_context_rules
event_context_rule_activations
```

This is the recommended target model.

### Entity: event_context_projections

Purpose:

- one projection per model-call attempt;
- records what strategy selected model input;
- records token budgets and estimates;
- links to execution/step/context;
- provides audit root for segments, compaction artifacts, retrieval results, and trace usage.

Conceptual fields:

```text
id
createdAt
updatedAt
status

segmentCount
sourceLinkCount

blockedReason

metadata
```

Suggested indexes:

```text

executionId
stepId
workflowRunId
status

```

Status values:


Important invariant:

```text
at most one used projection per executionId + stepId + iteration + model call attempt
```

### Link proposal

Conceptual links:

```text
event_context_projections -> event_contexts
event_context_projections -> event_executions
event_context_projections -> event_steps
event_context_projection_segments -> event_context_projections
event_context_projection_source_links -> event_context_projections
event_context_projection_source_links -> event_context_projection_segments
event_context_compaction_artifacts -> event_context_projections
event_context_retrieval_queries -> event_context_projections
event_context_retrieval_results -> event_context_retrieval_queries
event_context_retrieval_results -> event_context_projections
event_context_rule_activations -> event_context_projections
event_context_rule_activations -> event_context_rules
```

Current schema style already uses explicit forward/reverse labels for context/items/executions/steps/parts. The projection links should follow that style after approval.

### Data model option 3: mixed model

Store only projection roots and compaction artifacts as entities, and store segments/source links as JSON payloads.

Advantages:

- fewer entity additions;
- better than trace-only;
- simpler first migration.

Disadvantages:

- weak segment/source-link queryability;
- source-link coverage checks require JSON parsing;
- harder to build audit UI/reporting;
- likely to be replaced later.

Recommendation:

```text
do not choose this as the target design
```

It may be acceptable only as a short-lived development spike if the technical leader wants a smaller schema experiment before committing to first-class segment/source-link entities.

### Retention model

Projection data can become large. Retention must be explicit.

Suggested classes:

```text
raw source event history:
  retained according to event package policy

used projection roots:
  retain for audit

used projection segments:
  retain for audit, with content redaction policy if required

source links:
  retain with used projections

failed projection attempts:
  retain short-term with failure reason

retrieval candidates not selected:
  retain short-term or aggregate only

compaction artifacts used in model call:
  retain for audit

superseded compaction artifacts:
  retain at least lineage metadata
```

Migration tasks should use longer retention than ordinary chat contexts.

### Redaction model

Projection entities will store what the model saw. That can include secrets if upstream filtering fails.

Suggested redaction fields:

```text
contentRedacted
redactionReason
redactedAt
redactedBy
rawSourceStillExists
```

Redaction rule:

```text
redacting projection content does not delete source-link metadata
```

Reason:

- audit still needs to know which raw source rows were involved, even if content must be hidden.

### Migration rollout proposal

Because this is schema/domain work, it should only proceed after technical-leader approval.

Proposed rollout artifacts:

```text
schema dry-run plan
per-org matrix
migration script
verification queries
projection fixture report
rollback analysis
```

Minimum verification queries:

```text
count projections by context/execution/step
count segments by projection
count source links by projection
find summary segments with zero source links
find used compaction artifacts with failed validation
find used projections with estimatedPromptTokens > promptBudgetTokens
find rule activations without matching rules
find retrieval results selected but not linked
```

Hard gate:

```text
no production org rollout until planSchemaPush dry-run passes per app and verification queries are approved
```

### Recommendation

For Ekairos, first-class projection entities are the right target.

The core reason is auditability. A trace-only system can answer "what happened roughly?" A first-class projection ledger can answer "what exact sources did the model see, which sources were summarized, why were they selected, what was omitted, and how did that relate to the later migration plan?"

That second question is the one Ekairos needs to answer.

## Worked example: migration session compaction

Status: synthetic design example only. No data was created in InstantDB and no migration code was written.

This example shows how a long Ekairos migration-oriented context could be compacted without losing auditability.

### Scenario

The operator asks Ekairos to prepare a schema migration for an Esolbay workspace:

```text
Task:
  deprecate old supplier story usage
  adopt new context package behavior
  add supplier compliance status to requisition evaluation flow
  ship migration and verification artifacts together

Constraints:
  production org rollout is org-scoped
  schema dry-run must pass per app
  Clerk org matrix must resolve appId/adminToken
  dataset extraction must be auditable
  transaction plan must be idempotent
  verification queries must be included
```

The conversation grows over many iterations:

```text
turn 1:
  user provides task

turn 2:
  assistant inspects package docs and domain schema

turn 3:
  assistant inspects event context engine

turn 4:
  assistant drafts migration plan

turn 5:
  tool output includes huge schema query

turn 6:
  assistant discovers old story references

turn 7:
  tool output includes large grep result

turn 8:
  assistant rejects a shortcut that would skip org gate

turn 9:
  assistant runs schema dry-run in development

turn 10:
  user clarifies production rollout is canary-first

turn 11:
  assistant prepares migration report

turn 12:
  tool output includes verification query results

turn 13:
  context approaches model budget
```

### Raw source event categories

The raw source history contains:

| Category | Example | Treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| current user request | "prepare migration plan" | raw must-keep |
| project rule | "schema dry-run per app" | raw must-keep |
| recent assistant plan | latest transaction plan | raw recent window |
| recent tool result | verification query output | raw or structured excerpt |
| old search output | 400-line grep result | summarize/omit with source link |
| old assistant reasoning | discarded approach discussion | summarize with status |
| rejected shortcut | "skip org gate" rejected | preserve as rejected, never promote |
| prior summary | old compaction summary | use as previous summary lineage |
| migration artifact | draft report | selected as migration_artifact |

### Projection before compaction

Simplified budget:

```text
modelContextWindowTokens: 128000
promptBudgetTokens: 96000
outputReserveTokens: 16000
systemReserveTokens: 6000
estimatedTotalPromptTokens: 137000
estimatedMustKeepTokens: 52000
estimatedCompressibleTokens: 85000
```

Decision:

```text
decisionType: compaction_triggered
reason: estimatedTotalPromptTokens exceeded promptBudgetTokens
selectedStrategy: local_llm_source_labeled_summary
rejectedStrategies:
  provider_native_compaction: not approved for production migration artifacts
  tail_prune: violates source audit policy
  raw_only_larger_model: not configured for this run
```

### Projection segment plan

| Segment idx | Kind | Content mode | Token target | Notes |
| ---: | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| 0 | system_instructions | raw | 3500 | platform and package rules |
| 1 | project_rules | raw | 2500 | org gate, dry-run, audit |
| 2 | current_user_request | raw | 1200 | latest request |
| 3 | migration_artifact | raw | 12000 | draft plan/report |
| 4 | retrieved_source | excerpt | 14000 | schema/code references |
| 5 | compacted_history | summary | 12000 | old conversation |
| 6 | recent_event_window | raw | 22000 | latest turns |
| 7 | tool_schema | raw | 8000 | actions available |
| 8 | reserve | omitted | 12000 | output/tool headroom |

Projected total:

```text
estimatedPromptTokens: 75200
promptBudgetTokens: 96000
remainingPromptBudgetTokens: 20800
```

### Source-link coverage

Every summarized or excerpted segment needs source links:

```text
segment 4 retrieved_source:
  cites code files, schema files, and migration artifact paths

segment 5 compacted_history:
  summarizes event_items turn 1 through turn 8
  cites event_parts for large grep output
  cites trace events for failed shortcut decision

segment 6 recent_event_window:
  contains raw event_items turn 9 through turn 13
```

Coverage targets:

```text
summary segments: 100 percent have source links
retrieval segments: 100 percent have source links
omitted-source notices: 100 percent have source links
raw recent segments: source-linked to event ids
```

### Example compaction artifact

The compaction summary should be structured enough to validate.

```text
summary:
  The migration task is to remove old supplier story usage, adopt the new context package behavior, and add supplier compliance status to the requisition evaluation flow. Production rollout must remain org-scoped and canary-first.

decisions:
  - The org gate is mandatory. A prior shortcut to skip the org gate was explicitly rejected.
  - Schema dry-run planning must run per app before production rollout.
  - Dataset extraction must be auditable and tied to Clerk organization matrix resolution.
  - The transaction plan must be idempotent and paired with verification queries.

current_state:
  - Draft migration plan exists.
  - Verification query shape was discussed.
  - Large old grep output was summarized and remains available through source links.

next_steps:
  - Resolve org -> appId/adminToken matrix.
  - Run schema dry-run.
  - Generate migration report.
  - Validate with canary org.

forbidden_promotions:
  - Do not treat "skip org gate" as approved.
  - Do not treat local/dev dry-run as production verification.
```

Important property:

```text
The summary says the shortcut was rejected.
It does not say the shortcut is allowed.
```

### What the next model call receives

The task model sees a concise but source-labeled prompt:

```text
system/developer/project rules
current user request
migration artifact excerpts
retrieved schema/code snippets
source-labeled compacted history
recent raw turns
available tool schemas
```

It does not see:

```text
old 400-line grep output
repeated install logs
superseded old summary prompt scaffolding
full old low-signal chat narrative
```

It can still recover those omitted details because the projection manifest links to raw sources.

### Why this example matters

This example demonstrates the difference between chat convenience and migration-grade compaction.

Chat convenience asks:

```text
Can the model continue?
```

Migration-grade compaction asks:

```text
Can the model continue, and can a human later prove exactly which source material shaped the migration decision?
```

Ekairos should optimize for the second question.

## Technical-leader approval packet

Status: decision aid only. This is not implementation approval and does not change code.

This packet translates the research into explicit decisions. Because this workspace requires technical-leader architectural approval before execution, these decisions should be answered before any schema/code/config work starts.

### Decision D1: target abstraction

Question:

```text
Should context compaction be implemented as a first-class projection layer instead of an expandEvents-only behavior?
```

Recommended answer:

```text
yes, implement first-class projection
```

Reason:

- compaction needs budget, segment, source-link, trace, validation, and failure semantics;
- hiding it inside `expandEvents` makes it hard to audit;
- projection is the right boundary between raw event history and provider-facing model input.

If rejected:

- compaction can be implemented as app-level event expansion, but audit requirements become weaker and less reusable.

### Decision D2: reactor contract

Question:

```text
Should reactors receive pre-rendered model messages plus a projection manifest, or continue receiving events and building messages internally?
```

Recommended answer:

```text
reactors should receive pre-rendered model messages plus projection manifest
```

Reason:

- budget enforcement must happen before provider call;
- model-message rendering is part of projection, not provider execution;
- provider reactors should focus on streaming/model/tool I/O.

Breaking impact:

- AI SDK reactor params change;
- scripted reactor fixtures change;
- tests asserting `messagesForModel` shape change.

### Decision D3: schema target

Question:

```text
Should projection/segment/source-link data be first-class schema entities or trace payloads?
```

Recommended answer:

```text
first-class entities for target design
```

Reason:

- source-link coverage must be queryable;
- audit reports need durable relations;
- migration rollouts need verification queries.

Allowed staged compromise:

```text
trace-only prototype for local benchmark only, not production rollout
```

### Decision D4: compaction trigger policy

Question:

```text
What should trigger compaction?
```

Recommended answer:

```text
trigger on prompt budget pressure, not message count
```

Required inputs:

```text
model context window
model output reserve
configured prompt budget
estimated must-keep tokens
estimated compressible tokens
last actual provider prompt usage
cached/uncached token ratio where available
```

Rejected default:

```text
do not trigger only on number of turns
```

### Decision D5: failure behavior

Question:

```text
What happens when projection cannot fit must-keep material or summary validation fails?
```

Recommended answer:

```text
block and require operator/technical-leader review
```

Reason:

- unsafe compaction is worse than no compaction;
- migration plans should not be generated from corrupted context.

Possible blocked states:

```text
must_keep_too_large
missing_source_links
summary_validation_failed
provider_compaction_uninspectable
tool_pair_invalid
migration_gate_conflict
```

### Decision D6: provider-native compaction

Question:

```text
Should Ekairos use Anthropic/OpenAI provider-native compaction in production migration workflows?
```

Recommended answer:

```text
not for first production migration release
```

Reason:

- provider-native compaction can be valuable, but Ekairos first needs its own projection/source-link ledger;
- readable audit companion artifacts are required;
- provider-native outputs may not map cleanly to Ekairos source-link coverage.

Allowed use:

```text
research prototype
non-production benchmark
optional provider strategy after ledger exists
```

### Decision D7: recent window preservation

Question:

```text
How much recent conversation must remain raw?
```

Recommended starting answer:

```text
at least the current user request, explicit references, and the last 2 complete turns
minimum 20k recent-window token budget where model allows
```

Reason:

- Cline/OpenCode-style compaction works best when recent focus remains intact;
- current intent is too important to summarize.

Review needed:

```text
whether migration tasks need last 3 to 5 turns raw instead
```

### Decision D8: tool-output handling

Question:

```text
Can old tool outputs be pruned or summarized?
```

Recommended answer:

```text
yes in projection, never by mutating raw event_parts
```

Protected tool result classes:

```text
schema dry-run
admin runtime resolver
org/app matrix
dataset extraction
transaction application
verification queries
approval/rejection gate
security/auth resolver
```

Allowed compaction candidates:

```text
large repeated logs
long grep output
directory listings
duplicated install output
low-signal command output after an extracted error summary exists
```

### Decision D9: source authority ladder

Question:

```text
Should source authority be explicit in projection segments?
```

Recommended answer:

```text
yes, mandatory
```

Reason:

- summaries can accidentally elevate low-authority context;
- project rules must outrank auto memory and old assistant text;
- rejected ideas must stay rejected.

Minimum classes:

```text
platform
developer
approved_project_rule
current_user
explicit_reference
recent_execution
migration_artifact
retrieved_source
auto_memory
historical
tool_noise
unknown
```

### Decision D10: rule/memory/retrieval split

Question:

```text
Should durable rules, auto memory, and retrieval results be modeled separately?
```

Recommended answer:

```text
yes
```

Reason:

- Windsurf/Cursor-style systems distinguish durable rules from memory and retrieval;
- activation mode is a token budget control;
- auto memory should not become policy.

### Decision D11: validation threshold

Question:

```text
What validation must pass before a compacted projection can feed a task model call?
```

Recommended minimum:

```text
summary source-link coverage: 100 percent
current request raw: required
recent window raw: required
forbidden promotion check: pass
required migration facts: pass
tool-call pairing validation: pass
prompt budget validation: pass
```

If any fail:

```text
block model call
```

### Decision D12: trace event taxonomy

Question:

```text
Which trace event kinds should compaction add?
```

Recommended:

```text
context.projection
context.compaction
context.retrieval
context.projection.failed
```

Keep existing:

```text
context.llm
```

Reason:

- model usage alone is insufficient;
- reviewers need to correlate projection selection, compaction cost, retrieval cost, and final provider call.

### Decision D13: rollout scope

Question:

```text
Where should this be tested first?
```

Recommended:

```text
local Instant test app
development package tests
synthetic migration fixtures
non-production org canary only after schema approval
```

Production gate:

```text
planSchemaPush dry-run per app
org matrix resolved
verification queries approved
manual review report produced
```

### Decision D14: report format

Question:

```text
Should every compaction run produce a human-readable report?
```

Recommended:

```text
yes for migration workflows
```

Required report sections:

```text
projection summary
budget summary
segment table
source-link coverage
required fact checks
forbidden promotion checks
raw replay checks
trace ids
provider usage
operator decision
```

### Decision D15: default implementation sequence

Question:

```text
What should be built first after approval?
```

Recommended sequence:

1. Projection manifest type and renderer with no summarization.
2. Token estimation and budget decision records.
3. Trace events for projection.
4. Deterministic blocking over-budget behavior.
5. Source-link ledger.
6. Local LLM compaction artifact with validation.
7. Retrieval query/result plane.
8. Provider-native adapters.
9. Human report generation.

Reason:

- source/replay correctness comes before summary quality;
- budget observability comes before automatic compaction;
- provider-native compaction comes after Ekairos has an audit ledger.

### Approval form

Suggested approval record:

```text
approvedBy:
approvedAt:
scope:
  docs only
  prototype
  package schema
  package reactor contract
  production rollout

decisions:
  D1 target abstraction:
  D2 reactor contract:
  D3 schema target:
  D4 trigger policy:
  D5 failure behavior:
  D6 provider-native compaction:
  D7 recent window:
  D8 tool-output handling:
  D9 authority ladder:
  D10 rules/memory/retrieval split:
  D11 validation threshold:
  D12 trace taxonomy:
  D13 rollout scope:
  D14 report format:
  D15 implementation sequence:

explicit non-goals:

approved files/modules:

blocked files/modules:

required tests:

required manual verification:
```

### Recommendation summary

The recommended architecture is:

```text
first-class projection layer
breaking reactor contract
first-class projection entities
source-link ledger
hard failure on unsafe compaction
local validated compaction first
provider-native compaction later
human-readable report for migration workflows
```

This is the cleanest path if Ekairos is serious about being a database migration service, not only a chat orchestration layer.

## Expanded comparative matrix

Status: research synthesis. This matrix summarizes behavior from the sourced systems already cited in this artifact.

### Systems compared

```text
Claude API server-side compaction
Claude Code context-window behavior
OpenAI Responses compaction
OpenAI Codex agent loop
OpenCode session compaction
Cline Auto Compact
Hermes context compression and caching
Windsurf Memories/Rules/Fast Context/Codemaps
Cursor Rules/Codebase Indexing
Gemini CLI
Aider repo map
Continue context selection
```

### Matrix: primary mechanism

| System | Primary context mechanism | Is it true transcript compaction? | Ekairos lesson |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude API | server-side compaction blocks | yes | provider-native can work, but app needs audit ledger |
| Claude Code | agent context window management | mostly internal | user-facing continuation depends on hidden agent policy |
| OpenAI Responses | response compaction endpoint | yes | can be provider adapter, not source of truth |
| OpenAI Codex | agent loop and environment state | partially internal | harness/replay matters as much as prompt text |
| OpenCode | session summary plus tail preservation and pruning | yes | open-source selector/prune ideas are useful |
| Cline | Auto Compact summarization | yes | compaction should be visible and checkpoint-aware |
| Hermes | context compression/caching | yes/adjacent | cache and compression are distinct from authority |
| Windsurf | rules, memories, Fast Context, Codemaps | mostly retrieval/rules | retrieval is not compaction |
| Cursor | rules, indexing, references | mostly retrieval/rules | project rules are durable prefix context |
| Gemini CLI | command/context controls | limited | CLI controls are not enough for audit |
| Aider | repo map and selected files | retrieval/selection | code map can reduce prompt pressure without summary |
| Continue | context providers/selection | retrieval/selection | pluggable context providers need authority labels |

### Matrix: trigger model

| System | Trigger | Configurability | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude API | input-token threshold | trigger parameter; minimum documented threshold | provider handles summary but app must track usage iterations |
| OpenAI Responses | explicit compact call | app decides when to compact | app owns trigger policy |
| OpenCode | overflow based on usable context and token usage | config supports reserved/tail/prune behavior | early/late compaction can surprise users |
| Cline | approaching model context limit | feature/model support dependent | fallback truncation can lose context if model unsupported |
| Hermes | context/caching policy | app/agent configuration | cache hit rate can be confused with semantic recall |
| Windsurf | relevance and activation modes | memories/rules modes | always-on rules consume context every turn |
| Cursor | rule activation, indexing retrieval | path/manual/agent/user modes | indexed retrieval may look authoritative when it is only relevant |
| Aider | map/token budget choices | CLI options | selected file/map can miss non-local decisions |
| Continue | context provider selection | configuration | provider results need trust boundaries |

Ekairos recommendation:

```text
trigger on prompt budget pressure plus migration safety constraints
record trigger threshold and observed value
do not trigger only on turn count
do not silently fallback to destructive pruning
```

### Matrix: tail preservation

| System | Tail strategy | Ekairos equivalent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude API | pause-after-compaction can preserve recent messages after block | preserve current request and recent raw turns |
| OpenCode | `tail_turns` and tail budget selection | recent-window segment with source links |
| Cline | continues where it left off and Focus Chain keeps todos | current focus/todo outside raw summary |
| OpenAI Responses | app decides what to compact and what to send next | projection builder owns preserved segments |
| Windsurf/Cursor | explicit mentions/rules selected into current request | explicit references become must-keep |

Ekairos rule:

```text
current user request and explicit references are never summarized
recent tool call/result pairs stay structurally paired
```

### Matrix: source authority handling

| System | Authority model visible? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude API | role hierarchy exists, compaction summary is provider-generated | app must protect authority boundaries in custom instructions |
| OpenAI Responses | role hierarchy includes system/developer/user | compact endpoint should preserve hierarchy but app should verify |
| OpenCode | session messages and plugin-injected compaction context | plugin context can influence summary, needs trust policy |
| Cline | conversation summary and Focus Chain | docs emphasize technical details, less explicit authority taxonomy |
| Windsurf | rules vs memories vs AGENTS.md vs system-level rules | strong model for durable authority separation |
| Cursor | project/user rules and AGENTS.md | good model for prompt-level durable instructions |
| Aider | repo map versus chat/files | selected code is source evidence, not instruction |
| Continue | context providers | provider output must be labeled |

Ekairos recommendation:

```text
authorityClass is required on every projection segment
summary prompt alone is insufficient
source authority must exist in data
```

### Matrix: tool output strategy

| System | Tool-output behavior | Ekairos implication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenCode | caps tool output during compaction input and can prune old tool output | cap in projection, never mutate raw event_parts |
| Claude API | compacts conversation blocks provider-side | app must know what was summarized |
| Cline | preserves code changes and technical details by summary | require fact validation for tool outputs |
| Windsurf Fast Context | retrieves targeted code to avoid context pollution | retrieval can reduce need for dumping tool output |
| Aider repo map | map replaces huge code dumps | structured maps are safer than raw dumps |

Ekairos protected tool outputs:

```text
schema dry-run
org matrix
admin runtime resolution
dataset extraction
transaction plan
verification query
approval gate
```

### Matrix: observability and cost

| System | Cost/usage visibility | Ekairos requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude API | usage iterations distinguish compaction and message sampling | aggregate compaction plus task usage |
| OpenAI Responses | response objects/usage metadata | store provider usage and compaction ids |
| OpenCode | message cost/tokens and compaction events | trace projection/compaction/LLM separately |
| Cline | summarization tool call shows cost | compaction should be a visible step |
| Hermes | caching/compression | separate cache accounting from semantic compaction |

Ekairos trace minimum:

```text
context.projection
context.compaction
context.retrieval
context.llm
```

### Matrix: replay and rollback

| System | Replay/restore model | Ekairos lesson |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cline | checkpoints can restore before summarization | raw history and checkpoint state are essential |
| OpenCode | session storage and compaction messages | summary lineage should be explicit |
| OpenAI Codex | environment/session harness matters | file/process state must be part of audit context |
| Claude API | app passes compaction blocks forward | app must persist both raw and compacted conversation |
| Aider | git state and repo map | code state is a separate source of truth |

Ekairos rule:

```text
projection is derived state
raw event history remains append-only
compaction artifacts are lineage records
```

### Matrix: best transferable ideas

| Source system | Transferable idea | Ekairos adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic | trigger threshold, compaction block, pause-after-compaction, usage iterations | provider adapter after ledger |
| OpenAI | explicit compact endpoint and response item model | adapter with source-link companion |
| OpenCode | usable budget, tail selector, previous-summary lineage, tool-output cap | engine-level projection strategy |
| Cline | visible compaction, Focus Chain/todos, checkpoints | visible compaction step plus state outside summary |
| Windsurf | rules/memories distinction and activation modes | durable instruction plane |
| Cursor | scoped rules and codebase indexing | scoped rules and retrieval plane |
| Aider | repo map | domain/code maps as retrievable artifacts |
| Continue | pluggable context providers | retrieval provider interface with authority labels |
| Hermes | compression/caching separation | cache metrics distinct from semantic summary |

### Matrix: ideas to reject for Ekairos migration contexts

| Idea | Why reject |
| --- | --- |
| destructive transcript mutation | breaks audit and replay |
| summary with no source links | cannot prove migration decisions |
| compaction hidden inside reactor | provider execution should not own context policy |
| always-on large rules | burns context and hides activation cost |
| auto memory treated as policy | unsafe authority elevation |
| tail-only pruning | loses decisions outside recent window |
| provider-native only | app loses source-link control |
| exact summary text assertions in tests | brittle and misses semantic failures |
| unbounded retrieval dumps | context pollution instead of compaction |

### Final comparative conclusion

The state of the art is not one technique. It is a stack:

```text
durable rules for stable instructions
retrieval/indexing for relevant source discovery
tail preservation for immediate focus
summarization for older transcript compression
provider-native compaction as an optional accelerator
trace/cost accounting for operations
replay/checkpoints for trust
```

Ekairos should implement that stack as a projection ledger, not as a single "summarize old messages" helper.
