
Fixture: redaction leak.

```text
source contains admin token
summary reproduces token
expected failure: secret_leak_detected
```

### Implementation shape after approval

First approved slice can avoid model-assisted validation.

Proposed first slice:

```text
structured source packets
structured summary fields
deterministic claim ledger for required claims
blocking validation for active user instruction, approval state, tool pass/fail, and tenant scope
unit fixtures only
```

Proposed later slice:

```text
model-assisted claim extraction
model-assisted citation repair
recursive summary validation
provider-native companion ledgers
operator UI for claim inspection
```

### Recommendation

Make claim ledger validation the acceptance gate for compaction artifacts.

Reason:

```text
Ekairos migration work depends on traceable decisions, not merely shorter context
```

## Recursive compaction lineage and summary drift control

Status: design proposal.

Long-running agent sessions do not compact once. They compact repeatedly.

That creates a second-order risk:

```text
the model stops summarizing raw source material and starts summarizing previous summaries
```

If unmanaged, recursive compaction can create summary drift.

Summary drift means:

```text
claims become less precise
uncertainty disappears
source links become indirect
older mistakes become canonical
newer corrections are blended into older assertions
tenant scope becomes vague
```

Ekairos should treat recursive compaction as a lineage problem, not only a token problem.

### Recursive compaction example

Initial raw fact:

```text
tool result at T1: schema dry-run failed for org-a because field x is missing
```

First summary:

```text
schema dry-run failed for org-a due to missing field x
```

Second summary:

```text
schema dry-run had an issue
```

Third summary:

```text
schema validation was handled
```

This is unacceptable for migration work.

The later summary is shorter but loses:

```text
failure state
organization id
field name
tool authority
required next action
```

### Lineage principle

Every compacted artifact should know whether its sources are raw, compacted, retrieved, rule-derived, or memory-derived.

Recommended source categories:

```text
raw_event_part
raw_tool_result
raw_user_message
raw_system_instruction
raw_project_instruction
local_file_snapshot
external_source_snapshot
projection_segment
compaction_artifact
retrieval_result
rule_activation
memory_record
provider_native_state
```

Recursive compaction should prefer raw high-authority sources when material claims are still active.

### Lineage fields

Every compaction artifact should record:

```text
artifactId
artifactKind
projectionId
sourceDepth
sourceArtifactIds
rootSourcePartIds
rootSourceEventIds
rootSourceExternalIds
rootSourceCoverage
maxSummaryDepth
rawSourceShare
compactedSourceShare
generatedAt
generatedBy
validationStatus
```

Definitions:

```text
sourceDepth: number of compaction hops from raw source to current artifact
maxSummaryDepth: deepest summary chain represented in the artifact
rawSourceShare: share of material claims directly backed by raw sources
compactedSourceShare: share of material claims backed only by previous summaries
rootSourceCoverage: required raw source categories preserved through links
```

### Depth policy

Recommended default:

```text
depth 0: raw material
depth 1: summary generated from raw material
depth 2: summary generated from previous summary plus raw refresh
depth 3: block unless technical leader approves a special path
```

This is intentionally conservative.

Reason:

```text
migration decisions can survive token pressure only if their root evidence remains reachable
```

### Raw refresh requirement

When compacting an old compaction artifact, the projection builder should also rehydrate root sources for material active claims.

Raw refresh means:

```text
load previous artifact
read its claim ledger
identify material active claims
resolve root source links
include selected root source packets in the new compaction input
validate the new summary against root sources, not only against the previous summary
```

This keeps recursive compaction anchored to durable evidence.

### What can be summarized from a previous summary

Allowed from previous summary:

```text
low-risk narrative chronology
non-operative background
obsolete completed plan items
old rejected alternatives when no longer active
high-level source catalog when exact claims are separately linked
```

Not allowed from previous summary only:

```text
active user instructions
technical-leader approvals
denials or constraints
tool pass/fail results
tenant-scoped facts
schema dry-run results
production rollout state
security claims
secrets or redaction claims
current branch/worktree status
current timer gate
```

These must be validated against raw or highest-authority current sources.

### Drift detection metrics

Recommended metrics:

```text
claimCountDelta
materialClaimLossCount
specificityLossCount
uncertaintyLossCount
sourceDepthIncrease
rawSourceShare
rootCoverageRatio
contradictionIntroducedCount
tenantScopeLossCount
blockedClaimCarryForwardCount
```

Interpretation:

```text
claimCountDelta is not automatically bad
materialClaimLossCount above zero is usually bad
specificityLossCount on migration facts is bad
uncertaintyLossCount is bad when source was uncertain
sourceDepthIncrease is expected but bounded
rawSourceShare should remain high for active claims
rootCoverageRatio should be complete for required active claims
```

### Specificity ladder

The validator should detect when a summary makes a claim less specific in a behavior-changing way.

Example:

```text
org-a dry-run failed because field x is missing
```

Less specific but still acceptable for old background:

```text
an old dry-run failed
```

Less specific and unacceptable for active migration:

```text
schema validation was handled
```

Specificity dimensions:

```text
actor
tenant
environment
file path
symbol name
command
result
error code
time
decision state
approval state
next action
```

### Uncertainty preservation

Compaction must preserve uncertainty.

Source:

```text
official docs shell did not render, snippets suggest feature exists
```

Acceptable compacted claim:

```text
the Cursor source was lower-confidence because the official docs shell did not render during this run
```

Unacceptable compacted claim:

```text
Cursor officially guarantees the feature
```

Uncertainty markers:

```text
observed
inferred
lower-confidence
unverified
blocked
requires recheck
date caveat
```

Validation rule:

```text
a compacted claim may not increase confidence above the source confidence
```

### Correction preservation

Corrections must be treated as active override records.

Correction examples:

```text
the user changes the requested output from implementation to docs only
the user adds the five-hour time gate
the user rejects a proposed schema strategy
the user clarifies that branch creation needs explicit request
```

Recommended correction representation:

```text
correctionId
supersededClaimIds
replacementClaim
sourceId
authorityClass
timestamp
active
```

Projection rule:

```text
active corrections are must-keep until they are either superseded by a newer user correction or no longer relevant to the task
```

### Blocked claim carry-forward

If a claim was blocked in one compaction pass, the next pass must not silently turn it into accepted context.

Blocked claim record:

```text
claimId
claimText
failureCode
requiredRemediation
firstBlockedAt
lastSeenAt
status
```

Allowed transitions:

```text
blocked -> remediated by new source
blocked -> obsolete by newer instruction
blocked -> still blocked
```

Forbidden transition:

```text
blocked -> accepted without new source
```

### Lineage graph

Recursive compaction should be represented as a graph.

Conceptual edges:

```text
raw_event_part -> projection_segment
projection_segment -> compaction_artifact
compaction_artifact -> projection_segment
compaction_artifact -> later_compaction_artifact
raw_event_part -> later_compaction_artifact
```

Important property:

```text
the graph must retain a path from each material claim to at least one root source
```

### Root source coverage report

A recursive compaction report should include:

```text
artifactId
sourceDepth
maxSummaryDepth
rootSourceCount
materialClaimCount
materialClaimsWithRootSource
materialClaimsOnlyBackedBySummary
requiredActiveClaimsWithRootSource
driftWarnings
blockedClaims
```

Example:

```text
artifactId: compaction-009
sourceDepth: 2
maxSummaryDepth: 2
rootSourceCount: 184
materialClaimCount: 73
materialClaimsWithRootSource: 73
materialClaimsOnlyBackedBySummary: 0
requiredActiveClaimsWithRootSource: 12 of 12
driftWarnings: 0
blockedClaims: 0
```

### Recursive compaction modes

Mode 1: recompact with root refresh.

```text
default target mode
safe for active migration context
more expensive
```

Mode 2: summarize previous summary only.

```text
allowed only for low-risk background
not allowed for active decisions, tool results, tenant facts, or security constraints
```

Mode 3: archive old summary and keep only index pointer.

```text
useful when old context is not active
projection includes retrieval hook instead of summary content
```

Mode 4: block and ask operator.

```text
required when material root sources cannot be resolved or budget remains unsafe
```

### Handling provider-native recursive state

Provider-native state may be recursively compacted outside Ekairos visibility.

Risk:

```text
Ekairos cannot inspect provider-side source depth or drift
```

Policy:

```text
provider-native recursive state is never the only source for migration-critical claims
```

If a provider supports explicit compaction instructions and usage reporting, Ekairos can still use it as an optimization.

Required companion state:

```text
local projection manifest
local claim ledger
local root source links
provider compact id when available
provider usage metrics
provider instruction snapshot
```

### Drift remediation

If drift is detected:

```text
block projection
show drift report
rehydrate root sources
regenerate summary
validate again
```

If root sources are unavailable:

```text
mark the claim unverifiable
omit it from model-facing context
preserve blocked report for operator review
```

If a summary is too lossy but not unsafe:

```text
use retrieval pointer instead of lossy summary
keep high-level chronology only
do not include operational claims
```

### Recursive fixture pack

Fixture RC1: repeated confidence increase.

```text
source: lower-confidence external doc fetch
summary 1: lower-confidence
summary 2: official confirmed behavior
expected: uncertaintyLossCount 1
result: blocked
```

Fixture RC2: tenant scope loss.

```text
source: org-a dry-run failed
summary 1: org-a dry-run failed
summary 2: dry-run failed
summary 3: dry-run handled
expected: tenantScopeLossCount 1 and specificityLossCount 1
result: blocked while migration active
```

Fixture RC3: blocked claim accepted.

```text
pass 1: claim blocked because source missing
pass 2: summary says claim is true
expected: blockedClaimCarryForwardCount 1
result: blocked
```

Fixture RC4: raw refresh succeeds.

```text
pass 1: old summary has active test result
pass 2: root tool result is rehydrated
expected: materialClaimsWithRootSource complete
result: accepted
```

Fixture RC5: obsolete low-risk background.

```text
source: old alternative design rejected
current task: final report only
summary: old rejected alternatives existed
expected: low-risk summary-only source accepted with warning
result: accepted_with_warning
```

### Implementation slice after approval

First slice:

```text
add sourceDepth to compaction artifact contract
record root source ids in claim ledger
block active claims backed only by previous summaries
add recursive fixture tests
```

Later slice:

```text
graph query for lineage
drift metric computation
operator drift report
root source rehydration planner
provider-native recursive state tracking
```

### Recommendation

Recursive compaction should default to root-source refresh for all active operational claims.

Reason:

```text
summaries of summaries are useful for background, but dangerous as evidence for migrations
```

## Projection lifecycle state machine

Status: design proposal.

Context compaction should not be represented as a single boolean.

Bad model:

```text
compacted: true
```

Better model:

```text
projection has a lifecycle
each lifecycle state has allowed transitions
blocked states are explicit
rendering and provider dispatch happen only after validation
```

This matters because Ekairos contexts are durable, multi-step, and auditable.

### Lifecycle goals

The lifecycle should make these questions answerable:

```text
Was projection attempted?
Why was compaction triggered?
Which source material was eligible?
Which source material was protected?
Was a summary generated?
Was the summary validated?
Was it accepted or blocked?
Was the accepted projection actually sent to a model?
Which provider received it?
Did the model call write new parts?
Can the same projection be replayed?
```

### Proposed statuses

Created:

```text
projection record exists
source window has not been built
```

Source collected:

```text
raw source packets, rules, retrieval candidates, and tool schemas have been enumerated
```

Classified:

```text
source material is split into protected, recent, compressible, omitted, retrieval-only, and blocked categories
```

Budgeted:

```text
estimated tokens are computed for system prompt, messages, tools, provider overhead, and output reserve
```

No compaction needed:

```text
raw projection fits budget with required output reserve
```

Compaction needed:

```text
raw projection does not fit budget or projection policy requests compression
```

Compaction generated:

```text
summary or compacted artifact exists but has not passed validation
```

Validation running:

```text
claim ledger, required coverage, redaction, tenant, authority, and freshness checks are running
```

Validation failed:

```text
artifact exists but cannot be used
```

Blocked:

```text
projection cannot safely continue without operator action or approved workflow action
```

Accepted:

```text
projection manifest is valid and ready to render into provider-facing model messages
```

Rendered:

```text
provider-facing messages and tools have been produced and final budget check has passed
```

Dispatched:

```text
reactor has received rendered projection input and provider call has started
```

Completed:

```text
model call completed and new durable event parts or trace events were written
```

Archived:

```text
projection is retained for audit but no longer active
```

Superseded:

```text
newer projection replaced this projection before dispatch or after a user correction
```

### Forbidden transitions

These transitions should be invalid:

```text
created -> rendered
source_collected -> dispatched
compaction_generated -> dispatched
validation_failed -> accepted
blocked -> accepted without new source or operator action
accepted -> completed without rendered
rendered -> completed without dispatched
provider_native_state -> accepted without companion local validation
```

The most important rule:

```text
the provider call can only use an accepted and rendered projection
```

### Trigger reasons

Projection should record why it started.

Trigger reasons:

```text
new_user_turn
pre_reactor_budget_check
manual_operator_request
provider_context_overflow
long_running_session_checkpoint
recursive_compaction_refresh
retrieval_refresh
rule_activation_change
tool_surface_change
```

Trigger reason matters because validation expectations differ.

Example:

```text
provider_context_overflow should preserve the last provider error and mark the previous projection attempt as failed
```

Example:

```text
tool_surface_change should recalculate tool schema tokens even when message content has not changed
```

### Transition table

Created can transition to:

```text
source_collected
blocked
superseded
```

Source collected can transition to:

```text
classified
blocked
superseded
```

Classified can transition to:

```text
budgeted
blocked
superseded
```

Budgeted can transition to:

```text
no_compaction_needed
compaction_needed
blocked
superseded
```

No compaction needed can transition to:

```text
accepted
rendered
superseded
```

Compaction needed can transition to:

```text
compaction_generated
blocked
superseded
```

Compaction generated can transition to:

```text
validation_running
validation_failed
superseded
```

Validation running can transition to:

```text
accepted
validation_failed
blocked
superseded
```

Validation failed can transition to:

```text
blocked
superseded
```

Blocked can transition to:

```text
source_collected
classified
budgeted
compaction_generated
superseded
archived
```

Accepted can transition to:

```text
rendered
superseded
archived
```

Rendered can transition to:

```text
dispatched
superseded
archived
```

Dispatched can transition to:

```text
completed
blocked
archived
```

Completed can transition to:

```text
archived
```

### State payload fields

Every lifecycle transition should carry:

```text
projectionId
previousStatus
nextStatus
transitionReason
actor
sourceExecutionId
sourceStepId
timestamp
budgetSnapshot
validationSnapshot
traceEventId
```

Actor values:

```text
engine
reactor
operator
validator
provider_adapter
store
```

### Blocking taxonomy

Blocked states should be precise.

Blocking classes:

```text
budget_blocked
source_blocked
approval_blocked
tenant_blocked
redaction_blocked
validation_blocked
provider_blocked
tool_surface_blocked
unknown_blocked
```

Examples:

```text
budget_blocked: protected material alone exceeds model window
source_blocked: required root source cannot be resolved
approval_blocked: mutation tool would be included without approval
tenant_blocked: source packets cross org boundary
redaction_blocked: secret-bearing source has unknown redaction state
validation_blocked: claim ledger has material unresolved claim
provider_blocked: provider overflow occurred after rendered projection
tool_surface_blocked: required tool schemas exceed tool budget
```

### Nonterminal blocked states

Blocked should not mean failed forever.

Blocked means:

```text
the engine cannot safely proceed automatically
```

Allowed remediation:

```text
operator approves a narrower tool profile
operator removes a claim
approved tool result supplies missing source
projection budget switches to larger approved model
tenant source is split by organization
redaction pass reruns successfully
```

Each remediation must produce a new transition.

### Superseded states

Superseded is required because user corrections can arrive while projection is being built.

Example:

```text
projection starts for old user request
new user message changes the task
old projection becomes superseded
new projection starts from latest active intent
```

Superseded records should remain auditable.

They should include:

```text
supersededByProjectionId
supersededByEventId
reason
```

### Renderer final gate

Rendering is a separate status because token estimates can change after formatting.

Renderer final gate checks:

```text
rendered model messages fit budget
tool schemas fit budget
system prompt is present
current user message is last active intent
tool call/result pairs are valid
file/image parts keep required structure
no dangling synthetic context exists
```

If this fails:

```text
accepted -> blocked is allowed with reason rendered_budget_exceeded or renderer_invariant_failed
```

### Provider dispatch gate

Dispatch should record:

```text
provider
model
modelBudgetProfile
providerRequestId when available
toolCount
messageCount
renderedInputTokenEstimate
outputReserveTokens
projectionId
```

Provider response should update lifecycle:

```text
dispatched -> completed when provider completes
dispatched -> blocked when provider returns context overflow or structural error
dispatched -> archived only after completed or superseded trace exists
```

### Store replay behavior

Replay should be able to answer:

```text
which projection generated this provider call?
which accepted artifact did it include?
which raw parts were omitted?
which raw parts were summarized?
which raw parts remained recent?
```

This requires projection ids to flow through:

```text
event_trace_events
event_steps
event_parts metadata
operator reports
benchmark reports
```

### UI status mapping

Operator-facing statuses should be simpler than internal statuses.

Internal statuses:

```text
created
source_collected
classified
budgeted
compaction_generated
validation_running
accepted
rendered
dispatched
completed
```

Can display as:

```text
preparing context
checking budget
compacting context
validating context
sending to model
done
```

Blocked statuses should display precise remediation:

```text
context blocked: required source missing
context blocked: approval required
context blocked: tenant scope conflict
context blocked: redaction required
context blocked: model budget exceeded
```

### Lifecycle tests

Fixture LC1: raw context fits.

```text
created -> source_collected -> classified -> budgeted -> no_compaction_needed -> accepted -> rendered -> dispatched -> completed
```

Fixture LC2: summary validation fails.

```text
created -> source_collected -> classified -> budgeted -> compaction_needed -> compaction_generated -> validation_running -> validation_failed -> blocked
```

Fixture LC3: user correction supersedes projection.

```text
projection A: validation_running -> superseded
projection B: created -> source_collected
```

Fixture LC4: rendered budget exceeds estimate.

```text
accepted -> rendered attempt -> blocked
failure reason: rendered_budget_exceeded
```

Fixture LC5: provider overflow after dispatch.

```text
rendered -> dispatched -> blocked
failure reason: provider_context_overflow
```

Fixture LC6: missing approval for mutation tool.

```text
budgeted -> blocked
failure reason: approval_required_for_tool_surface
```

### Recommendation

Represent projection and compaction as a lifecycle state machine with auditable transitions.

Reason:

```text
implicit context mutation is not enough for a migration-grade event engine
```

## Provider-rendering contract and message-shape budgets

Status: design proposal.

Projection is provider-neutral.

Rendering is provider-specific.

This split is important because compaction safety decisions should not depend on the accidental shape of one provider SDK.

### Current local rendering anchors

The current store exposes model-message conversion:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\stores\instant.store.ts:695

The shared event conversion helpers describe conversion to AI SDK ModelMessages:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\context.events.ts:393

The current AI SDK reactor obtains messages and sends them to `streamText`:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:153

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:184

Tool conversion also happens before the provider call:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:178

The proposal is not to remove these behaviors blindly. The proposal is to insert an approved projection and rendering contract before provider dispatch.

### Boundary rule

Recommended boundary:

```text
event_parts remain canonical
projection manifest selects and classifies source material
compaction artifact summarizes only eligible source material
claim ledger validates the artifact
provider renderer turns accepted projection into provider-specific messages and tools
reactor dispatches rendered input
```

Forbidden boundary:

```text
provider renderer silently drops raw parts to fit budget
reactor privately summarizes messages
store mutates event_parts to reflect compacted content
provider-native compacted state becomes canonical source
```

### Provider renderer responsibilities

Renderer should own:

```text
message role mapping
content part mapping
tool call mapping
tool result mapping
system prompt placement
file/image handling
provider-specific metadata
final token estimate
rendered input hash
provider request preview for audit
```

Renderer should not own:

```text
source selection
authority classification
tenant boundary decisions
summary generation
claim validation
operator approval policy
```

### Renderer input

Provider renderer should receive an accepted projection, not raw events.

Conceptual input:

```text
projectionId
contextIdentifier
modelBudgetProfile
systemInstructions
acceptedSegments
acceptedCompactionArtifacts
recentRawItems
toolProfile
toolSpecs
providerTarget
outputReserveTokens
```

The renderer can include source metadata in provider-visible text only when useful and safe.

Default:

```text
source metadata is stored in projection manifest and trace
model-visible source ids are included only for compacted artifacts and audit-critical instructions
```

### Renderer output

Conceptual output:

```text
projectionId
provider
model
messageFormat
messages
tools
toolChoice
stopPolicy
inputTokenEstimate
toolTokenEstimate
systemTokenEstimate
messageTokenEstimate
outputReserveTokens
renderedInputHash
rendererWarnings
```

Renderer output should be immutable once dispatched.

If a newer user message arrives before dispatch:

```text
old rendered output becomes superseded
new projection begins
```

### Message-shape budget

Different providers and SDKs can represent the same content with different overhead.

Budget should therefore be checked in two phases:

```text
projection budget: source material and abstract segments
rendered budget: exact provider-facing messages and tool schemas
```

Projection budget can pass while rendered budget fails.

Reasons:

```text
tool schema JSON expands after conversion
file parts require provider-specific wrappers
system instructions are duplicated by SDK shape
tool calls/results add structural overhead
source id labels add tokens
```

Required response:

```text
do not dispatch
record rendered_budget_exceeded
choose approved remediation
```

### Role mapping risks

Role mapping is a safety boundary.

Risks:

```text
system instruction rendered as user content
user correction rendered before older assistant text
tool result rendered as assistant assertion
summary inserted after current user intent
provider-native state inserted without visible instruction
```

Invariant:

```text
current user intent must remain the final active request in the rendered conversation unless provider protocol requires a different explicit field
```

### Tool call and result mapping

Tool pairs are especially sensitive.

Renderer must preserve:

```text
tool call id
tool name
tool input
tool result
tool error state
execution status
ordering
```

Forbidden:

```text
rendering a failed tool result as successful assistant text
rendering a tool result without its call
rendering a tool call without its result when result already exists
changing tool name during compaction
dropping approval metadata for approval-gated tools
```

### File and image parts

File and image parts should not be compacted into prose unless the projection policy explicitly permits a derived description.

For migration work:

```text
file path and artifact identity are usually more important than visual prose
```

Renderer policy:

```text
preserve supported structured parts
store unsupported structured parts as omitted-with-reference
include human-readable omission note only when model needs to know the artifact exists
```

Example:

```text
artifact omitted from provider input due to unsupported file part
source link preserved in projection manifest
operator report records omission
```

### System prompt placement

Provider renderers differ in how system instructions are represented.

Ekairos policy should be provider-neutral:

```text
highest-authority instructions stay highest-authority in rendered input
project rules remain separate from assistant summaries
summary content never becomes system instruction
```

If a provider has no explicit system role:

```text
renderer must record downgraded authority as a warning or block if unsafe
```

### Provider adapter capability record

Each provider renderer should declare capabilities.

Capability fields:

```text
provider
messageFormat
supportsSystemRole
supportsStructuredToolCall
supportsStructuredToolResult
supportsFileParts
supportsImageParts
supportsProviderNativeCompaction
supportsPromptCaching
usageFields
contextWindowTokens
maxOutputTokens
toolSchemaFormat
```

Why this matters:

```text
projection cannot make a safe budget decision without renderer capability data
```

### Provider-native compaction rendering

Provider-native compaction should be treated as a renderer/provider adapter feature.

It should not be an engine-level substitute for projection.

Provider-native render flow:

```text
build accepted local projection
render local provider input
optionally call provider compact feature when approved
store provider compact metadata
keep local claim ledger canonical
dispatch using provider-specific compacted state if valid
```

If the provider compact feature changes message shape:

```text
record pre-compact rendered hash
record post-compact provider id when available
record provider usage before and after when available
```

### Rendering preview

For audit, renderer should produce a safe preview.

Preview includes:

```text
message count
roles
content part counts
tool names
token estimates
omission notices
compaction artifact ids
source id counts
```

Preview excludes:

```text
secret values
full large tool outputs
raw tenant data unless operator has scope
provider credentials
```

### Rendering trace events

Recommended trace events:

```text
context.render.started
context.render.completed
context.render.failed
context.provider.dispatch.started
context.provider.dispatch.completed
context.provider.dispatch.failed
```

Required trace fields:

```text
projectionId
rendererName
provider
model
messageCount
toolCount
inputTokenEstimate
toolTokenEstimate
outputReserveTokens
renderedInputHash
failureCode
```

### Renderer tests

Fixture PR1: role preservation.

```text
input: system rule, old assistant text, current user correction
expected: system rule stays highest authority and current correction remains active
```

Fixture PR2: tool pair preservation.

```text
input: completed tool call and result
expected: rendered output contains valid pair with same identity
```

Fixture PR3: failed tool result.

```text
input: tool error result
expected: rendered output preserves failure state
```

Fixture PR4: message budget passes but rendered budget fails.

```text
input: small messages, large tool schemas
expected: rendered_budget_exceeded
```

Fixture PR5: unsupported file part.

```text
input: file part unsupported by provider
expected: omission notice plus source link preserved
```

Fixture PR6: provider-native compact metadata.

```text
input: approved provider-native compact path
expected: local claim ledger remains canonical and provider metadata is recorded
```

### Implementation slice after approval

First slice:

```text
extract provider rendering contract types
compute rendered budget estimate
record rendered preview in trace
keep existing AI SDK behavior behind renderer
add role/tool/file invariant tests
```

Target slice:

```text
break reactor contract so reactor receives rendered projection input
add provider capability records
add provider-native compaction adapter hooks
add replayable rendered input hash
```

### Recommendation

Separate provider-neutral projection from provider-specific rendering.

Reason:

```text
Ekairos should decide what context is valid before any provider-specific message shape decides what fits
```

## Usage telemetry calibration loop

Status: design proposal.

Token estimation before a model call is necessary, but it is never perfect.

Ekairos should treat provider usage results as feedback for future projection decisions.

### Current local usage anchors

The AI SDK reactor reads usage from the result object:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:320

It extracts prompt, completion, and total token counts:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:355

It also attempts to read cached prompt token variants:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:362

Those fields are useful for a projection calibration loop.

### Why calibration matters

Pre-call budget estimates can be wrong because:

```text
provider tokenizers differ
SDK message wrappers add overhead
tool schema conversion changes JSON shape
file/image parts have provider-specific costs
system prompt placement changes overhead
provider prompt caching changes billed tokens
model aliases change context windows
provider-native compaction changes effective input size
```

If Ekairos uses a static estimator, it will either:

```text
compact too aggressively and lose useful context
```

or:

```text
compact too late and hit provider overflow
```

Usage telemetry lets the engine tune estimates by provider, model, renderer, and tool profile.

### Calibration record

Each completed provider call should produce a calibration record.

Recommended fields:

```text
calibrationId
projectionId
renderedInputHash
provider
model
rendererName
modelBudgetProfile
messageCount
toolCount
estimatedInputTokens
estimatedToolTokens
estimatedSystemTokens
estimatedMessageTokens
estimatedOutputReserveTokens
actualPromptTokens
actualCompletionTokens
actualTotalTokens
actualCachedPromptTokens
providerUsageRaw
estimatorVersion
rendererVersion
createdAt
```

Derived fields:

```text
inputEstimatorError
inputEstimatorErrorRatio
totalEstimatorError
cacheHitRatio
budgetHeadroomBeforeCall
budgetHeadroomAfterCall
overflowRiskBeforeCall
```

### Error ratio

Recommended calculation:

```text
inputEstimatorError = actualPromptTokens - estimatedInputTokens
inputEstimatorErrorRatio = inputEstimatorError / max(actualPromptTokens, 1)
```

Interpretation:

```text
positive error means estimate was too low
negative error means estimate was too high
```

Policy:

```text
underestimation is more dangerous than overestimation
```

### Safety margin policy

Projection should keep a safety margin.

Initial margin:

```text
10 percent of model budget or configured minimum reserve
```

Adaptive margin:

```text
increase margin when underestimation is observed
decrease margin slowly only after enough stable samples
never decrease below approved minimum
```

Suggested per-profile margins:

```text
small context window: 15 percent
medium context window: 10 percent
large context window: 8 percent
very large context window: 5 percent plus absolute reserve
```

Large windows still need an absolute reserve because tool calls and output can grow.

### Calibration buckets

Estimator correction should be bucketed.

Bucket keys:

```text
provider
model
rendererName
messageFormat
toolProfile
toolCountRange
hasFileParts
hasImageParts
hasProviderNativeCompaction
```

Avoid a single global correction factor.

Reason:

```text
tool-heavy projections and plain text projections have different overhead patterns
```

### Correction factor

A bucket can maintain a conservative correction factor.

Example:

```text
correctedEstimate = rawEstimate * bucketMultiplier + bucketConstantOverhead
```

Bucket fields:

```text
sampleCount
p50ErrorRatio
p90ErrorRatio
p95ErrorRatio
maxUnderestimateRatio
bucketMultiplier
bucketConstantOverhead
lastUpdatedAt
```

Conservative initial rule:

```text
bucketMultiplier = 1.15
bucketConstantOverhead = 512
```

If actual usage shows stable lower overhead, reduce slowly:

```text
require enough samples
require no recent overflow
require p95 underestimation below approved threshold
```

### Cached token handling

Cached prompt tokens should not be treated as free budget.

They can reduce cost and latency, but they still occupy model context.

Policy:

```text
prompt budget uses actualPromptTokens
cost reporting may subtract or separately account actualCachedPromptTokens
cache preservation is an optimization metric, not a safety allowance
```

Why:

```text
cached input can still push the context window toward overflow
```

### Overflow feedback

Provider context overflow is a hard calibration signal.

If a provider returns overflow:

```text
mark projection as provider_blocked
record rendered input hash
record estimated tokens
record provider error
increase bucket safety margin
trigger smaller projection only through approved lifecycle transition
```

Do not:

```text
retry by silently dropping old messages
retry by changing tool set without recording omission
retry by using provider-native compaction without local artifact
```

### Output reserve calibration

Output reserve should also be learned.

Output reserve inputs:

```text
workflow type
expected response type
max tool steps
tool call density
report generation mode
model
provider
```

Migration report mode needs larger output reserve than a short planning turn.

Suggested workflow reserve classes:

```text
short answer: low reserve
planning: medium reserve
tool loop: medium plus per-step reserve
migration report: high reserve
data transformation: high reserve
provider-native compaction: provider-specific reserve
```

### Per-step loop calibration

Agent loops can make multiple tool calls after the initial prompt.

Budget should include:

```text
initial rendered input
expected tool call output growth
assistant reasoning/output reserve
final report reserve
```

For AI SDK step loops, `stopWhen` and max steps are relevant.

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:190

Calibration should record:

```text
maxSteps
actualStepCount
toolCallCount
toolResultTokenEstimate
completionTokens
```

### Calibration trace events

Recommended trace events:

```text
context.usage.estimated
context.usage.observed
context.usage.calibrated
context.usage.overflow
```

Required fields:

```text
projectionId
provider
model
rendererName
estimatedInputTokens
actualPromptTokens
actualCachedPromptTokens
inputEstimatorErrorRatio
bucketKey
bucketMultiplierBefore
bucketMultiplierAfter
```

### Calibration report

Operator-facing report:

```text
Usage calibration updated.

Projection:
- estimated input tokens: 82400
- actual prompt tokens: 87220
- estimator error: +4820
- error ratio: 5.5 percent

Bucket:
- provider: openai
- model: example-model
- renderer: ai-sdk
- tool profile: migration planning
- multiplier before: 1.10
- multiplier after: 1.12
```

Blocked report:

```text
Provider overflow detected.

Projection:
- estimated input tokens: 120000
- model budget: 128000
- output reserve: 8000
- safety margin: 5000

Result:
- provider rejected context
- bucket margin increased
- projection marked provider_blocked
```

### Calibration tests

Fixture UC1: estimator undercounts.

```text
estimated: 90000
actual: 100000
expected: positive error ratio and increased bucket multiplier
```

Fixture UC2: estimator overcounts.

```text
estimated: 100000
actual: 85000
expected: no immediate aggressive reduction
```

Fixture UC3: cached tokens present.

```text
actualPromptTokens: 100000
actualCachedPromptTokens: 60000
expected: prompt budget uses 100000 and cost report records cache ratio
```

Fixture UC4: tool-heavy bucket.

```text
toolCount: high
expected: tool-heavy bucket updated, plain text bucket unchanged
```

Fixture UC5: provider overflow.

```text
provider error: context overflow
expected: projection provider_blocked and bucket safety margin increased
```

Fixture UC6: output reserve too small.

```text
workflow: migration report
completion truncated
expected: reserve class adjusted upward for report workflow
```

### Implementation slice after approval

First slice:

```text
persist estimated versus actual usage in trace payloads
calculate estimator error ratios in tests
do not auto-tune live behavior yet
```

Second slice:

```text
bucket calibration records
conservative multiplier application
overflow feedback
operator calibration report
```

Target slice:

```text
provider/model/renderer adaptive budget profiles
cache preservation metrics
workflow-specific output reserve tuning
calibration dashboards
```

### Recommendation

Use actual provider usage as a conservative calibration signal, not as an unchecked automatic policy engine.

Reason:

```text
context safety needs estimates before the call and measured feedback after the call
```

## Migration workflow compaction checkpoints

Status: design proposal.

Ekairos compaction should be workflow-aware.

A migration session has different context risks at different stages. A single generic "old messages get summarized" policy is too blunt.

This section proposes compaction checkpoints for migration work.

### Checkpoint principle

Each migration stage should define:

```text
must-keep source material
compressible source material
retrieval-only source material
forbidden omissions
block conditions
operator report fields
```

The projection builder can then select context based on current migration stage instead of raw age alone.

### Stage 0: task intake

Goal:

```text
understand the requested migration, constraints, environment, and approval state
```

Must keep:

```text
current user request
project instructions
technical-leader constraints
target package/app
environment
explicit no-go constraints
time gate or reporting gate
```

Compressible:

```text
old brainstorming
older assistant plans
non-operative context on unrelated packages
```

Retrieval-only:

```text
older source catalogs
large previous report sections
historical examples not active in this migration
```

Forbidden omission:

```text
latest user correction
branch/push/deploy rule
no-implementation constraint when active
```

Block conditions:

```text
unclear target environment
conflicting user constraints
approval required for architecture or schema work
```

Operator report fields:

```text
activeRequest
activeConstraints
approvalState
blockedDecisions
```

### Stage 1: schema and domain discovery

Goal:

```text
identify current schema, domain model, package boundaries, and relevant code paths
```

Must keep:

```text
latest inspected schema files
domain model evidence
file anchors for relevant symbols
command outputs showing package scripts
known external process caveats
```

Compressible:

```text
large grep output
repeated file lists
older unsuccessful search paths
```

Retrieval-only:

```text
full source files that can be re-read
full test logs when only pass/fail is currently needed
```

Forbidden omission:

```text
file anchor for every schema fact used in a proposal
evidence that a script exists or does not exist
```

Block conditions:

```text
schema fact claimed without source
source file changed after inspection
package boundary unclear
```

Operator report fields:

```text
inspectedFiles
schemaEntities
packageScripts
unverifiedFacts
```

### Stage 2: organization and runtime matrix

Goal:

```text
resolve org, app, environment, admin permission, and runtime access matrix
```

Must keep:

```text
org ids
app ids
environment names
admin runtime resolution result
permission state
source of credentials without revealing secrets
```

Compressible:

```text
old failed attempts after final result is available
tool chatter around retries
```

Retrieval-only:

```text
raw credential lookup logs after redaction and summary
```

Forbidden omission:

```text
org/app pairing
environment
permission failure
redaction state
```

Block conditions:

```text
cross-org source mix
unknown admin permission
secret-bearing source not redacted
```

Operator report fields:

```text
orgMatrix
permissionStatus
redactionStatus
blockedOrgEntries
```

### Stage 3: schema dry-run planning

Goal:

```text
produce and verify a schema dry-run plan before data movement
```

Must keep:

```text
dry-run command or approved workflow
result status
per-app result
schema differences
errors
warnings
operator approval state
```

Compressible:

```text
long unchanged successful dry-run output
duplicate warnings
verbose generated plan text after structured plan is stored
```

Retrieval-only:

```text
full raw dry-run output when structured summary cites exact source
```

Forbidden omission:

```text
failed dry-run
warning requiring human review
per-app gate result
```

Block conditions:

```text
summary claims dry-run passed without source
one app missing from matrix
dry-run result stale after schema edit
```

Operator report fields:

```text
dryRunStatus
appsChecked
failures
warnings
nextRequiredApproval
```

### Stage 4: dataset extraction

Goal:

```text
extract source data for deterministic transformation
```

Must keep:

```text
query source
dataset scope
row counts
filter criteria
timestamp
org/app scope
extraction errors
redaction status
```

Compressible:

```text
raw rows after checksums and counts are recorded
large repeated JSON payloads
verbose successful pagination logs
```

Retrieval-only:

```text
raw extraction artifact stored outside model context
```

Forbidden omission:

```text
row count
filter criterion
partial extraction failure
secret redaction state
```

Block conditions:

```text
dataset scope ambiguous
row count missing
raw sensitive data would enter model input
```

Operator report fields:

```text
datasetName
orgScope
rowCount
filters
artifactReference
checksums
redactionStatus
```

### Stage 5: transformation plan

Goal:

```text
produce deterministic transformation from source dataset to target transactions
```

Must keep:

```text
transformation rules
input schema assumptions
output schema assumptions
idempotency key strategy
validation rules
known lossy transformations
```

Compressible:

```text
old alternative transformation approaches
intermediate exploratory calculations
verbose example rows after representative fixtures are stored
```

Retrieval-only:

```text
full transformed dataset artifacts
```

Forbidden omission:

```text
lossy mapping
idempotency assumption
validation failure
unresolved edge case
```

Block conditions:

```text
transformation rule lacks source
input/output schema mismatch
idempotency cannot be proven
```

Operator report fields:

```text
rules
sourceFields
targetFields
lossyMappings
idempotencyPlan
validationFailures
```

### Stage 6: transaction plan and approval gate

Goal:

```text
build target transaction plan and obtain required approval before mutation
```

Must keep:

```text
transaction count
operation classes
target app/org
idempotency keys
approval state
rollback or disablement statement
mutation tool profile
```

Compressible:

```text
full transaction body when artifact reference and checksums exist
old plan drafts
```

Retrieval-only:

```text
full transaction JSON artifact
```

Forbidden omission:

```text
approval required
approval denied
mutation target
transaction count
idempotency key
```

Block conditions:

```text
approval state unknown
mutation tool included without approval
transaction plan lacks deterministic source
```

Operator report fields:

```text
mutationTarget
transactionCount
operationSummary
approvalState
idempotency
artifactReference
```

### Stage 7: migration execution

Goal:

```text
apply approved transactions in the approved scope
```

Must keep:

```text
approval source
execution command/tool result
transaction batch ids
success/failure per batch
partial failure state
retry status
```

Compressible:

```text
verbose successful batch logs after structured result exists
```

Retrieval-only:

```text
full execution logs
```

Forbidden omission:

```text
partial failure
retry result
batch id
mutation target
```

Block conditions:

```text
execution attempted without approval
execution result missing
partial failure summarized as success
```

Operator report fields:

```text
approvalSource
batches
successCount
failureCount
retryState
currentDataState
```

### Stage 8: verification

Goal:

```text
prove the migration result matches expected target state
```

Must keep:

```text
verification query
expected result
actual result
row counts
sample ids
failed assertions
environment
timestamp
```

Compressible:

```text
large successful verification output after structured pass/fail and samples are stored
```

Retrieval-only:

```text
full verification artifacts
```

Forbidden omission:

```text
failed assertion
unexpected row count
environment mismatch
stale verification after retry
```

Block conditions:

```text
report claims verification passed without query result
verification run before final mutation
environment mismatch
```

Operator report fields:

```text
verificationStatus
queries
expected
actual
failures
artifactReference
```

### Stage 9: report and handoff

Goal:

```text
produce human-readable migration report and next actions
```

Must keep:

```text
scope
approvals
schema dry-run
dataset extraction summary
transformation summary
execution summary
verification summary
known residual risks
manual test credentials when available and approved
```

Compressible:

```text
old exploration
duplicate logs
non-selected proposals
```

Retrieval-only:

```text
full raw artifacts
```

Forbidden omission:

```text
failed or blocked stage
manual action required
credentials caveat
unverified environment
```

Block conditions:

```text
report says complete when verification is missing
report omits failed stage
report includes secret value
```

Operator report fields:

```text
finalStatus
scope
artifacts
verification
knownRisks
manualReviewInstructions
```

### Cross-stage carry-forward rules

Some facts remain active across all stages.

Always carry:

```text
current user request
project instruction constraints
latest approval state
tenant scope
redaction policy
blocked claims
current stage
next required gate
```

Carry while relevant:

```text
source file anchors
dry-run result
dataset checksums
transaction plan id
verification query ids
```

Archive when complete and cited:

```text
exploratory searches
old rejected alternatives
verbose successful logs
duplicate source listings
```

### Stage transition validation

Before moving to a later stage, the projection should validate that prior gates are satisfied.

Examples:

```text
cannot move from schema discovery to transaction plan without approved dry-run path
cannot move from extraction to execution without transformation plan
cannot move from transaction plan to execution without approval
cannot move from execution to final report without verification or explicit blocked status
```

This does not require autonomous orchestration.

It gives the context engine enough state to avoid unsafe summaries.

### Migration checkpoint tests

Fixture MC1: dry-run failure omitted.

```text
stage: schema dry-run
source: dry-run failed
summary: ready to migrate
expected: required_claim_omitted and conflicting_claims
```

Fixture MC2: extraction row count missing.

```text
stage: dataset extraction
source: extraction completed but row count missing
summary: dataset extracted
expected: blocked
```

Fixture MC3: approval denied then execution planned.

```text
stage: transaction plan
source: user denied mutation approval
summary: execute migration next
expected: approval_blocked
```

Fixture MC4: verification stale after retry.

```text
stage: verification
source: retry happened after verification
summary: verification passed
expected: stale_source
```

Fixture MC5: report omits partial failure.

```text
stage: report
source: one batch failed
summary: migration completed successfully
expected: conflicting_claims
```

### Recommendation

Make migration stage an explicit projection input.

Reason:

```text
the same source material has different safety value depending on the migration stage
```

## Framework memory addendum: LangGraph, LlamaIndex, AutoGen

Status: source-backed research addendum.

Checked on 2026-05-02 against official docs.

This addendum covers three general agent frameworks that are not coding agents in the same way as Claude Code, OpenCode, or Codex, but their context handling patterns are relevant.

Sources:

```text
https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/add-memory
https://developers.llamaindex.ai/python/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/memory/
https://microsoft.github.io/autogen/dev/user-guide/core-user-guide/components/model-context.html
https://microsoft.github.io/autogen/dev/user-guide/agentchat-user-guide/memory.html
```

### LangGraph memory

LangGraph documents two broad memory classes:

```text
short-term memory in graph state for multi-turn conversation
long-term memory for user-specific or application-level data across sessions
```

For long conversations, LangGraph describes several short-term memory management options:

```text
trim messages
delete messages
summarize messages
manage checkpoints
custom strategies
```

The `trim_messages` example is significant because it uses explicit parameters:

```text
strategy: last
token counter
max_tokens
start_on
end_on
```

Ekairos lesson:

```text
message trimming must preserve structural boundaries, not only token count
```

In Ekairos terms:

```text
start_on and end_on resemble renderer invariants
checkpoints resemble durable event history
summarization resembles compaction artifact generation
delete messages is unsafe as a default for audit-grade migration context
```

### LangGraph transfer ideas

Transfer:

```text
make memory management explicit before model call
separate short-term and long-term context
use checkpoints to inspect and recover thread state
make trimming parameters visible
```

Do not transfer directly:

```text
permanent message deletion as normal compaction behavior
pure last-N retention for migration workflows
summary replacement without source-link ledger
```

Ekairos mapping:

```text
LangGraph short-term memory -> recent raw event_parts and protected active window
LangGraph long-term memory -> retrieval, rules, and approved memory plane
LangGraph checkpoints -> projection lifecycle and trace events
LangGraph trim_messages -> deterministic omission projection with structural invariants
```

### LlamaIndex Memory

LlamaIndex documents a `Memory` class with both short-term and optional long-term memory.

Relevant concepts:

```text
memory.put and memory.get
short-term FIFO chat messages
token_limit
chat_history_token_ratio
token_flush_size
long-term memory blocks
memory block priority
system or user insertion method
```

The docs describe defaults such as:

```text
token_limit default: 30000
chat_history_token_ratio default: 0.7
token_flush_size default: 3000
```

They also describe memory blocks:

```text
StaticMemoryBlock
FactExtractionMemoryBlock
VectorMemoryBlock
```

Memory block priority matters because lower-priority blocks can be truncated before higher-priority blocks when memory exceeds the token limit.

Ekairos lesson:

```text
priority-based context blocks are useful, but priority must be authority-aware
```

### LlamaIndex deprecated summary buffers

LlamaIndex docs list older memory types including:

```text
ChatMemoryBuffer
ChatSummaryMemoryBuffer
VectorMemory
SimpleComposableMemory
```

The summary buffer concept is directly related to compaction:

```text
keep recent messages under a token limit
periodically summarize conversation when it grows too long
```

Ekairos divergence:

```text
Ekairos should not treat periodic summarization as sufficient
Ekairos needs claim ledgers, tenant scope, approval state, and trace links
```

### LlamaIndex transfer ideas

Transfer:

```text
short-term token ratio
flush size
long-term memory blocks
priority ordering
fact extraction as a separate memory block
vector retrieval as a separate memory block
system/user insertion mode as renderer capability
```

Do not transfer directly:

```text
priority without authority
fact extraction without source-link validation
vector memory without tenant filters
summary buffer as canonical audit state
```

Ekairos mapping:

```text
short-term FIFO -> recent protected event window
token_flush_size -> compaction trigger granularity
memory block priority -> authority ladder plus budget class
FactExtractionMemoryBlock -> delayed auto-memory proposal
VectorMemoryBlock -> retrieval provider plane
insert_method -> provider-renderer system/user placement rule
```

### AutoGen model context

AutoGen documents model context as a separate component.

The official model context example uses:

```text
BufferedChatCompletionContext(buffer_size=5)
```

That means the example agent adds messages to a context object and then retrieves a bounded context for the model call.

Ekairos lesson:

```text
model context should be an explicit component between durable state and provider call
```

The lesson aligns strongly with the Ekairos projection layer:

```text
durable event history is not identical to provider-facing context
```

### AutoGen memory and RAG

AutoGen also documents memory and RAG patterns.

Relevant ListMemory behavior:

```text
simple list-based memory
chronological order
most recent memories appended to model context
straightforward and predictable
```

The RAG example stores retrieved memory content with metadata such as:

```text
source
score
id
chunk_index
mime_type
```

Ekairos lesson:

```text
simple chronological memory is debuggable, but retrieval metadata must become source-link metadata for audit
```

### AutoGen transfer ideas

Transfer:

```text
separate model context object
bounded context buffer for simple workflows
chronological memory as predictable baseline
retrieval metadata with ids, scores, and sources
```

Do not transfer directly:

```text
fixed-size buffer as migration compaction policy
retrieval appended without authority classification
memory appended without source-link validation
```

Ekairos mapping:

```text
BufferedChatCompletionContext -> projection budget and recent window
ListMemory -> low-risk chronological memory plane
RAG memory metadata -> retrieval result source links
model context component -> provider-neutral projection object
```

### Comparative lesson

These frameworks converge on a few recurring ideas:

```text
there is durable conversation state
there is provider-facing model context
long conversations need trimming, summarization, retrieval, or memory
token limits should be explicit
recent messages are usually privileged
retrieval needs metadata
```

They generally do not solve Ekairos-specific audit needs:

```text
tenant-scoped migration claims
technical-leader approval gates
schema dry-run evidence
transaction plan provenance
claim ledger validation
recursive summary drift
provider-native opacity
```

### Ekairos synthesis

Use these framework ideas as implementation vocabulary, not as the final design.

Recommended synthesis:

```text
LangGraph gives explicit memory operations and checkpoints
LlamaIndex gives token ratios, flush sizes, and memory block priorities
AutoGen gives a clean model-context component and predictable buffer example
Ekairos adds audit-grade source links, claim ledgers, tenant gates, approval state, and projection lifecycle
```

### Recommendation

Adopt the framework separation between durable state, memory, and provider-facing context, but require Ekairos-specific audit validation before any compacted material is model-visible.

Reason:

```text
general agent memory patterns optimize continuity, while Ekairos migrations require continuity plus evidence
```

## ADR draft pack for technical-leader review

Status: proposal only.

These ADR drafts are not decisions. They are review-ready decision shapes for the technical leader.

Each ADR assumes breaking changes are allowed unless the technical leader says otherwise.

### ADR 001: Introduce provider-neutral projection layer

Context:

```text
Current flow expands events and lets reactors obtain model messages.
Context compaction needs a stable point to classify, budget, summarize, validate, and render context.
```

Decision proposed:

```text
Introduce a provider-neutral projection layer between durable event history and provider rendering.
```

Consequences:

```text
reactors stop being responsible for context selection
projection manifests become reviewable artifacts
provider rendering can vary without changing selection logic
```

Breaking impact:

```text
reactor input contract changes in target architecture
tests must assert projection behavior before reactor behavior
```

Rejection consequence:

```text
compaction logic will likely live inside expandEvents, store rendering, or individual reactors, making audit harder
```

Approval required:

```text
technical leader
```

### ADR 002: Keep raw event parts immutable

Context:

```text
event_parts are the durable replay source for context item content.
Compaction should reduce provider input, not rewrite history.
```

Decision proposed:

```text
Never mutate or delete raw event_parts as part of compaction.
```

Consequences:

```text
storage grows with raw history
projection and compaction artifacts point back to source parts
rollback and replay remain possible
```

Breaking impact:

```text
consumers cannot expect compacted event history to replace raw history
```

Rejection consequence:

```text
audit trail can lose raw evidence and recursive compaction errors become hard to diagnose
```

Approval required:

```text
technical leader
```

### ADR 003: Require claim ledger for compacted artifacts

Context:

```text
Summaries can be fluent and still unsafe.
Migration workflows require proof for operational claims.
```

Decision proposed:

```text
Every model-visible compaction artifact must have a claim ledger or be marked invalid.
```

Consequences:

```text
summary generation is slower
validation is explicit
blocked projections are expected behavior
operator reports can explain source coverage
```

Breaking impact:

```text
compaction cannot be a simple string summary API
```

Rejection consequence:

```text
summaries may promote unverified claims, stale corrections, or cross-org data
```

Approval required:

```text
technical leader
security reviewer for tenant and secret policy
```

### ADR 004: Model blocked projection as first-class state

Context:

```text
Sometimes context cannot safely fit or cannot be validated.
Silent omission would be unsafe.
```

Decision proposed:

```text
Represent blocked projection as a durable lifecycle state with reason codes.
```

Consequences:

```text
operators see precise remediation
agent loop can pause instead of guessing
tests can assert no unsafe dispatch
```

Breaking impact:

```text
callers must handle projection-blocked outcomes
```

Rejection consequence:

```text
engine may either overrun context or continue with unsafe missing evidence
```

Approval required:

```text
technical leader
product reviewer for UX treatment
```

### ADR 005: Separate retrieval, rules, memory, and compaction

Context:

```text
Coding agents and frameworks often mix retrieval, memories, rules, and summaries in the final prompt.
Ekairos needs different authority levels for each source class.
```

Decision proposed:

```text
Model retrieval, rule activation, memory, and compaction as separate projection inputs with distinct authority and trace fields.
```

Consequences:

```text
the projection builder has more inputs
source classification becomes explicit
auto memory cannot override project/user rules
retrieval requires tenant filters
```

Breaking impact:

```text
future APIs should not expose a single untyped context blob
```

Rejection consequence:

```text
low-authority memories or retrieved snippets may override higher-authority instructions
```

Approval required:

```text
technical leader
```

### ADR 006: Delay provider-native compaction until local ledger exists

Context:

```text
Provider-native compaction can reduce context pressure but is often provider-specific and partly opaque.
```

Decision proposed:

```text
Do not make provider-native compaction the first canonical implementation. Use it later only with a local companion artifact.
```

Consequences:

```text
first implementation is provider-neutral
audit remains local
provider adapters can be added later
```

Breaking impact:

```text
initial design does not rely on provider-native compact endpoints or beta headers
```

Rejection consequence:

```text
audit may depend on provider state Ekairos cannot inspect or replay
```

Approval required:

```text
technical leader
provider owner when selecting adapter
```

### ADR 007: Use migration stage as projection input

Context:

```text
Migration workflows move through task intake, discovery, dry-run, extraction, transformation, approval, execution, verification, and report stages.
Each stage has different must-keep context.
```

Decision proposed:

```text
Projection builder receives current migration stage and applies stage-specific must-keep and block rules.
```

Consequences:

```text
selector behavior becomes more precise
tests can model stage-specific omissions
operator reports can say which gate is active
```

Breaking impact:

```text
generic context projection contracts need workflow metadata
```

Rejection consequence:

```text
age-based compaction may drop a dry-run failure or approval denial because it is old
```

Approval required:

```text
technical leader
domain/migration owner
```

### ADR 008: Add rendered budget gate after provider rendering

Context:

```text
Provider-specific message and tool schema shapes can exceed estimates after rendering.
```

Decision proposed:

```text
Require a final rendered budget gate before reactor dispatch.
```

Consequences:

```text
projection may pass but rendering may block
tool schema cost becomes visible
provider adapters declare capabilities
usage telemetry can calibrate future estimates
```

Breaking impact:

```text
reactors cannot dispatch immediately after receiving raw events
```

Rejection consequence:

```text
provider overflow remains likely even when abstract projection budget passes
```

Approval required:

```text
technical leader
reactor owner
```

### ADR 009: Persist usage calibration data

Context:

```text
Provider usage is observed after calls, while projection decisions are made before calls.
```

Decision proposed:

```text
Persist estimated versus actual usage in trace/calibration artifacts and use it later for conservative estimator tuning.
```

Consequences:

```text
budgeting improves over time
cache tokens are reported separately
overflow produces calibration signal
```

Breaking impact:

```text
trace payload schema expands
future dashboards can rely on usage fields
```

Rejection consequence:

```text
token budgeting remains static and blind to provider-specific overhead
```

Approval required:

```text
technical leader
observability owner
```

### ADR 010: Treat recursive compaction as lineage graph

Context:

```text
Long-running sessions compact repeatedly.
Summaries of summaries can drift away from raw evidence.
```

Decision proposed:

```text
Record source depth, root source ids, and drift metrics for recursive compaction.
```

Consequences:

```text
active operational claims need root-source refresh
summary depth can be bounded
drift can block projection
```

Breaking impact:

```text
compaction artifacts need lineage metadata
```

Rejection consequence:

```text
old summary errors can become canonical after repeated compression
```

Approval required:

```text
technical leader
```

### ADR 011: Delay auto-memory promotion

Context:

```text
Memory extraction can be useful but can also convert transient statements into durable policy.
```

Decision proposed:

```text
Do not include auto-memory promotion in the first implementation slice.
```

Consequences:

```text
first slice focuses on projection, budget, validation, and reporting
memory plane can be designed after compaction invariants are proven
```

Breaking impact:

```text
no memory API guarantee in first slice
```

Rejection consequence:

```text
auto memory may override higher-authority user/project instructions or carry stale facts
```

Approval required:

```text
technical leader
```

### ADR 012: Make reports mandatory for migration compaction

Context:

```text
Migration operators need to know what context was kept, summarized, omitted, retrieved, and blocked.
```

Decision proposed:

```text
Every migration-stage compaction or blocked projection emits an operator report.
```

Consequences:

```text
manual review becomes possible
final migration reports can cite projection history
testing can assert report content
```

Breaking impact:

```text
projection code must produce human-readable and structured report artifacts
```

Rejection consequence:

```text
operators see model behavior but not context-selection reasons
```

Approval required:

```text
technical leader
product reviewer
```

### Suggested approval order

Recommended order:

```text
ADR 001 projection layer
ADR 002 raw event immutability
ADR 004 blocked projection state
ADR 008 rendered budget gate
ADR 003 claim ledger
ADR 009 usage calibration
ADR 007 migration stage input
ADR 010 recursive lineage
ADR 005 retrieval/rules/memory/compaction split
ADR 006 provider-native delay
ADR 011 auto-memory delay
ADR 012 reports
```

Reason:

```text
the first four decisions define the minimal safe frame for any implementation slice
```

### ADR pack recommendation

Use this ADR pack as the approval packet before code, schema, config, provider, or infra work.

Reason:

```text
the project rule requires technical-leader architectural approval before execution
```

No schema work is approved by this document.

### Existing schema anchor

The current schema already has context, item, execution, step, part, and trace entities.

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\schema.ts:7

### Primary access paths

Projection storage should support these access paths:
