```text
very large context windows still benefit from retrieval-first projection
```

### Budget decision table

Decision table:

```text
raw fits with high headroom and low noise -> raw_fits
raw fits but old material is noisy -> compact_old_history
raw fits but tool schemas are unrelated -> reduce_tool_surface
raw fits but source catalog is large -> retrieve_instead_of_inline
protected material exceeds budget -> block or split task
unknown model budget -> block
unknown redaction state -> block
```

### Ledger trace fields

Trace should record:

```text
projectionId
modelWindowTokens
estimatedInputTokens
estimatedTotalRequiredTokens
headroomTokens
decision
budgetBreakdown
toolSchemaTokens
outputReserveTokens
safetyMarginTokens
```

### Recommendation

Expose the budget as a ledger in traces and reports.

Reason:

```text
operators need to see why context was compacted, not only that compaction happened
```

## Cross-system design laws for Ekairos compaction

Status: synthesis proposal.

Across Claude, OpenAI Responses, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, Cline, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Aider, Continue, Zed, Goose, Roo, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, and AutoGen, the same context-management pressures repeat.

The systems differ in implementation, but the design laws for Ekairos are clear.

### Law 1: durable history and model context are not the same thing

Observed pattern:

```text
agents retain durable or session state separately from what they send to the model
frameworks expose memory, checkpoints, buffers, or provider conversation state
coding agents rely on project files and transcript state but still select a prompt window
```

Ekairos law:

```text
event_parts remain durable history
projection is the model-facing view
```

Design consequence:

```text
never implement compaction by rewriting raw event history
```

### Law 2: recent intent has privileged status

Observed pattern:

```text
trimming utilities often keep the last messages
coding agents prioritize recent user turns and current task state
manual compaction guidance often preserves current task and next steps
```

Ekairos law:

```text
current user intent, latest correction, and active approval state are protected source packets
```

Design consequence:

```text
recent active material is not summarized merely because it is long
```

### Law 3: token count is necessary but insufficient

Observed pattern:

```text
frameworks use token limits, buffer sizes, and trimming thresholds
coding agents compact when near context window limits
providers expose usage and context windows
```

Ekairos law:

```text
projection must check budget and authority together
```

Design consequence:

```text
context can be compacted even when it fits if it is noisy, and blocked even after compaction if protected material exceeds budget
```

### Law 4: summarization is only one context strategy

Observed pattern:

```text
systems use trimming, deletion, retrieval, repo maps, memory blocks, rules, checkpoints, and summaries
```

Ekairos law:

```text
summarization, retrieval, rules, memory, and omission are separate projection strategies
```

Design consequence:

```text
do not build a single summarizeOldMessages function as the context architecture
```

### Law 5: retrieval score is not authority

Observed pattern:

```text
retrieval systems return ranked snippets, vector matches, or codemap context
```

Ekairos law:

```text
retrieval can find candidates, but authority comes from source class, tenant scope, and freshness
```

Design consequence:

```text
retrieved snippets must pass source classification before model visibility
```

### Law 6: memory is not policy

Observed pattern:

```text
agent frameworks can store long-term memory or extracted facts
IDE agents can maintain memories or rules
```

Ekairos law:

```text
memory is lower authority than current user, project instruction, technical-leader approval, and local tool result
```

Design consequence:

```text
auto memory cannot approve or deny schema, branch, release, provider, infra, or migration execution decisions
```

### Law 7: provider-native compaction is an adapter feature

Observed pattern:

```text
some providers expose conversation state or compaction mechanisms
coding agents may have provider-specific context behavior
```

Ekairos law:

```text
provider-native compaction may optimize provider state, but local projection remains canonical
```

Design consequence:

```text
provider-native compacted state needs a local companion artifact and claim ledger
```

### Law 8: tool schemas are prompt context

Observed pattern:

```text
agent loops pass tool definitions to models
tool-heavy contexts consume large input budgets
tools imply action capability
```

Ekairos law:

```text
tool schema selection is part of projection and approval policy
```

Design consequence:

```text
tool count, tool schema token estimate, tool danger class, and omitted tools must be recorded
```

### Law 9: summaries drift unless rooted

Observed pattern:

```text
recursive summaries can become less precise
memory extraction can strengthen weak claims
manual summaries can omit failed or blocked state
```

Ekairos law:

```text
recursive compaction must preserve root source links for active operational claims
```

Design consequence:

```text
summaries of summaries are allowed for background, not as sole evidence for active migration facts
```

### Law 10: model-visible context must be auditable

Observed pattern:

```text
coding agents often show some transcript or context but not always full source provenance
frameworks prioritize memory continuity over audit
```

Ekairos law:

```text
every model-visible compacted claim needs source-link validation
```

Design consequence:

```text
claim ledger is the acceptance gate for compaction artifacts
```

### Law 11: blocked context is product behavior

Observed pattern:

```text
many tools either trim or summarize automatically
some systems expose manual compaction or context management controls
```

Ekairos law:

```text
unsafe projection should block and explain remediation
```

Design consequence:

```text
blocked projection state must be explicit, traceable, and visible to the operator
```

### Law 12: evaluation must include lost-claim tests

Observed pattern:

```text
context systems often measure fit and cost but safety depends on what is lost
```

Ekairos law:

```text
test compaction by checking required claim recall, forbidden promotion, source coverage, authority boundaries, and tenant scope
```

Design consequence:

```text
budget pass is not sufficient; claim and fixture pass are required
```

### Law 13: large context windows do not remove context engineering

Observed pattern:

```text
modern models can have large windows, but long prompts still carry cost, latency, distraction, and retrieval-noise risks
```

Ekairos law:

```text
projection should optimize for evidence quality, not only fitting the model window
```

Design consequence:

```text
old noisy material may be compacted even in 128k, 200k, or larger windows
```

### Law 14: workflow stage matters

Observed pattern:

```text
general frameworks expose memory primitives but do not know migration gates
coding agents know tasks but not Ekairos migration stages by default
```

Ekairos law:

```text
migration stage is a projection input
```

Design consequence:

```text
dry-run failures, extraction counts, approval denials, execution batches, and verification results have stage-specific preservation rules
```

### Law 15: traces are part of the feature

Observed pattern:

```text
provider usage, agent loop steps, and durable events create debugging trails
```

Ekairos law:

```text
projection, compaction, validation, rendering, dispatch, and usage calibration all need trace events
```

Design consequence:

```text
if the system cannot explain why a source was omitted or summarized, it is not ready for migration compaction
```

### Law-to-proposal mapping

Mapping:

```text
Law 1 -> projection layer and raw event immutability
Law 2 -> protected recent window
Law 3 -> budget ledger and blocked projection
Law 4 -> retrieval/rules/memory/compaction split
Law 5 -> source packet authority fields
Law 6 -> delayed auto-memory design
Law 7 -> provider-native adapter strategy
Law 8 -> tool-schema budget
Law 9 -> recursive lineage
Law 10 -> claim ledger
Law 11 -> lifecycle blocked state
Law 12 -> fixture and evaluation plan
Law 13 -> model-window profiles and retrieval-first projection
Law 14 -> migration checkpoints
Law 15 -> trace payloads and operator reports
```

### Recommendation

Use these laws as the design review rubric.

Reason:

```text
they turn a wide survey of agent systems into concrete Ekairos approval criteria
```

## Rejected unsafe pattern catalog

Status: design guardrail.

These patterns should be rejected during technical review unless the technical leader explicitly approves a different direction.

### Pattern 1: hidden transcript truncation

Description:

```text
drop old messages until the prompt fits
```

Why unsafe:

```text
can remove approvals, denials, failed tool outputs, tenant scope, or latest corrections
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
projection manifest with omitted-source records and block states
```

### Pattern 2: summary replaces raw history

Description:

```text
write compacted summary back over raw event history
```

Why unsafe:

```text
destroys replay evidence and makes drift permanent
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
raw event_parts stay immutable and compaction artifacts link back to them
```

### Pattern 3: provider-only compaction

Description:

```text
call provider-native compact feature and treat provider state as canonical
```

Why unsafe:

```text
local audit cannot prove which source claims survived
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
local projection manifest and claim ledger remain canonical; provider-native state is optional adapter metadata
```

### Pattern 4: age-only selector

Description:

```text
summarize anything older than a fixed number of turns
```

Why unsafe:

```text
old facts can still be active, especially approvals, dry-run failures, transaction plans, and verification results
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
stage-aware selector with authority, freshness, tenant, and materiality checks
```

### Pattern 5: summary as system instruction

Description:

```text
put assistant-generated summary into the highest-authority prompt channel
```

Why unsafe:

```text
assistant summary can override project or user instructions
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
summary remains explicitly compacted context with source ids and lower authority than system/project/user instructions
```

### Pattern 6: memory as approval

Description:

```text
extract a memory that says a user usually approves a workflow and use it as approval
```

Why unsafe:

```text
approval must be explicit, current, and scoped
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
approval state comes from current user or technical-leader source packets only
```

### Pattern 7: retrieval without tenant filter

Description:

```text
retrieve semantically similar context without org/app/environment constraint
```

Why unsafe:

```text
can leak or blend tenant-scoped migration data
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
retrieval provider requires tenant scope and source authority metadata
```

### Pattern 8: tool surface is all or nothing

Description:

```text
include every registered tool in every model call
```

Why unsafe:

```text
tool schemas consume context, distract the model, and expose capabilities not relevant to current stage
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
stage-specific tool profiles with omitted-tool reporting and approval metadata
```

### Pattern 9: rendered budget skipped

Description:

```text
trust abstract projection estimates and dispatch without checking provider-rendered shape
```

Why unsafe:

```text
provider message wrappers and tool schemas can exceed budget after rendering
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
final rendered budget gate before reactor dispatch
```

### Pattern 10: failed tool output becomes narrative success

Description:

```text
summarize a failed command or tool result as if the task was handled
```

Why unsafe:

```text
model may continue from a false state
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
tool result status is must-keep and validated in claim ledger
```

### Pattern 11: dry-run result decays into background

Description:

```text
summarize dry-run failures as old context after more turns pass
```

Why unsafe:

```text
dry-run failure remains a migration gate until remediated
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
migration stage keeps dry-run status active until newer verified source supersedes it
```

### Pattern 12: source URLs without fetch date

Description:

```text
cite external docs without recording when they were checked
```

Why unsafe:

```text
provider behavior and docs can change
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
external source packets include fetchedAt and confidence caveat
```

### Pattern 13: no blocked state

Description:

```text
force projection to always return some prompt
```

Why unsafe:

```text
some contexts cannot safely fit or cannot be validated
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
blocked projection lifecycle status with remediation report
```

### Pattern 14: large-window complacency

Description:

```text
skip compaction because the target model has a large context window
```

Why unsafe:

```text
large windows still suffer from cost, latency, attention pollution, and stale evidence
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
budget plus context-quality decisions, even when raw text fits
```

### Pattern 15: implementation before approval

Description:

```text
make code, schema, config, provider, branch, release, or infra changes without technical-leader approval
```

Why unsafe:

```text
violates project governance and can introduce uncontrolled contract or rollout changes
```

Ekairos alternative:

```text
produce proposal docs, ADRs, approval packets, and tests plans first
```

### Review usage

During future PR review, each implementation slice should answer:

```text
which rejected patterns were considered?
which tests prove they are not present?
which trace/report fields make the safe behavior visible?
```

### Recommendation

Treat this catalog as a negative acceptance checklist.

Reason:

```text
clear rejected patterns reduce ambiguity before implementation starts
```

## Technical-leader approval templates

Status: proposal only.

These templates are designed to be copied into future approval requests. They do not approve any implementation.

### Template: projection contracts only

Approval request:

```text
Approve implementation of projection contract types only.
```

Scope:

```text
source packet types
projection segment types
budget ledger types
projection manifest type
blocked projection result type
unit tests for pure classification and budgeting
```

Explicit non-scope:

```text
no schema changes
no provider-native compaction
no reactor contract break
no runtime behavior change
no branch creation unless separately requested
no release
```

Breaking stance:

```text
new public types may be added intentionally
existing behavior should not silently change
```

Required validation:

```text
typecheck
typecheck:tests
test
artifact report listing exported types and test files
```

Decision needed:

```text
approve or reject first pure contract slice
```

### Template: projection builder in engine loop

Approval request:

```text
Approve adding projection builder execution before reactor dispatch.
```

Scope:

```text
build source packets from expanded events
classify packets into segments
compute budget ledger
record projection trace payload
allow raw_fits path to preserve current behavior
block on explicit unsafe states
```

Explicit non-scope:

```text
no automatic LLM summary
no provider-native compaction
no schema entity migration unless separately approved
no mutation of raw event_parts
```

Breaking stance:

```text
engine may return blocked projection result if approved
```

Required validation:

```text
unit tests for selector
scripted reactor tests
workflow tests if durable behavior changes
operator report snapshot for blocked state
```

Decision needed:

```text
approve or reject engine insertion point and blocked behavior
```

### Template: reactor contract break

Approval request:

```text
Approve breaking reactor contract so reactors receive projection-aware input.
```

Scope:

```text
new reactor params
projection manifest passed to reactor
provider-neutral action metadata preserved
renderer output passed to provider-specific reactor
consumer migration notes
```

Explicit non-scope:

```text
no provider-native compaction adapter unless separately approved
no schema migration unless separately approved
```

Breaking stance:

```text
public reactor contract changes intentionally
downstream reactor authors must update
```

Required validation:

```text
typecheck
typecheck:tests
test:scripted-reactor
test:ai-sdk-reactor
consumer contract report
```

Decision needed:

```text
approve or reject reactor contract break
```

### Template: schema/domain expansion

Approval request:

```text
Approve first-class projection schema/domain entities.
```

Scope:

```text
projection entities
projection segment entities
source link entities
compaction artifact entities
claim ledger fields
trace/domain links
schema dry-run plan
```

Explicit non-scope:

```text
no production rollout
no data migration execution
no provider-native compaction
```

Breaking stance:

```text
schema changes are intentional and require migration artifacts
```

Required validation:

```text
schema plan
local typecheck
store tests
query/access path report
migration report draft
```

Decision needed:

```text
approve or reject schema/domain expansion
```

### Template: local LLM compaction artifact

Approval request:

```text
Approve local compaction artifact generation with claim-ledger validation.
```

Scope:

```text
compactor prompt pack
structured summary output
claim extraction
source-link validation
blocked projection on validation failure
operator report
```

Explicit non-scope:

```text
no provider-native compact endpoint
no auto-memory promotion
no production data migration
```

Breaking stance:

```text
model-facing summaries are accepted only after validation
```

Required validation:

```text
claim-ledger unit fixtures
red-team fixtures
migration fixture pack
manual report review
```

Decision needed:

```text
approve or reject local compactor and validator
```

### Template: provider-native compaction adapter

Approval request:

```text
Approve provider-native compaction adapter for a named provider and model family.
```

Scope:

```text
provider adapter capability record
provider compact call
provider metadata trace
local companion projection and claim ledger
usage telemetry comparison
```

Explicit non-scope:

```text
no provider-native-only canonical state
no provider adapter for other providers
no release without provider validation report
```

Breaking stance:

```text
provider adapter behavior is explicit and provider-specific
```

Required validation:

```text
official provider docs checked on current date
adapter unit tests
real provider smoke if approved and credentials available
local companion ledger proof
cost/usage report
```

Decision needed:

```text
approve or reject provider-native adapter
```

### Template: migration-stage selector

Approval request:

```text
Approve migration-stage-aware selector policy.
```

Scope:

```text
stage enum or policy input
must-keep rules by stage
blocked conditions by stage
operator reports by stage
fixtures for dry-run, extraction, approval, execution, verification, and report
```

Explicit non-scope:

```text
no autonomous migration execution
no production rollout
no schema changes unless separately approved
```

Breaking stance:

```text
projection behavior changes based on workflow stage
```

Required validation:

```text
migration selector tests
blocked report examples
manual review by migration owner
```

Decision needed:

```text
approve or reject stage-aware selector
```

### Template: downstream beta validation

Approval request:

```text
Approve downstream beta validation of released package behavior.
```

Scope:

```text
publish or consume beta version after package validation
update downstream app dependency
run approved product flow
capture credentials/review links only when available and safe
```

Explicit non-scope:

```text
no production rollout unless separately approved
no branch creation unless explicitly requested
no Vercel or deployment inspection unless branch/deploy flow is active and approved
```

Breaking stance:

```text
downstream consumer receives intentional beta behavior
```

Required validation:

```text
package tests
publish workflow success if used
npm beta version check if used
downstream install/update report
product smoke report
```

Decision needed:

```text
approve or reject downstream beta validation
```

### Approval record fields

Every approval should record:

```text
approvalId
approvedBy
approvedAt
scope
explicitNonScope
breakingChangesAccepted
requiredValidation
expiration or supersession condition
```

### Recommendation

Use explicit approval templates before implementation.

Reason:

```text
project governance requires architectural approval, and compaction touches public contracts, schema, runtime behavior, and provider calls
```

## Source reliability and recheck policy

Status: research governance proposal.

This artifact uses several source classes. They should not be treated as equal.

### Reliability tiers

Tier 1: current project instructions.

```text
highest authority for what may be done in this workspace
must override assistant plans and external patterns
```

Tier 2: current user instruction.

```text
highest authority for the active task
must be checked for latest corrections
```

Tier 3: local repository source inspected in this run.

```text
highest authority for current local code shape
can become stale after file edits
```

Tier 4: local command output from this run.

```text
high authority for observed state at command time
can become stale after changes
```

Tier 5: official vendor documentation fetched in this run.

```text
high authority for provider/framework behavior at fetch time
can change after fetch date
```

Tier 6: upstream source repository inspected in this run.

```text
high authority for implementation details at inspected branch or commit
not always authority for product guarantees
```

Tier 7: academic papers.

```text
useful supporting evidence and terminology
not direct authority over Ekairos implementation
```

Tier 8: secondary documentation, snippets, or crawler extracts.

```text
lower confidence
must be marked with caveat
do not use as sole source for implementation decisions
```

### Local evidence policy

Local file claims should include:

```text
absolute file anchor
line number when available
inspection date or run context
whether file is unmodified since inspection when relevant
```

When a local file changes:

```text
code facts about that file must be rechecked
```

Example:

```text
AI SDK reactor maps actions to AI SDK tools before streamText
source: local reactor file anchor
recheck: required if reactor file changes
```

### Command-output policy

Command claims should include:

```text
command
working directory
exit code
important output
time context
```

Command output expires when:

```text
files change
dependencies change
environment changes
provider credentials change
branch changes
```

Example:

```text
package scripts observed in package.json
source: local file plus command output
recheck: required if package.json changes
```

### Official docs policy

Official docs claims should include:

```text
source URL
publisher
date checked
specific behavior summarized
confidence caveat if fetched page did not render fully
```

Recheck before:

```text
implementation
provider adapter selection
using beta header
relying on current model or context-window claim
shipping docs to consumers
```

### Upstream source policy

Upstream source claims should include:

```text
repository URL
branch or commit when available
file path
observed behavior
date checked
```

Distinguish:

```text
observed code behavior
product documentation claim
inference about design intent
```

### Lower-confidence source policy

Some docs can render poorly through fetch tools or only expose snippets.

Policy:

```text
mark lower confidence
do not use as sole operational proof
prefer official docs or source repository
recheck with a browser or alternate fetch path before implementation
```

Examples from this artifact:

```text
Cursor docs were partly lower-confidence because official docs shell did not render cleanly in this run
Roo Code docs include a dated shutdown caveat and need recheck after 2026-05-15
```

### Date-sensitive claims

Claims requiring recheck:

```text
provider model windows
provider beta headers
API endpoint availability
agent product behavior
package dependencies
current branch/worktree state
GitHub workflow results
Vercel deploy status
consumer app behavior
Roo Code availability after 2026-05-15
```

Stable enough for planning but still recheck before implementation:

```text
general idea that trimming, summarization, retrieval, and memory are common context strategies
high-level local architecture shape until files change
```

### Research claim labels

The document can label claims as:

```text
observed_local
observed_official_docs
observed_upstream_source
observed_paper
inferred_from_sources
lower_confidence
proposal
requires_approval
requires_recheck
```

Recommended use:

```text
implementation decisions require observed_local, observed_official_docs, or explicit technical-leader approval
```

### Recheck checklist before implementation

Before code work:

```text
re-read relevant local files
re-run relevant rg commands
re-check package scripts
re-check official provider docs if provider feature involved
re-check upstream source if copying an external algorithm idea
re-check current branch and worktree state
confirm explicit technical-leader approval
```

Before schema work:

```text
re-read schema
re-read domain exports
confirm approved migration path
run approved schema planning flow
confirm no external process is reverting docs or package files
```

Before downstream validation:

```text
confirm branch instruction
confirm release instruction
confirm package version
confirm downstream app path and dependency state
confirm credentials and review data policy
```

### Recommendation

Keep source reliability labels in future implementation artifacts.

Reason:

```text
context compaction research is only useful if readers know which facts are observed, inferred, stale-risk, or merely proposed
```

## Artifact hygiene and client link policy

Status: active document maintenance rule.

The client detects local file references reliably only when they are written as plain absolute paths with an `@` prefix.

Therefore this artifact should use:

```text
@C:\absolute\path
@C:\absolute\path:LINE
@C:\absolute\path:LINE:COLUMN
@C:\absolute\path#LSTART-LEND
```

The artifact should avoid:

```text
relative local file references
markdown links for local files
unprefixed Windows paths
file URLs
editor URLs
```

### Local path audit

Path audit checks should include:

```text
unprefixed local Windows paths
relative package paths
relative artifact paths
markdown local links
file URL schemes
editor URL schemes
```

Current focused checks:

```text
unprefixed local Windows path scan
relative package/artifact path scan
placeholder and non-ASCII scan
```

### Why this matters

The document is long. If paths are not clickable, the technical leader has to manually search for source anchors.

For compaction research, source anchors are part of the argument.

Therefore:

```text
path formatting is not cosmetic
it affects reviewability and audit quality
```

### Recommendation

Keep path-format checks in the final audit.

Reason:

```text
the artifact is intended for technical review, and source navigation must be reliable
```

## Stale-source invalidation rules

Status: design proposal.

A projection is only valid relative to its sources.

If the source changes, the projection may become stale.

### Invalidation principle

The projection builder should track enough source metadata to answer:

```text
does this accepted projection still reflect current source reality?
```

If not:

```text
do not reuse it as active context
mark it superseded or stale
build a new projection
```

### Source changes that invalidate projections

User correction:

```text
new user instruction changes scope, output format, constraints, approval state, or stop condition
```

Project instruction change:

```text
project docs or governance rules change
```

Local file edit:

```text
file cited by a code fact changes
```

Command rerun:

```text
new command output supersedes old pass/fail/count/status claim
```

Branch/worktree change:

```text
branch changes, files are added/removed, or previously untracked artifact moves
```

Provider docs recheck:

```text
official docs change or new provider capability is observed
```

Tenant data change:

```text
organization matrix, dataset, transaction plan, execution result, or verification result changes
```

Tool surface change:

```text
registered actions, schemas, approval metadata, or danger classes change
```

Model budget change:

```text
provider, model, context window, output cap, or tokenizer behavior changes
```

### Source metadata for invalidation

Local file sources should record:

```text
absolutePath
line
contentHash
gitStatus
inspectedAt
```

Command sources should record:

```text
command
workingDirectory
exitCode
stdoutHash
stderrHash
observedAt
```

External sources should record:

```text
url
publisher
fetchedAt
retrievalMethod
confidenceCaveat
```

Tenant sources should record:

```text
orgId
appId
environment
artifactId
artifactHash
observedAt
```

Tool sources should record:

```text
toolName
schemaHash
approvalMode
dangerClass
registeredAt
```

### Staleness levels

Fresh:

```text
source metadata still matches current known state
```

Possibly stale:

```text
source might have changed but no direct contradiction is known
```

Stale:

```text
source changed after projection was accepted
```

Superseded:

```text
newer source of same or higher authority replaces prior claim
```

Invalid:

```text
projection contains claim now known false or unsafe
```

### Staleness policy by claim class

Operator instruction:

```text
newer user correction supersedes old instruction immediately
```

Technical-leader approval:

```text
newer approval or denial supersedes previous approval state
approval expires if scope no longer matches current task
```

Code fact:

```text
file edit marks code fact stale until re-read
```

Tool result:

```text
newer rerun supersedes old result for current state
old result may remain historical evidence
```

Migration fact:

```text
newer org/app/execution/verification state supersedes older state
```

External docs:

```text
implementation requires recheck if source is date-sensitive
```

### Projection reuse rules

Allowed reuse:

```text
same context
same source hashes
same tool schema hashes
same model budget profile
same active user intent
same tenant scope
```

Warning reuse:

```text
external docs are older but only used for background
old local file source is not currently active
```

Blocked reuse:

```text
new user correction exists
cited local file changed
tool schema changed
tenant matrix changed
verification result changed
model budget unknown
redaction policy changed
```

### Invalidation trace events

Recommended trace events:

```text
context.projection.staleness_checked
context.projection.marked_stale
context.projection.superseded
context.source.changed
context.source.rechecked
```

Trace payload fields:

```text
projectionId
sourceId
sourceKind
previousHash
currentHash
stalenessLevel
reason
supersededBySourceId
```

### Report examples

Stale file report:

```text
Projection marked stale.

Reason:
- cited local file changed after projection acceptance

Source:
- sourceKind: local_file
- stalenessLevel: stale

Required action:
- rebuild projection from current file content
```

User correction report:

```text
Projection superseded.

Reason:
- newer user correction changed active constraints

Required action:
- rebuild projection with latest user intent
```

### Invalidation tests

Fixture SI1: local file edit.

```text
projection cites file hash A
file hash becomes B
expected: code claims marked stale
```

Fixture SI2: command rerun.

```text
old command failed
new command passed
expected: old failure remains historical, current state uses new result
```

Fixture SI3: user correction.

```text
old projection includes implementation plan
new user says docs only
expected: old projection superseded
```

Fixture SI4: tool schema changed.

```text
projection accepted with tool schema hash A
tool schema hash becomes B
expected: rendered budget recheck required
```

Fixture SI5: external docs date-sensitive.

```text
provider compaction endpoint claim older than implementation review
expected: requires_recheck
```

### Recommendation

Treat staleness as a first-class projection property.

Reason:

```text
an accurate summary can become unsafe when the source facts it summarized are no longer current
```

## Compression-loss taxonomy

Status: design proposal.

Compaction failures are not all the same.

Different loss types need different validators, reports, and remediation.

### Loss type 1: deletion loss

Definition:

```text
a required claim or source packet disappears from model-visible context
```

Example:

```text
latest user correction is omitted
```

Risk:

```text
model follows stale intent
```

Detection:

```text
required claim coverage check
```

Remediation:

```text
rebuild projection with required claim protected
```

### Loss type 2: specificity loss

Definition:

```text
a claim remains present but loses operational details
```

Example:

```text
org-a dry-run failed because field x is missing
becomes
dry-run had an issue
```

Risk:

```text
operator or model cannot choose correct next action
```

Detection:

```text
specificity dimension check for tenant, file, command, result, timestamp, approval, and next action
```

Remediation:

```text
restore structured fields or root source citation
```

### Loss type 3: confidence inflation

Definition:

```text
summary expresses stronger certainty than source evidence allows
```

Example:

```text
lower-confidence documentation snippet becomes official confirmed fact
```

Risk:

```text
implementation relies on uncertain source
```

Detection:

```text
confidence marker preservation
```

Remediation:

```text
mark lower confidence or recheck official source
```

### Loss type 4: authority dilution

Definition:

```text
claims from different authority levels are merged without preserving hierarchy
```

Example:

```text
assistant proposal and project instruction become one "decision"
```

Risk:

```text
low-authority text overrides high-authority rules
```

Detection:

```text
authority ladder validation
```

Remediation:

```text
separate claims by source authority
```

### Loss type 5: authority promotion

Definition:

```text
lower-authority source is rendered as higher-authority instruction
```

Example:

```text
assistant-generated summary is placed in system prompt channel
```

Risk:

```text
summary becomes policy
```

Detection:

```text
renderer role and authority invariant
```

Remediation:

```text
render summary as compacted context with source ids, not system instruction
```

### Loss type 6: temporal inversion

Definition:

```text
summary reverses or obscures event order
```

Example:

```text
verification appears after retry in summary, but it happened before retry
```

Risk:

```text
model trusts stale verification
```

Detection:

```text
timeline and freshness validation
```

Remediation:

```text
include timestamps or stage transition ordering
```

### Loss type 7: tool-pair loss

Definition:

```text
tool call and tool result relationship is broken
```

Example:

```text
result remains but call id is omitted
```

Risk:

```text
renderer creates invalid provider message sequence or model misunderstands result source
```

Detection:

```text
tool call/result pairing invariant
```

Remediation:

```text
preserve pair or summarize both as a validated artifact
```

### Loss type 8: failure-state loss

Definition:

```text
failure becomes ambiguous or disappears
```

Example:

```text
command failed
becomes
command was run
```

Risk:

```text
model proceeds as if gate passed
```

Detection:

```text
tool result status must-keep check
```

Remediation:

```text
preserve pass/fail and exit code
```

### Loss type 9: tenant-scope loss

Definition:

```text
tenant, org, app, or environment scope disappears
```

Example:

```text
org-a verification failed
becomes
verification failed
```

Risk:

```text
cross-org actions or misleading report
```

Detection:

```text
tenant scope validation
```

Remediation:

```text
restore scope fields or split projection by tenant
```

### Loss type 10: tenant blending

Definition:

```text
facts from two tenant scopes are merged into one claim
```

Example:

```text
org-a app id with org-b row count
```

Risk:

```text
wrong production target
```

Detection:

```text
source link tenant compatibility check
```

Remediation:

```text
block and rebuild with tenant filters
```

### Loss type 11: redaction loss

Definition:

```text
redaction state is not preserved or secret content appears in summary
```

Example:

```text
admin token enters compacted artifact
```

Risk:

```text
secret leak to provider or report
```

Detection:

```text
redaction state validation and secret detector
```

Remediation:

```text
block, redact before summary, regenerate artifact
```

### Loss type 12: artifact identity loss

Definition:

```text
summary mentions an artifact but loses its stable reference
```

Example:

```text
the migration report
without path, id, hash, or source link
```

Risk:

```text
operator cannot inspect evidence
```

Detection:

```text
artifact identity required-field check
```

Remediation:

```text
include artifact id, hash, or absolute path when safe
```

### Loss type 13: actionability loss

Definition:

```text
summary preserves facts but drops next required action
```

Example:

```text
dry-run failed due to missing field
but required schema remediation is omitted
```

Risk:

```text
agent loops without clear next gate
```

Detection:

```text
stage-specific next-action coverage
```

Remediation:

```text
restore required action from stage policy or source packet
```

### Loss type 14: policy scope loss

Definition:

```text
policy remains but loses where it applies
```

Example:

```text
branch creation requires explicit request
becomes
avoid branches
```

Risk:

```text
operator or agent misapplies governance
```

Detection:

```text
policy scope validation
```

Remediation:

```text
preserve condition and scope
```

### Loss type 15: traceability loss

Definition:

```text
summary is substantively accurate but lacks source links
```

Example:

```text
test passed
without command source
```

Risk:

```text
audit cannot prove claim
```

Detection:

```text
claim citation coverage
```

Remediation:

```text
attach source ids or mark claim unverified
```

### Loss-to-validator mapping

Mapping:

```text
deletion loss -> required claim recall
specificity loss -> specificity dimension check
confidence inflation -> confidence marker check
authority dilution -> source authority split
authority promotion -> renderer authority invariant
temporal inversion -> freshness/timeline check
tool-pair loss -> tool pairing invariant
failure-state loss -> result status check
tenant-scope loss -> tenant required fields
tenant blending -> tenant compatibility check
redaction loss -> redaction validation
artifact identity loss -> artifact required fields
actionability loss -> stage next-action check
policy scope loss -> policy scope check
traceability loss -> source-link coverage
```

### Recommendation

Use this taxonomy to classify validation failures.

Reason:

```text
operators need precise loss reports, not a generic "summary invalid" message
```

## Compaction incident response playbook

Status: design proposal.

Even with strong validation, a compacted artifact may later be found wrong, stale, incomplete, or unsafe.

Ekairos should define how to respond.

### Incident definition

A compaction incident occurs when:

```text
accepted compaction artifact contains false material claim
accepted compaction artifact omits required active claim
accepted compaction artifact includes secret or sensitive raw value
accepted compaction artifact crosses tenant scope
accepted compaction artifact promotes lower-authority source
provider dispatch used a stale or superseded projection
operator report relied on invalid summary
```

### Severity levels

Severity 1:

```text
secret exposure
cross-tenant exposure
production mutation influenced by invalid compaction
```

Severity 2:

```text
approval state misrepresented
failed migration gate summarized as passed
wrong tenant/app/environment in model-visible context
```

Severity 3:

```text
important but non-mutating code fact wrong
external source confidence inflated
operator report incomplete but no action taken
```

Severity 4:

```text
background chronology imprecise
non-operational source catalog omission
```

### Immediate response

For Severity 1 or 2:

```text
mark projection invalid
mark compaction artifact invalid
block context continuation
preserve raw evidence
notify operator
identify downstream provider requests
identify event parts written after invalid projection
```

For Severity 3:

```text
mark artifact suspect
rebuild projection before next provider call
add report warning
```

For Severity 4:

```text
record correction
refresh summary when next projection rebuild happens
```

### Invalid artifact record

Invalidation should record:

```text
artifactId
projectionId
invalidatedAt
invalidatedBy
severity
reason
affectedClaimIds
affectedSourceIds
affectedProviderRequestIds
recommendedAction
```

Allowed statuses:

```text
suspect
invalid
replaced
archived_invalid
```

### Trace events

Recommended trace events:

```text
context.compaction.incident_detected
context.compaction.invalidated
context.projection.invalidated
context.projection.rebuilt_after_incident
context.compaction.incident_resolved
```

Required fields:

```text
incidentId
projectionId
artifactId
severity
failureCodes
affectedClaims
affectedSources
affectedProviderRequests
```

### Source impact analysis

When an artifact is invalidated, query:

```text
which claims used the artifact?
which provider calls used the projection?
which event parts were produced after those provider calls?
which operator reports cited the artifact?
which downstream migration stages were influenced?
```

This requires:

```text
projection id on provider dispatch
compaction artifact id on projection segments
claim ids in operator reports
source links from claims to raw parts
```

### Rebuild procedure

Rebuild steps:

```text
1. Load raw event history.
2. Exclude invalid artifact as source for active claims.
3. Rehydrate root sources for affected claims.
4. Apply latest user/project instructions.
5. Re-run projection classification.
6. Regenerate compaction artifact if needed.
7. Validate claim ledger.
8. Emit replacement report.
```

Replacement report should say:

```text
which artifact was invalidated
why it was invalidated
which claims changed
which sources now support the replacement
whether downstream actions were affected
```

### Provider request impact

If invalid projection reached a provider:

```text
record provider request id when available
record rendered input hash
record assistant output ids written after dispatch
mark affected model outputs for review
```

Do not:

```text
silently delete model outputs
rewrite event history
pretend the bad projection never happened
```

Instead:

```text
append correction traces and operator reports
```

### Migration incident handling

If a migration action was influenced:

```text
stop further automatic steps
identify org/app/environment
identify approval state
identify transaction batches
identify verification status
prepare technical-leader report
```

If mutation occurred:

```text
do not infer rollback path
document current state
request explicit technical-leader instruction
```

### Secret incident handling

If secret leaked into compacted artifact or provider input:

```text
mark artifact invalid
mark affected rendered input invalid
identify provider request
record secret class without repeating value
follow project security process
rotate credential only when instructed by responsible owner
```

Projection response:

```text
redact source
rebuild summary from redacted source
add redaction failure fixture
```

### Incident tests

Fixture IR1: invalidated summary claim.

```text
accepted artifact says tests passed
later audit finds command failed
expected: artifact invalid, projection invalid, replacement required
```

Fixture IR2: provider output after invalid projection.

```text
assistant event created from bad projection
expected: output marked review_required through trace/report, not deleted
```

Fixture IR3: secret in summary.

```text
compaction artifact contains credential value
expected: severity 1 incident and artifact invalid
```

Fixture IR4: tenant blend.

```text
summary blends org-a and org-b facts
expected: severity 1 or 2 depending action impact
```

Fixture IR5: background-only inaccuracy.

```text
old non-operational chronology imprecise
expected: severity 4 correction on next rebuild
```

### Recommendation

Add incident response semantics before production compaction.

Reason:

```text
audit-grade systems need a way to invalidate and replace bad derived artifacts without destroying raw history
```

## Static review rules for future implementation

Status: proposal only.

Runtime tests are necessary, but static review rules can catch entire classes of unsafe implementation before tests run.

These rules should be applied manually during review unless the technical leader approves automated linting.

### Rule S1: no reactor-side source selection

Rejected code shape:

```text
reactor loads raw events and chooses what to drop or summarize
```

Expected shape:

```text
reactor receives accepted projection or rendered provider input
```

Review check:

```text
search reactors for direct old-history truncation, summarization, or filtering
```

### Rule S2: no raw event_parts mutation for compaction

Rejected code shape:

```text
compaction updates or deletes raw event_parts
```

Expected shape:

```text
compaction creates projection/summary/trace records that point to raw parts
```

Review check:

```text
store writes to event_parts should remain normal event persistence, not compaction replacement
```

### Rule S3: no provider-native compact path without local companion artifact

Rejected code shape:

```text
provider compact endpoint called and provider result used as only context record
```

Expected shape:

```text
local projection manifest and claim ledger exist before provider-native compaction is used
```

Review check:

```text
provider compact adapter code must require projectionId and local validation status
```

### Rule S4: no hidden budget fallback

Rejected code shape:

```text
if prompt too long, slice messages and retry
```

Expected shape:

```text
budget failure creates blocked projection or approved smaller projection path
```

Review check:

```text
search for array slicing or token-limit retry around model message lists
```

### Rule S5: no summary without source ids

Rejected code shape:

```text
summary string is accepted without claim ledger or source links
```

Expected shape:

```text
compaction artifact includes validation status and source ids
```

Review check:

```text
summary creation code returns structured artifact, not bare string
```

### Rule S6: no memory as authority

Rejected code shape:

```text
memory record inserted into instruction channel or used as approval
```

Expected shape:

```text
memory has lower authority and cannot approve protected actions
```

Review check:

```text
memory projection code must include authority class and expiration
```

### Rule S7: no retrieval without source scope

Rejected code shape:

```text
retrieval query runs without tenant/source scope for tenant data
```

Expected shape:

```text
retrieval query includes source scope, tenant scope, and authority class
```

Review check:

```text
retrieval provider interface requires scope fields
```

### Rule S8: no tool schema omission without report

Rejected code shape:

```text
tool is omitted from model call but omission is not recorded
```

Expected shape:

```text
toolNamesIncluded and toolNamesOmitted are recorded in projection manifest
```

Review check:

```text
tool profile selector emits included/omitted lists and reason
```

### Rule S9: no renderer bypass

Rejected code shape:

```text
provider call receives messages built directly from store after projection layer exists
```

Expected shape:

```text
provider call receives renderer output tied to accepted projection
```

Review check:

```text
AI SDK streamText call should trace projectionId and renderedInputHash after contract break
```

### Rule S10: no blocked state collapse

Rejected code shape:

```text
blocked projection returns generic failed execution without projection reason
```

Expected shape:

```text
blocked projection has explicit block class, failure codes, and operator report
```

Review check:

```text
blocked path includes trace event and report id
```

### Rule S11: no secret-bearing preview

Rejected code shape:

```text
rendered preview or operator report includes raw secret value
```

Expected shape:

```text
preview uses redacted content, hashes, or metadata-only state
```

Review check:

```text
preview/report code uses redaction state before serializing content
```

### Rule S12: no claim confidence upgrade

Rejected code shape:

```text
summary generation drops lower-confidence or requires-recheck caveat
```

Expected shape:

```text
claim ledger preserves confidence and recheck state
```

Review check:

```text
external source claims include confidence label and fetched date
```

### Rule S13: no migration stage ignorance

Rejected code shape:

```text
selector treats migration dry-run, execution, and report stages the same
```

Expected shape:

```text
selector receives migration stage or stage policy input
```

Review check:

```text
tests cover stage-specific required claims
```

### Rule S14: no stale projection reuse

Rejected code shape:

```text
accepted projection reused after cited source changes
```

Expected shape:

```text
projection reuse checks source hashes, tool schemas, active intent, and model profile
```

Review check:

```text
projection cache key includes invalidation metadata
```

### Rule S15: no unreported public contract break

Rejected code shape:

```text
reactor params, schema, trace payloads, or exports change without migration notes
```

Expected shape:

```text
breaking change report names affected entrypoints and validation commands
```

Review check:

```text
PR includes consumer contract section when public exports or behavior change
```

### Static review report format

Report:

```text
Static compaction review

Rules checked:
- S1 no reactor-side source selection
- S2 no raw event_parts mutation
- S3 no provider-native compact path without local companion artifact

Findings:
- none or list with file anchors

Residual risk:
- tests not run
- provider path not validated
```

### Recommendation

Use static review rules in addition to unit, integration, and real-provider tests.

Reason:

```text
unsafe compaction often appears as misplaced responsibility, which static review can catch early
```

## Operator UI state inventory

Status: proposal only.

A future UI should make context projection visible without turning the product into a debug console.

The key is to expose the right state at the right level.

### UI principle

Operator-facing UI should answer:

```text
what context was sent?
what was compacted?
what was omitted?
why was projection blocked?
what sources prove the summary?
what approval is needed?
what changed since the last projection?
```

It should not require operators to read raw trace JSON for normal review.

### State: preparing context

Display when:

```text
projection lifecycle is created, source_collected, classified, or budgeted
```

Data needed:

```text
contextId
projectionId
currentStage
sourceCount
estimatedTokens
toolCount
```

Operator action:

```text
none
```

### State: raw context fits

Display when:

```text
projection decision is raw_fits
```

Data needed:

```text
projectionId
budgetLedger
headroomTokens
recentWindowSize
toolProfile
```

Operator action:

```text
optional inspect context
```

### State: context compacted

Display when:

```text
compaction artifact accepted
```

Data needed:

```text
projectionId
compactionArtifactId
claimLedgerId
rawTokensBefore
tokensAfter
sourceLinkCount
claimCount
warningCount
```

Operator action:

```text
inspect summary
inspect sources
continue
```

### State: context blocked


```text
projectionId
blockClass
failureCodes
blockedClaims

sourceIds
operatorReportId
```

Operator actions:

```text
view blocked report
choose smaller tool profile
split task
provide missing approval
```

### State: source stale

```text
projection or claim source is stale, possibly stale, or superseded
```

```text
sourceId

```

```text
request technical-leader review
```

### Source-link inspector

Purpose:


Data needed:

```text
claimText

validationResult

rootSourceIds
authorityClass

redactionState
```

Display shape:

```text

source list

redaction labels
```

### Budget ledger panel

Purpose:

```text
show why projection compacted, reduced tools, retrieved, or blocked
```

Data needed:

```text
compactionArtifactTokens
```

```text
show which tools were included or omitted
```

Data needed:

### Redaction panel

Purpose:

### UI no-go states

Do not:

```text

hide blocked claims behind generic error
show raw secrets in previews

```

### Recommendation

Design future UI around projection state, not just chat messages.

Reason:

```text
operators need to inspect context decisions when migration safety depends on them
```

## Task splitting and re-entry protocol

Status: design proposal.

Some contexts cannot safely fit, even after compaction.

When that happens, Ekairos should split the task or ask the operator to narrow scope instead of forcing a lossy projection.

### Split triggers

Task split should be considered when:

```text
protected material exceeds budget
tenant-scoped material spans too many organizations
tool surface required for stage is too large
output reserve needed for final report is too large
claim ledger validation keeps failing due to source conflicts
operator asks for multiple independent deliverables in one turn
```

Task split should not be used to bypass:

```text
approval gates
redaction requirements
tenant scope checks
schema dry-run requirements
verification gates
```

### Split types

By tenant:

```text
one projection per org/app/environment
```

By migration stage:

```text
planning
dry-run
extraction
transformation
approval
execution
verification
report
```

By artifact class:

```text
source research
schema evidence
dataset evidence
transaction plan
verification report
```

By tool profile:

```text
read-only planning
dry-run
report-only
mutation after approval
```

By deliverable:

```text
research report
approval packet
test plan
implementation slice
```

### Split decision record

Projection should record:

```text
splitId
parentProjectionId
splitReason
splitType
childProjectionIds
sourcePartitionRule
tenantScope
stageScope
operatorInstruction
```

### Parent projection behavior

The parent projection should:

```text
record why it could not continue as one prompt
record split plan
block direct provider dispatch
create or request child projections
```

The parent projection should not:

```text
summarize protected material to force fit
drop tenant scope
hide split decision
```

### Child projection behavior

Each child projection should:

```text
inherit current user intent
inherit project instructions
inherit approval state
inherit relevant source links
apply narrower scope
emit its own budget ledger
emit its own operator report
```

Child projections should not:

```text
lose parent constraints
infer approval from sibling projection
mix tenant data from siblings
```

### Re-entry summary

After child projections complete, the parent can receive a re-entry summary.

Re-entry summary must include:

```text
childProjectionIds
childStatuses
acceptedClaims
blockedClaims
artifactReferences
tenantScopes
stageScopes
remainingOpenQuestions
```

Re-entry summary must not:

```text
turn blocked child into accepted parent claim
drop failed child status
merge tenant-scoped facts without explicit comparison
```

### Example: split by organization

Parent context:

```text
five production organizations
large dataset extraction for each
protected org matrices exceed budget
```

Decision:

```text
split by org
```

Child projections:

```text
org-a extraction and verification
org-b extraction and verification
org-c extraction and verification
org-d extraction and verification
org-e extraction and verification
```

Parent re-entry:

```text
org-a passed
org-b blocked due to row count mismatch
org-c passed
org-d passed
org-e blocked due to missing admin runtime
```

Parent result:

```text
final report says partial completion, not full success
```

### Example: split by stage

Parent context:

```text
operator asks for research, schema plan, migration execution, and final report
```

Decision:

```text
split by stage
```

Allowed sequence:

```text
research and schema plan
dry-run
approval
execution
verification
final report
```

Blocked sequence:

```text
execution before approval
final report before verification
```

### Re-entry validation

Before parent re-entry is accepted:

```text
all child claims have source links
blocked child statuses are preserved
tenant scopes remain separate
stage sequence is valid
approval state is current
```

Failure codes:

```text
child_projection_missing
child_blocked_omitted
tenant_merge_invalid
stage_sequence_invalid
approval_state_stale
```

### Operator report

Split report:

```text
Projection split required.

Reason:
- protected material exceeds budget

Split type:
- tenant

Children:
- org-a: pending
- org-b: pending

Required action:
- run child projections or narrow scope
```

Re-entry report:

```text
Split re-entry completed.

Children:
- org-a: accepted
- org-b: blocked

Parent status:
- blocked until org-b remediation
```

### Recommendation

Make splitting an explicit projection outcome.

Reason:

```text
splitting is safer than summarizing protected context beyond recognition
```

## Updated synthesis checkpoint at 10k seconds

Status: active checkpoint, not final.

This checkpoint summarizes the research state after the artifact passed roughly 10,000 seconds of active goal time.

The five-hour gate remains incomplete.

### Current synthesis

The design has converged further from:

```text
context compaction as summarization
```

to:

```text
context compaction as a projection, validation, rendering, and audit subsystem
```

The strongest target design is now:

```text
raw event history
source packet normalization
visibility and authority classification
budget ledger
stage-aware selector
optional compaction artifact
claim ledger validation
rendered provider input
provider dispatch
usage calibration
operator report
staleness and incident handling
```

### Why the design became broader

The added detail is not ornament.

Each broadening came from a concrete failure mode:

```text
tool schemas consume prompt budget
summaries can lack source proof
recursive summaries drift
rendered provider input can exceed abstract estimates
provider usage can calibrate future estimates
migration stages preserve different facts
external source claims have different reliability
local file references can become stale
bad summaries need invalidation
operators need visible blocked states
some tasks must split rather than compact
```

### Minimal safe implementation shape

The minimal safe implementation remains smaller than the target design.

First approved slice should still be:

```text
source packet contracts
projection segment contracts
budget ledger contracts
blocked projection result
pure selector tests
no schema change
no provider-native compaction
no reactor contract break until separately approved
```

Reason:

```text
the first slice should prove classification and budget behavior before adding persistence, provider adapters, or runtime behavior changes
```

### Strongest target architecture

Target architecture after approvals:

```text
first-class projection records
first-class source links
first-class compaction artifacts
claim ledger validation
projection lifecycle state machine
provider renderer contract
usage calibration records
migration-stage selector
operator report surface
incident invalidation path
```

### Highest-value design choices

Highest value:

```text
immutable raw event_parts
projection manifest before model call
claim ledger as acceptance gate
rendered budget gate before dispatch
blocked projection as explicit state
source packet visibility policy
stale-source invalidation
tool surface budgeting
```

### Highest-risk design choices

Highest risk:

```text
reactor contract break
schema/domain expansion
provider-native compaction adapter
UI/report surface expansion
downstream package release and beta validation
```

These require explicit technical-leader approval.

### Current artifact quality state

Current qualities:

```text
Markdown-only
no code changes
no schema changes
no config changes
no branch created
no push attempted
artifact remains untracked
local file references remediated to @C:\... form where audited
placeholder and ASCII scans clean
```

### Remaining productive work while gate remains open

Useful next additions:

```text
manual reviewer worksheet
projection benchmark fixture table
provider adapter acceptance checklist
release notes draft for future beta
source catalog confidence table
final audit packet after time gate reaches 18000 seconds
```

### Checkpoint conclusion

The research is already implementation-ready as a proposal packet, but the explicit time gate remains active.

Therefore:

```text
do not mark the goal complete
continue iterating until the goal timer reaches at least 18000 seconds
```

## Manual reviewer worksheet

Status: proposal only.

This worksheet is for a technical leader or reviewer evaluating a future implementation proposal.

It is not an approval by itself.

### Review part 1: scope

Questions:

```text
Is the proposal docs-only, contract-only, runtime behavior, schema/domain, provider adapter, UI, or release work?
Is the proposal explicitly breaking or non-breaking?
Does the proposal name explicit non-scope?
Does it avoid code/config/schema/provider/infra work without approval?
```

Reviewer notes:

```text
scope accepted:
scope rejected:
missing scope:
```

### Review part 2: architecture boundary

Questions:

```text
Where does projection run?
Where does compaction run?
Where does validation run?
Where does provider rendering run?
Where is raw event history preserved?
```

Required answer:

```text
raw event_parts remain canonical
projection happens before provider dispatch
renderer happens after accepted projection
reactor does not privately select old context
```

### Review part 3: source packets

Questions:

```text
Does every source packet have sourceKind, authorityClass, visibilityMode, redactionState, and tenantScope?
Does each local file source have an absolute @C:\... anchor when referenced?
Does each command source record exit code and result?
Does each external source record date checked?
```

Block if:

```text
source material cannot be traced
tenant scope missing for tenant data
redaction state unknown for sensitive source
```

### Review part 4: budget ledger

Questions:

```text
Does budget include system, messages, tools, provider overhead, output reserve, and safety margin?
Is tool schema cost visible?
Is rendered budget checked after provider formatting?
What happens when protected material exceeds budget?
```

Acceptable outcomes:

```text
raw_fits
compact_old_history
reduce_tool_surface
retrieve_instead_of_inline
block
split_task
```

### Review part 5: claim ledger

Questions:

```text
Does every material summary claim have source ids?
Are required active claims preserved?
Are source authority and freshness validated?
Are tenant boundaries checked?
Are redaction states checked?
```

Block if:

```text
summary is accepted without claim ledger
approval is inferred
failed tool result is summarized as success
```

### Review part 6: lifecycle

Questions:

```text
Does projection have explicit statuses?
Can projection be blocked?
Can projection be superseded by user correction?
Can stale projections be invalidated?
Can incidents be recorded?
```

Required statuses:

```text
accepted
rendered
dispatched
completed
blocked
superseded
invalid
```

### Review part 7: migration stage

Questions:

```text
What migration stage is active?
Which facts are must-keep for that stage?
What blocks stage transition?
What operator report is emitted?
```

Block if:

```text
execution is planned without approval
final report is produced without verification or blocked status
dry-run failure is omitted
```

### Review part 8: provider strategy

Questions:

```text
Is this provider-neutral or provider-specific?
If provider-specific, were official docs rechecked?
Is provider-native compaction optional or canonical?
Is a local companion artifact required?
```

Block if:

```text
provider-native state is the only audit source
provider compact feature is used without rechecking current docs
rendered budget is skipped
```

### Review part 9: tests

Questions:

```text
Which existing tests are preserved?
Which new projection tests are added?
Are red-team fixtures included?
Are migration-stage fixtures included?
Are path-format and artifact audits included for docs?
```

Minimum for first slice:

```text
typecheck
typecheck:tests
test
projection segment fixtures
budget fixtures
blocked projection fixtures
```

### Review part 10: reports and UX

Questions:

```text
Can the operator see why context compacted?
Can the operator see why projection blocked?
Can the operator inspect source links?
Are secrets redacted in previews?
Is tool omission visible?
```

Block if:

```text
operator only sees generic error
operator cannot inspect source coverage
model-visible summary has no report
```

### Review part 11: release and downstream

Questions:

```text
Does proposal affect public package exports?
Does it affect reactor params?
Does it affect schema/domain?
Does it affect @C:\ek or downstream apps?
Is beta validation required?
```

Block if:

```text
public contract break lacks migration notes
schema/domain change lacks migration plan
release/push/branch work lacks explicit instruction
```

### Reviewer decision form

Decision:

```text
approved
approved with narrower scope
rejected
needs more research
```

Required comments:

```text
approved scope:
explicit non-scope:
required validation:
expiration/supersession condition:
```

### Worksheet recommendation

Use this worksheet before approving implementation.

Reason:

```text
the design spans context selection, validation, rendering, storage, UX, testing, and release surfaces
```

## Provider adapter acceptance checklist

Status: proposal only.

Provider-native compaction or provider-specific rendering should not be accepted because a provider feature exists.

It should be accepted only when the adapter satisfies Ekairos audit and safety requirements.

### Adapter identity

Required fields:

```text
provider
modelFamily
adapterName
adapterVersion
officialDocsUrl
docsCheckedAt
capabilityRecord
```

Review question:

```text
which provider and model family does this adapter actually cover?
```

### Capability declaration

Adapter must declare:

```text
supportsSystemRole
supportsToolCalls
supportsToolResults
supportsFileParts
supportsImageParts
supportsPromptCaching
supportsProviderNativeCompaction
supportsUsageMetrics
supportsRequestIds
contextWindowTokens
maxOutputTokens
```

Block if:

```text
capabilities are inferred but not checked against current official docs or observed API behavior
```

### Projection compatibility

Adapter must accept:

```text
acceptedProjectionId
renderedInputHash
message list
tool schema set
budget ledger
visibility decisions
```

Adapter must not accept:

```text
raw event history as its only input
unvalidated summary string
provider-native compacted state without local projection
```

### Provider-native compaction requirements

If provider-native compaction is used, required:

```text
local projection manifest exists
local claim ledger accepted
provider compact request is traceable
provider compact response id or metadata stored when available
pre-compact rendered hash stored
post-compact provider metadata stored
usage before/after stored when available
```

Block if:

```text
provider-native compacted state becomes canonical source
local source links are skipped
claim ledger is skipped
```

### Rendering requirements

Adapter renderer must preserve:

```text
role hierarchy
current user intent
tool call/result pairing
failed tool state
file/image identity
source id labels where required
redaction state
```

Block if:

```text
system instructions are downgraded without warning
summary is promoted to system instruction
tool failure becomes assistant prose success
```

### Budget requirements

Adapter must compute:

```text
rendered message token estimate
tool schema token estimate
provider overhead estimate
output reserve
safety margin
headroom
```

Adapter must block when:

```text
rendered budget exceeds model profile
model budget unknown
tool schema estimate missing for tool-heavy call
```

### Usage telemetry requirements

Adapter should capture when provider returns:

```text
prompt tokens
completion tokens
total tokens
cached prompt tokens
request id
finish reason
context overflow errors
```

Usage record should link to:

```text
projectionId
renderedInputHash
provider
model
adapterVersion
```

### Error mapping

Adapter should map provider errors into Ekairos failure codes.

Examples:

```text
context overflow -> provider_context_overflow
invalid tool schema -> provider_tool_schema_invalid
invalid message order -> provider_message_order_invalid
rate limit -> provider_rate_limited
auth failure -> provider_auth_failed
unknown model -> provider_model_unknown
```

Adapter should not:

```text
retry by silently dropping messages
retry by dropping tools without projection update
hide provider error behind generic failure
```

### Security requirements

Adapter must prove:

```text
redacted preview only
no raw credentials in provider input
tenant scope is preserved
provider request logging does not store secrets
operator report does not reproduce sensitive content
```

Block if:

```text
adapter serializes raw secrets into trace, logs, preview, or provider metadata
```

### Tests required

Unit tests:

```text
role rendering
tool pair rendering
budget calculation
provider error mapping
redaction handling
```

Integration tests:

```text
accepted projection dispatch
blocked rendered budget
usage telemetry capture
tool schema omission report
```

Real-provider tests when explicitly approved:

```text
small request
tool call request
usage fields
provider-native compaction path if used
context overflow handling if safe to simulate
```

### Acceptance report

Adapter acceptance report should include:

```text
provider and model family
official docs checked date
capability record
rendering invariants tested
budget behavior tested
usage telemetry observed
provider-native compaction status
known gaps
approval decision
```

### Recommendation

Treat provider adapters as reviewable, auditable boundary components.

Reason:

```text
provider-specific behavior is useful only when it preserves Ekairos projection and audit guarantees
```

## Future beta release notes structure

Status: proposal only.

This section defines the release-note shape for a future approved beta that changes `@ekairos/events` compaction behavior.

No release is approved by this document.

### Release note title

Template:

```text
@ekairos/events beta: projection-ledger context compaction
```

Alternative titles by slice:

```text
@ekairos/events beta: projection contracts
@ekairos/events beta: blocked projection lifecycle
@ekairos/events beta: provider-rendered projection input
@ekairos/events beta: first-class projection schema
```

### Summary

Template:

```text
This beta introduces projection-aware context handling for @ekairos/events. The package now models model-facing context as a projection derived from durable event history, with budget decisions, source classification, and audit reports.
```

Must state:

```text
what changed
what did not change
whether behavior is breaking
which entrypoints are affected
which validation commands passed
```

### Breaking changes

Template:

```text
Breaking changes:

- Reactor params changed to include projection metadata.
- Blocked projection can stop provider dispatch before reactor execution.
- Trace payloads include projection and budget fields.
```

Required for each breaking change:

```text
old behavior
new behavior
affected entrypoint
migration action
test coverage
```

### Public entrypoints affected

List:

```text
@ekairos/events
@ekairos/events/reactor
@ekairos/events/runtime
@ekairos/events/react
@ekairos/events/instant
@ekairos/events/schema
@ekairos/events/domain
@ekairos/events/codex
```

For each affected entrypoint:

```text
added exports
changed exports
removed exports
behavior change
consumer action
```

### Migration guide

Template:

```text
If you implement a custom reactor:

1. Read projection metadata from reactor params.
2. Do not rebuild model messages directly from raw event items.
3. Preserve blocked projection behavior.
4. Preserve tool approval metadata.
```

Schema migration guide should include:

```text
new entities
new links
dry-run plan
data migration requirements
rollback or disablement plan
```

### Validation report

Release notes should list:

```text
typecheck command
typecheck:tests command
test command
workflow tests
scripted reactor tests
AI SDK reactor tests
real provider tests if approved
schema dry-run if schema changed
downstream smoke if performed
```

Each command entry should include:

```text
command
environment
pass/fail
timestamp
important caveats
```

### Compaction behavior section

Required:

```text
projection trigger
budget behavior
blocked behavior
source-link behavior
tool surface behavior
provider-native behavior
operator report behavior
```

Example:

```text
When protected context exceeds the configured model budget, @ekairos/events returns blocked projection state instead of silently truncating raw history.
```

### Security section

Required:

```text
redaction behavior
tenant-scope behavior
secret preview behavior
provider logging caveats
incident response path
```

Must state:

```text
raw credentials are never model-visible
tenant-scoped retrieval requires tenant filters
```

### Observability section

Required:

```text
new trace events
new trace fields
usage calibration fields
operator reports
budget ledger fields
```

Example trace fields:

```text
projectionId

claimLedgerId
renderedInputHash
inputTokenEstimate
toolSchemaTokenEstimate
failureCodes
```

### Known gaps

Release notes should be explicit:

```text
provider-native compaction not included
auto-memory not included
schema entities not included
UI source-link inspector not included
real provider smoke not run
```

Known gaps should not be hidden as roadmap marketing.

They are operational caveats.

### Downstream validation

If downstream validation is performed:

```text
downstream app
package version
scenario
credentials policy
review link
pass/fail
known data seeded
```

If not performed:

```text
downstream validation not performed
reason
required next step
```

### Release note no-go

Do not publish release notes that:

```text
say compaction is safe without validation evidence
omit breaking reactor contract changes
omit schema/domain changes
omit blocked projection behavior
omit known provider-native gaps
claim real-provider validation when only unit tests ran
```

### Recommendation

Prepare release notes as part of implementation review, not after merge.

Reason:

```text
compaction changes affect downstream contracts and operator expectations
```

## Implementation slice dependency graph

Status: proposal only.

This section converts the research into a dependency graph that a technical leader can approve, split, reject, or reorder.

It is not an authorization to implement.

The graph keeps orchestration code, schema work, provider work, UI work, package release work, and downstream validation separate.

Reason:

```text
context compaction crosses model input policy, durable audit, provider adapters, tests, and release contracts
```

Treating those as one change would hide decision boundaries.

### Graph principles

The implementation graph should satisfy five principles:

```text
every slice has one approval owner
every slice has a measurable output
every slice can fail without requiring unrelated rollback
every slice states whether schema/config/provider/release work is involved
every slice names the exact evidence needed before the next slice starts
```

These principles are more important than the exact slice count.

They protect the package from accidental broad refactors.
