### Dependency graph in text form

Graph:

```text
slice zero decision record
  -> slice one projection vocabulary and contracts
      -> slice two source packet extractor
          -> slice three budget ledger
              -> slice four projection decision engine
                  -> slice five renderer to model messages
                      -> slice six trace-only projection reports
                          -> slice seven manual summary artifact
                              -> slice eight durable projection schema
                                  -> slice nine provider adapter integration
                                      -> slice ten operator report and UX contract
                                          -> slice eleven downstream package release
                                              -> slice twelve downstream product validation
```

Parallelizable after approval:

```text
slice one can prepare contract fixtures while slice zero ADR text is reviewed
slice three budget profiles can be drafted while slice two extractor tests are built
slice ten report fixtures can be drafted after slice six trace payloads are accepted
release notes can be drafted before slice eleven but not published
```

Non-parallelizable gates:

```text
provider adapter integration depends on rendered projection input
durable schema depends on accepted data model
auto compaction depends on manual summary validation
downstream product validation depends on released package version
```

### Minimal first implementation path

If the technical leader wants the smallest useful implementation:

```text
slice zero
slice one
slice two
slice three
slice four
slice five
slice six
```

Behavior delivered:

```text
projection can be planned
model input can be rendered from a projection
unsafe projection can be blocked
trace/report artifacts can explain the decision
no durable projection schema
no automatic summary generation
no provider-native compaction
```

Why this is useful:

```text
the package gains policy and observability before it gains summarization
```

What it does not solve:

```text
very long sessions still require either manual summary or reference-only behavior
queryable projection history remains limited
downstream UI cannot deeply inspect persisted projection entities
```

### Full audit-grade path

If the technical leader wants the target architecture:

```text
slice zero through slice twelve
```

Behavior delivered:

```text
projection policy
budget ledger
source packet classification
manual summary artifacts
first-class durable projection schema
provider adapter integration
operator reports
release notes
downstream product validation
```

Why this is heavier:

```text
it changes package contracts, data model, operator workflow, and downstream expectations
```

Why it may be justified:

```text
Ekairos migration work requires traceable source decisions and recoverable projection lineage
```

### Slices that must not be merged together casually

Do not combine these without explicit approval:

```text
projection contract break plus durable schema creation
manual summary generation plus auto compaction trigger
provider adapter integration plus provider-native compaction
package release plus downstream consumer update
operator UI plus report data model
```

Reason:

```text
each pair mixes policy, data, runtime, or release risk
```

### Approval packet per slice

Each slice should be presented with:

```text
slice id
business reason
files affected
schema impact
config impact
provider impact
public contract impact
test plan
rollback or disable plan
known risks
explicit out-of-scope list
```

The out-of-scope list is mandatory.

Without it, compaction work can expand into general agent redesign.

### Stop conditions

Stop before implementation if any of the following is unresolved:

```text
source authority classes are not approved
blocked projection behavior is not approved
schema persistence is ambiguous
provider-native compaction is requested without audit companion design
current user literal protection is not testable
unresolved action protection is not testable
tenant source filtering is not testable
```

Stop before release if any of the following is unresolved:

```text
release notes omit breaking behavior
tests do not cover blocked projection
source coverage report is missing
schema dry-run evidence is missing for schema work
provider adapter can dispatch after projection validation fails
downstream validation status is unknown
```

### Recommended review order

Review order:

```text
1. approve or reject projection-ledger architecture
2. approve protected source classes
3. approve blocking behavior
4. approve public contract break
5. approve whether schema persistence is in first implementation
6. approve provider-native compaction timing
7. approve release and downstream validation expectations
```

This order prevents early implementation from deciding architecture by accident.

### Summary

The graph favors a staged break:

```text
first make model input explainable
then make compaction artifacts validated
then make projection history durable
then integrate providers
then release and validate downstream
```

The most important first cut is not summarization.

The most important first cut is a projection decision engine that can say:

```text
this context can be rendered safely
this context needs explicit compaction
this context is blocked because protected source material cannot fit
```

## Projection benchmark fixture table

Status: proposal only.

This section defines benchmark fixtures for judging whether a future Ekairos context compaction implementation is actually useful.

The purpose is not to maximize compression ratio.

The purpose is to preserve task correctness, migration safety, source traceability, and operator review quality under context pressure.

### Benchmark design goals

The fixture set should cover:

```text
short contexts that should not compact
long contexts that can safely summarize old middle history
long contexts that should reference heavy artifacts instead of summarizing them
contexts that must block dispatch
contexts with secrets or tenant boundaries
contexts with migration gates and verification evidence
contexts with tool schemas consuming significant budget
contexts with provider estimate error
contexts with stale retrieved source material
contexts with current user instructions that override old plans
```

The fixture set should not reward:

```text
dropping source links
rewriting current user intent
compressing unresolved tool/action state
summarizing credentials
turning failed commands into successful claims
turning unverified schema changes into accepted facts
using provider-native compaction as the only audit artifact
```

### Required fixture fields

Each benchmark fixture should be represented as structured data with at least:

```text
fixtureId
fixtureName
sessionShape
domainScenario
tenantShape
sourcePacketCount
contextItemCount
eventPartCount
traceEventCount
toolCallCount
toolSchemaCount
estimatedInputTokens
targetModelProfile
expectedProjectionStatus
expectedProtectedSources
expectedSummarizedSources
expectedReferencedSources
expectedOmittedSources
expectedBlockedReason
expectedRenderedInputHash
expectedClaimCoverageMinimum
expectedOperatorReportSections
```

Optional fields:

```text
providerNativeArtifact
retrievalProviderShape
downstreamAppName
migrationReportShape
redactionPolicyCase
knownEstimateError
```

The exact serialized format needs approval.

The important part is that future tests compare projection behavior against named expectations.

### Measurement axes

Each fixture should be scored along these axes:

```text
literal preservation
source coverage
claim support
budget correctness
blocked-state correctness
secret handling
tenant isolation
tool continuity
migration evidence preservation
operator report clarity
provider independence
render determinism
```

Suggested score values:

```text
pass
fail
not_applicable
requires_manual_review
```

Numeric score alone is insufficient.

Context compaction errors tend to be categorical.

A projection either preserved an unresolved approval gate or it did not.

### Fixture B001: no-compaction baseline

Purpose:

```text
prove that projection code does not introduce unnecessary summarization
```

Session shape:

```text
one system/developer policy block
one short user request
two assistant turns
one small tool result
no migration gate
no secrets
input budget well below threshold
```

Expected status:

```text
render_full
```

Protected sources:

```text
current user request

latest tool result
system/developer policy
```

Expected result:

```text
no summary artifact
no omitted high-authority source
no blocked state
budget ledger emitted
source coverage complete
```

Failure examples:

```text
summary generated even though budget is sufficient
tool result converted to unsupported claim
current user request appears in nonliteral form
```

### Benchmark acceptance thresholds

Suggested first-slice threshold:

```text
all blocked-state fixtures pass
all current-user literal fixtures pass
all unresolved-action fixtures pass
all secret fixtures pass
budget ledger present for every fixture
source coverage report present for every nonblocked render
```

Suggested target threshold:

```text
all first-slice thresholds
claim coverage above approved minimum
recursive compaction lineage valid
provider-native comparison artifact recorded when applicable
operator report accepted by manual review
migration report regeneration fixture passes
```

Do not average away a safety failure.

A single secret exposure, tenant leak, or missing approval gate should fail the benchmark run.

## Provider source recheck packet

Status: proposal only.

Provider behavior, model context windows, native compaction APIs, and agent SDK conventions are unstable.

Before any implementation slice depends on provider-native behavior, the technical leader should receive a fresh source recheck packet.

This section defines that packet.

### Recheck trigger

Run a provider source recheck when any of these are true:

```text
implementation touches provider adapter behavior
implementation changes model message rendering
implementation uses provider-native compaction
implementation changes token budget profiles
implementation changes tool schema exposure
release notes mention provider support
downstream validation depends on a specific model family
more than thirty days passed since the last source check
```

For this research artifact, no provider implementation is approved.

### Required source classes

The packet should separate source classes by authority:

```text
official provider API reference
official provider guide
official provider SDK or agent guide
official source code repository
community source code repository
third-party docs
academic paper
local package source
```

Highest authority:

```text
official API reference
official provider guide
official source code for the exact project
local package source for current implementation facts
```

Lower authority:

```text
blog posts
unversioned community docs
incomplete scraped docs
secondary summaries
```

Lower authority can inspire a proposal.

Lower authority should not decide an Ekairos provider contract.

### Recheck packet fields

Each source entry should include:

```text
sourceId
providerOrProject
sourceClass
urlOrPath
retrievedAt
versionOrCommit
featureArea
claimsExtracted
claimsRejected
stabilityRisk
implementationImpact
approvalImpact
```

For local file sources, use absolute paths:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\schema.ts

### Staleness policy

Recommended policy:

```text
official provider API claims expire after thirty days
official local package source claims expire when code changes
community source claims expire after fourteen days
project-status claims expire after seven days
academic architecture claims do not expire quickly but implementation relevance must be rechecked
```

The expiry is not about truth.

It is about implementation risk.

Provider APIs can change faster than architectural principles.

### Summary

Provider source recheck should be a mandatory gate before provider-specific implementation.

The result should not be a broad literature review.

It should be a compact approval packet answering:

```text
what current source says
what changed
what Ekairos design decision it affects
what can be implemented now
what remains blocked
```

## Migration data artifact reference policy

Status: proposal only.

Migration work produces large artifacts that should usually not be copied into model context in full.

Examples:

```text
dataset extracts
admin query output
schema dry-run output
transaction plans
verification query results
per-org rollout matrices
operator reports
failed command logs
```

Context compaction for migrations must decide when to include a literal excerpt, when to include a structured summary, and when to include only a hash-backed reference.

The durable artifact remains the authority.

The model-facing projection is a controlled view.

### Core policy

Recommended policy:

```text
small high-authority evidence can be literal
large high-authority evidence should be referenced with digest and relevant excerpt
secret-bearing evidence should be redacted or not model-visible
tenant-scoped evidence should never cross tenant boundaries
failed verification evidence should remain literal enough to guide next action
operator approvals should remain literal
```

The projection builder should not treat all large outputs as summary candidates.

Some large outputs are proof artifacts.

Proof artifacts can be compressed only if their evidentiary role survives.

### Artifact classes

Proposed artifact classes:

```text
schema_plan
org_matrix
dataset_extract
transform_input
transform_output
transaction_plan
transaction_result
verification_query
verification_result
operator_approval
release_evidence
incident_evidence
```

Each class should carry:

```text
artifactId
artifactClass
tenantScope
createdAt
createdBy
sourceCommandOrQuery
contentHash
byteSize
tokenEstimate
redactionState
modelVisibility
retentionClass
summaryAllowed
referenceAllowed
literalRequired
```

These are proposed fields only.

No schema is approved by this document.

### Schema planning artifacts

Schema planning artifacts include:

```text
planSchemaPush output
schema diff
schema validation errors
index or relationship changes
generated migration notes
```

Default projection policy:

```text
include status literal
include errors literal
include changed entity names literal
include full output by reference when large
include content hash
include command metadata
```

Never reduce:

```text
failure status
entity names involved in failure
field names involved in failure
required manual decision
```

Reason:

```text
schema planning determines whether any migration can proceed
```

### Organization matrix artifacts

Organization matrix artifacts include:

```text
Clerk organization id
workspace id
app id
admin runtime resolution
per-org gate state
rollout eligibility
```

Default projection policy:

```text
include current target org literal
include gate state literal
reference full matrix if large
redact admin token values
preserve app id/admin token resolution status without raw secret
```

Protected fields:

```text
org id
app id
gate state
rollout cohort
blocked reason
```

Not model-visible:

```text
raw admin token
raw Clerk secret
raw provider credential
```

Reason:

```text
wrong org/app mapping can migrate the wrong data
```

### Dataset extract artifacts

Dataset extracts include:

```text
raw domain endpoint export
raw Instant admin query output
CSV/JSON export
record count
sample rows
tenant identifiers
source timestamps
```

Default projection policy:

```text
include metadata literal
include record counts literal
include schema shape literal
include small representative sample only if safe
reference full raw extract by hash
redact tenant-private fields unless explicitly needed
```

Required metadata:

```text
query or endpoint
tenant scope
record count
content hash
extract timestamp
redaction state
```

Do not summarize as:

```text
dataset looks correct
records migrated successfully
all rows are valid
```

Those are unsupported claims unless verified by explicit checks.

### Transformation artifacts

Transformation artifacts include:

```text
script inputs
script outputs
mapping tables
validation errors
row-level transform counts
discard lists
id remap tables
```

Default projection policy:

```text
include transform intent literal
include counts literal
include validation errors literal
reference full mapping table by hash
include small row samples only when safe
```

Protected evidence:

```text
number of input records
number of output records
number of skipped records
reason for skipped records
validation failure category
id remap strategy
```

Reason:

```text
transformation correctness is often where data loss occurs
```

### Transaction plan artifacts

Transaction plan artifacts include:

```text
idempotent transaction plan
upsert list
delete list
edge/link operations
precondition checks
dry-run transaction summary
```

Default projection policy:

```text
include operation counts literal
include destructive operations literal
include preconditions literal
reference full transaction payload by hash
include idempotency key strategy literal
```

Literal-required cases:

```text
delete operation present
merge operation present
manual approval needed
precondition failed
transaction target unknown
```

Reason:

```text
the model must not lose awareness of destructive or irreversible operations
```

### Transaction result artifacts

Transaction result artifacts include:

```text
applied transaction output
partial failure output
retry output
rollback output
affected record counts
```

Default projection policy:

```text
include status literal
include failure output literal
include affected counts literal
reference large success payload by hash
include retry state literal
```

Failure preservation:

```text
if a transaction failed, the exact failure status and diagnostic line should remain model-visible
```

Reason:

```text
retry planning depends on exact failure state
```

### Verification artifacts

Verification artifacts include:

```text
verification query
verification result
before/after counts
sample comparison
integrity check
manual review output
```

Default projection policy:

```text
include query intent literal
include pass/fail literal
include failed checks literal
include counts literal
reference full result by hash
```

Never reduce:

```text
failed check name
expected count
actual count
missing record ids when safe
duplicate record ids when safe
manual review required marker
```

Reason:

```text
verification is the gate between migration and rollout expansion
```

### Operator approval artifacts

Operator approval artifacts include:

```text
technical-leader approval
manual gate decision
release approval
rollout cohort approval
incident approval
```

Default projection policy:

```text
include approval or rejection literal
include scope literal
include timestamp literal
include approving actor literal if policy allows
include unresolved approval as protected literal
```

Never summarize unresolved approval as:

```text
approval pending but probably fine
approval likely
approved by implication
```

The projection decision engine should treat unresolved approval as a protected source.

### Release evidence artifacts

Release evidence includes:

```text
package version
commit
test run summary
publish command output
GitHub action status
npm view output
downstream update result
```

Default projection policy:

```text
include exact version literal
include command status literal
include failed release command literal
reference large CI logs by hash
include downstream validation status literal
```

This matters because release state is temporal.

The model should not act on an old version claim without evidence.

### Incident evidence artifacts

Incident evidence includes:

```text
bad projection report
source coverage gap
provider dispatch that should have blocked
secret exposure report
tenant-scope violation report
operator correction
```

Default projection policy:

```text
include incident state literal
include affected source ids literal
include mitigation state literal
reference large logs by hash
block dispatch if incident state is unresolved and relevant
```

Incident evidence should override normal summarization preferences.

### Reference packet format

When an artifact is too large for literal inclusion, render a reference packet:

```text
artifactRef
artifactClass
sourceCommandOrQuery
tenantScope
createdAt
contentHash
byteSize
tokenEstimate
recordCount
redactionState
modelVisibility
summary
relevantExcerpts
knownFailures
verificationStatus
operatorActionRequired
```

The reference packet should be concise but not vague.

Bad reference:

```text
large dataset omitted
```

Good reference:

```text
dataset extract for org X, 12,438 records, hash H, three validation failures, full extract not model-visible, relevant failed ids listed in verification artifact
```

### Hash policy

Hash policy should define:

```text
hash algorithm
hash input boundary
redaction before or after hash
hash storage location
hash display format
hash verification command
```

Approval questions:

```text
should hash be computed over raw artifact or redacted artifact
should both raw and redacted hashes exist
where should hash verification be recorded
```

Recommended direction:

```text
record raw artifact hash only in secure audit storage
record redacted/model-visible hash in projection report
state which hash each report uses
```

### Excerpt policy

Excerpts should be selected by relevance:

```text
failed rows
changed entity schema
affected ids
count mismatch
manual gate line
destructive operation line
current target org line
```

Excerpts should not be selected by:

```text
first N lines only
random sample only
largest rows
most recent rows without relevance
```

Reason:

```text
model context should contain decision-relevant evidence, not arbitrary slices
```

### Summary policy

Summaries should be allowed only when:

```text
source artifact is not secret-bearing
source artifact is not current user instruction
source artifact is not unresolved approval
source artifact is not a failed gate requiring exact diagnostics
source coverage can be recorded
claim ledger can validate retained claims
```

Summaries should include:

```text
what source was summarized
what was preserved
what was excluded
what evidence supports each retained claim
whether any failures remain
```

Summaries should not include:

```text
unsupported success claims
guessed counts
cross-tenant merged state
raw secrets
hidden approval assumptions
```

### Omission policy

Omission should be explicit.

Each omitted artifact should have:

```text
artifact id
artifact class
omission reason
authority class
tenant scope
whether a reference remains
whether omission affects safety
```

Allowed omission cases:

```text
obsolete exploratory output superseded by later verified output
low-authority duplicate source
large success log with exact counts preserved elsewhere
irrelevant old diagnostic after current user changed scope
```

Not allowed:

```text
failed verification output
unresolved approval
current target org mapping
destructive transaction plan
secret-bearing output without redaction audit
```

### Operator report requirements

Migration projection reports should show:

```text
artifact class counts
literal artifact count
reference artifact count
summary artifact count
omitted artifact count
blocked artifact count
secret-bearing artifact count
tenant scopes included
verification status
approval gate status
```

The report should answer:

```text
what evidence was visible to the model
what evidence was not visible
why not
where the durable source remains
what manual action is required
```

### Recommended first implementation scope

For a first approved implementation, this policy can be reduced to:

```text
classify artifact type
preserve current user and unresolved approvals
preserve failed verification literal
reference large dataset extracts by hash
redact secrets from model-visible projection
emit operator report
block when protected evidence cannot fit
```

Out of scope for the first slice unless separately approved:

```text
full artifact storage schema
automatic dataset hash verification
UI artifact inspector
provider-native compaction integration
downstream release automation
```

### Summary

Migration context compaction should not ask:

```text
how much can be summarized
```

It should ask:

```text
which artifacts are evidence
which evidence must remain literal
which evidence can be referenced by hash
which evidence is unsafe for model visibility
which missing evidence should block dispatch
```

This is the difference between generic chat summarization and migration-safe context projection.

## Claim ledger reviewer examples

Status: proposal only.

A claim ledger is useful only if a reviewer can read it and decide whether model-visible context is supported by durable sources.

This section gives concrete examples of good, bad, and blocked claims.

### Claim ledger purpose

The claim ledger should answer:

```text
what claim is being shown to the model
which source packets support it
which source packets contradict it
whether the claim is a fact, decision, instruction, estimate, or inference
whether the claim is current or stale
whether the claim is safe for model visibility
whether the claim is required for task continuity
```

The ledger should not be a prose summary.

It should be a reviewable table or structured object.

### Claim fields

Proposed fields:

```text
claimId
claimText
claimType
sourcePacketIds
contradictingSourcePacketIds
supportLevel
authorityClass
stalenessState
tenantScope
modelVisibility
requiredForCurrentTurn
validationStatus
reviewNotes
```

Claim types:

```text
fact
decision
instruction
open_question
estimate
inference
rejected_option
superseded_plan
failure_evidence
approval_state
```

Support levels:

```text
direct
derived
weak
contradicted
unsupported
not_model_visible
```

Validation statuses:

```text
accepted
accepted_with_caveat
rejected
blocked
manual_review_required
```

### Example C001: direct fact from local code

Claim:

```text
event_parts is the durable source for replayed context content
```

Claim type:

```text
fact
```

Supporting source:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\schema.ts:45

Expected support:

```text
direct
```

Reviewer decision:

```text
accepted
```

Why:

```text
the claim points to the local schema entity that stores event part records
```

Model-visible rendering:

```text
The durable event part table is treated as source history for projection decisions.
```

Required caveat:

```text
do not claim that event_parts is the only table involved in context replay unless local engine flow confirms it
```

### Example C002: local code plus engine flow

Claim:

```text
context expansion occurs before reactor execution
```

Claim type:

```text
fact
```

Supporting sources:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\context.engine.ts:1452

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\context.engine.ts:1497

Expected support:

```text
direct
```

Reviewer decision:

```text
accepted_with_caveat
```

Caveat:

```text
line anchors must be rechecked before implementation because local code can change
```

Model-visible rendering:

```text
The current engine flow should be reviewed around context expansion and reactor invocation before inserting projection logic.
```

### Example C003: unsupported provider inference

Claim:

```text
provider-native compaction is sufficient for Ekairos migration audit
```

Claim type:

```text
inference
```

Supporting source:

```text
none sufficient
```

Contradicting design requirement:

```text
migration workflows require source traceability and operator evidence
```

Expected support:

```text
unsupported
```

Reviewer decision:

```text
rejected
```

Reason:

```text
official provider docs can show compaction capability, but they do not prove Ekairos-specific audit sufficiency
```

Allowed replacement claim:

```text
provider-native compaction can be evaluated as an optional provider artifact if local source coverage remains authoritative
```

### Example C004: rejected option preserved as rejected

Claim:

```text
auto-memory should be part of the first implementation slice
```

Claim type:

```text
decision
```

Supporting source:

```text
none accepted
```

Contradicting source class:

```text
research recommendation separates memory from compaction
```

Expected support:

```text
contradicted
```

Reviewer decision:

```text
rejected
```

Correct model-visible rendering:

```text
Auto-memory is intentionally out of the first compaction slice unless separately approved.
```

Failure mode:

```text
summary turns a discussed future idea into an accepted task
```

### Example C005: stale provider docs

Claim:

```text
OpenAI compact endpoint request shape is current
```

Claim type:

```text
fact
```

Source:

```text
official API reference fetched during earlier research
```

Expected support:

```text
weak
```

Reviewer decision:

```text
manual_review_required
```

Reason:

```text
provider API docs can change and must be rechecked at implementation time
```

Allowed rendering:

```text
Earlier research found an OpenAI Responses compact endpoint; exact current request and response shape must be rechecked before implementation.
```

Blocked rendering:

```text
Implement the endpoint using the earlier shape without recheck.
```

### Example C006: tenant-scope fact

Claim:

```text
retrieved source belongs to the current organization
```

Claim type:

```text
fact
```

Required source fields:

```text
source org id
current org id
retrieval query scope
retrieval timestamp
```

Expected support:

```text
direct
```

Reviewer decision:

```text
accepted only if all fields match
```

Blocked if:

```text
source org id missing
current org id missing
retrieval query lacks tenant filter
source is from another org
```

Model-visible rendering:

```text
Only tenant-scoped sources for the current organization are included in the projection.
```

### Example C007: secret-bearing output

Claim:

```text
the command output contains an authentication token
```

Claim type:

```text
fact
```

Source support:

```text
direct from redaction classifier
```

Expected support:

```text
not_model_visible
```

Reviewer decision:

```text
accepted for audit, not visible to model as raw value
```

Allowed model-visible rendering:

```text
The command output contained secret-bearing material and is represented only by a redacted diagnostic reference.
```

Blocked model-visible rendering:

```text
raw token value
```

### Example C008: failed verification evidence

Claim:

```text
verification failed because expected count and actual count differ
```

Claim type:

```text
failure_evidence
```

Required source support:

```text
verification command or query
expected count
actual count
exit status or check status
timestamp
```

Expected support:

```text
direct
```

Reviewer decision:

```text
accepted
```

Literal-required elements:

```text
failed check name
expected count
actual count
```

Failure mode:

```text
summary says verification had issues but omits count mismatch
```

### Example C009: destructive operation

Claim:

```text
the transaction plan includes delete operations
```

Claim type:

```text
fact
```

Required source support:

```text
transaction plan artifact
operation count
target entity
approval state
```

Expected support:

```text
direct
```

Reviewer decision:

```text
accepted_with_caveat
```

Caveat:

```text
requires literal preservation of delete count and approval state
```

Blocked if:

```text
delete count cannot fit
approval state cannot fit
transaction plan source is missing
```

### Example C010: current user instruction

Claim:

```text
the user only wants Markdown documentation and no implementation
```

Claim type:

```text
instruction
```

Required support:

```text
current or controlling user message
```

Expected support:

```text
direct
```

Reviewer decision:

```text
accepted
```

Literal requirement:

```text
the controlling instruction should remain literal or near-literal, not only summarized
```

Failure mode:

```text
projection loses no-implementation constraint and starts code changes
```

### Example C011: inferred implementation sequence

Claim:

```text
source packet extraction should precede provider-native compaction
```

Claim type:

```text
inference
```

Supporting sources:

```text
local architecture recommendation
provider recheck packet
benchmark fixture requirements
```

Expected support:

```text
derived
```

Reviewer decision:

```text
accepted_with_caveat
```

Caveat:

```text
this is a proposal that requires technical-leader approval
```

Model-visible rendering:

```text
Proposal: implement source packet extraction before any provider-native compaction integration.
```

Blocked rendering:

```text
Provider-native compaction must be implemented after source extraction.
```

Reason:

```text
the source supports a proposal, not an approved command
```

### Example C012: source conflict

Claim:

```text
the migration gate passed
```

Claim type:

```text
fact
```

Supporting source:

```text
old assistant note
```

Contradicting source:

```text
new verification result failed
```

Expected support:

```text
contradicted
```

Reviewer decision:

```text
rejected
```

Correct rendering:

```text
An older note claimed the gate passed, but the latest verification result failed; treat the gate as failed until reviewed.
```

Failure mode:

```text
summary keeps only the older success note
```

### Reviewer workflow

Recommended workflow:

```text
read projection manifest
read claim ledger
sort claims by authority class
inspect blocked and rejected claims first
inspect current user and approval claims
inspect migration evidence claims
inspect source conflicts
inspect stale provider claims
approve or reject projection
```

The reviewer should not need to read the full raw transcript for every normal run.

The reviewer must be able to inspect raw sources when a claim is blocked, rejected, stale, or high-risk.

### Claim ledger no-go cases

Reject a projection when:

```text
claim has no source ids
claim cites source ids from another tenant
claim contradicts newer source without caveat
claim turns rejected option into accepted decision
claim hides unresolved approval
claim summarizes raw secret
claim says verification passed without evidence
claim uses stale provider docs as current implementation fact
```

### Report shape

Suggested report:

```text
totalClaims
acceptedClaims
acceptedWithCaveatClaims
rejectedClaims
blockedClaims
manualReviewClaims
unsupportedClaims
contradictedClaims
staleClaims
secretClaims
tenantScopedClaims
```

High-risk claim table:

```text
claimId
claimType
supportLevel
validationStatus
sourcePacketIds
reviewNotes
modelVisible
```

### Summary

The claim ledger is the guard against plausible but unsafe compression.

It forces every retained statement to carry an evidence status.

The key distinction:

```text
the model may see a compact projection
the operator must be able to audit why every important claim survived
```

## Downstream validation credentials and data policy

Status: proposal only.

This research does not create a branch, push code, deploy, seed data, or create credentials.

For a future approved implementation and release, context compaction should have a downstream validation packet that includes ready-to-test data and safe credentials when the platform policy allows it.

The goal is to make validation concrete without leaking secrets or overstating what was tested.

### When this policy applies

Apply this policy when:

```text
@ekairos/events compaction behavior changes
package release is planned
consumer app update is planned
Vercel preview validation is planned
mobile or web product behavior depends on context projection
manual reviewer needs seeded data
```

Do not apply it during pure research unless the technical leader asks for provisioning.

### Consumer target

Known downstream workspace from project identity:

@C:\ek

Known remote mobile target from project identity:

```text
http://192.168.1.23:3000/mobile-codex
```

Known consumer page from project identity:

@C:\ek\packages\web\src\pages\mobile-codex.tsx

Known mobile endpoint area from project identity:

@C:\ek\packages\web\src\app\api\mobile\codex

These are references only.

No consumer update is approved by this document.

### Validation packet fields

A future downstream validation packet should include:

```text
package name
package version
consumer app
consumer branch
consumer commit
deploy URL
test environment
seeded organization id
seeded workspace id
seeded project id
seeded context id
seeded scenario ids
test credential policy
manual test steps
expected compaction behavior
known limitations
cleanup instructions
```

If credentials are returned, include:

```text
login URL
test user email
test user password or one-time flow according to policy
organization visible name
role
expiry if applicable
data reset policy
```

If credentials cannot be returned, include:

```text
reason credentials are unavailable
who can provision them
exact command or workflow expected to produce them
which seeded data exists without login
```

### Credential safety rules

Credentials for manual validation should follow these rules:

```text
test-only account
least privilege role
no production admin secret
no raw provider API key
no raw Clerk secret
no raw Instant admin token
expires or can be revoked
seeded data is clearly synthetic or approved
```

Model-visible docs should not include:

```text
raw admin runtime token
raw provider key
raw service-role secret
raw cookie
raw personal account credential
```

If a validation flow requires privileged credentials, return the workflow and evidence status instead of exposing the secret.

### Seeded data requirements

Compaction validation data should include at least one normal case and one safety case.

Normal case:

```text
long but safe context
old exploratory history
current user request
retrieved domain source
successful tool result
projection report visible
model dispatch allowed
```

Safety case:

```text
protected source exceeds budget
unresolved approval or failed verification exists
projection report visible
model dispatch blocked
operator can see blocked reason
```

Migration case:

```text
org matrix
schema dry-run artifact
dataset extract reference
transform result
transaction plan
verification result
operator report
```

Secret case:

```text
tool output classified as secret-bearing
redacted model-visible projection
raw secret not shown
audit report records redaction state
```

Tenant case:

```text
two organizations with similar project names
current run scoped to one org
other org data excluded
claim ledger does not cite other tenant private sources
```

### Manual test steps

A future manual validation packet should give steps such as:

```text
open deploy URL
log in with test account
select seeded organization
open seeded project
start or resume context run
trigger normal long-context scenario
inspect projection report
confirm model dispatch occurred
trigger blocked projection scenario
inspect blocked reason
confirm model dispatch did not occur
inspect source coverage
inspect budget ledger
inspect redaction state if secret scenario is included
```

Each step should have:

```text
expected UI state
expected trace state
expected event/state record if visible
pass/fail result
notes
```

### Evidence returned to reviewer

The validation packet should include:

```text
deploy URL
credentials or provisioning status
seeded data identifiers
screenshots if requested and approved
trace ids
context ids
projection ids
test command outputs
known failures
```

For this research-only artifact, none of those runtime items exist.

### E2E workflow relationship

The workspace note says GitHub Actions e2e tests may return credentials that can inspire manual validation.

For future implementation, use that only as a controlled source:

```text
inspect action output policy
confirm credentials are test-only
confirm credentials are safe to share in the requested channel
confirm seeded data matches compaction scenario
record exact workflow run
record expiry or cleanup policy
```

Do not assume:

```text
any CI credential is safe to paste into docs
any e2e scenario validates context compaction
any successful deploy validates projection safety
```

### Validation result statuses

Use explicit statuses:

```text
not_started
provisioned
deploy_ready
credentials_ready
manual_review_ready
passed
failed
blocked
not_applicable
```

Do not use vague statuses:

```text
looks good
probably works
seems validated
ready enough
```

### Failure reporting

When downstream validation fails, report:

```text
scenario id
expected behavior
actual behavior
environment
deploy URL
context id
projection id if available
trace id if available
credential/account used
logs inspected
impact
next required approval
```

For compaction-specific failures, classify:

```text
missing projection report
wrong blocked state
dispatch occurred after blocked projection
source coverage gap
claim ledger gap
secret exposure
tenant-scope leak
budget ledger mismatch
provider artifact mismatch
operator report unclear
```

### Cleanup policy

Seeded validation data should have a cleanup plan:

```text
delete test org
disable test user
revoke test credential
remove seeded project
archive trace evidence if policy allows
keep nonsecret validation report
```

If cleanup is intentionally skipped:

```text
reason
owner
retention window
manual cleanup instruction
```

### Release packet integration

Release notes should state:

```text
downstream validation performed or not performed
deploy URL if available
credential status
seeded scenario ids
normal scenario status
blocked scenario status
secret scenario status
tenant scenario status
known gaps
```

If downstream validation is not performed:

```text
downstream validation not performed
reason
required next step
approval owner
```

This prevents a package release from implying product validation.

### Suggested validation scenarios

Scenario D001:

```text
name: normal long-context projection
expected: render allowed
evidence: projection report plus source coverage
```

Scenario D002:

```text
name: unresolved approval block
expected: dispatch blocked
evidence: blocked reason and source ids
```

Scenario D003:

```text
name: migration dry-run failure
expected: failure evidence literal
evidence: schema plan artifact and operator report
```

Scenario D004:

```text
name: redacted tool output
expected: raw secret absent from model-visible projection
evidence: redaction report and trace
```

Scenario D005:

```text
name: cross-org retrieval guard
expected: other org data excluded
evidence: source packet tenant scope report
```

### Approval requirements

Future downstream validation requires approval for:

```text
updating consumer package version
running provisioning workflows
creating test accounts
seeding data
deploying preview or production
returning credentials
inspecting logs that may contain secrets
```

Docs-only work does not need those approvals because it does not execute those actions.

### Summary

Future compaction work should return a deploy link and credentials only when they are actually created through approved test flows.

The validation packet should distinguish:

```text
package tests passed
preview deployed
credentials ready
seeded data ready
manual scenario passed
downstream not validated
```

This prevents a research document, package unit test, or release note from implying a product-level validation that did not happen.

## Projection failure mode catalog

Status: proposal only.

This catalog defines failures that a future Ekairos context projection system should detect, report, and, when necessary, block.

The catalog is intentionally strict because the package is positioned for migration-heavy, audit-sensitive workflows.

### Severity scale

Proposed severity values:

```text
critical
high
medium
low
informational
```

Blocking rule:

```text
critical failures block provider dispatch
high failures block dispatch unless explicitly approved for the scenario
medium failures require trace/report evidence and may allow dispatch
low failures require observability but do not block
informational findings enrich review reports
```

This is a proposal.

The technical leader should approve the exact severity behavior.

### Failure F001: current user instruction compressed

Severity:

```text
critical
```

Description:

```text
the newest controlling user instruction is summarized, omitted, or altered
```

Impact:

```text
the model may act on old scope, old constraints, or an instruction the user has changed
```

Detection:

```text
current user source packet not marked literalRequired
rendered input lacks exact or near-literal current user content
claim ledger treats current user instruction as derived instead of direct
```

Required behavior:

```text
block dispatch if current user instruction cannot fit literally
```

Operator report:

```text
current user instruction cannot be rendered within budget
```

### Failure F002: unresolved approval hidden

Severity:

```text
critical
```

Description:

```text
an approval gate, manual decision, or unapproved action is summarized away
```

Impact:

```text
the model may execute or recommend work that requires technical-leader approval
```

Detection:

```text
approval source packet exists
approval state is pending or rejected
projection omits or summarizes approval state
```

Required behavior:

```text
block dispatch if unresolved approval is relevant and cannot remain literal
```

Operator report:

```text
projection blocked because unresolved approval source is protected
```

### Failure F003: failed verification demoted

Severity:

```text
critical
```

Description:

```text
failed verification output becomes a vague summary or is omitted
```

Impact:

```text
the model may proceed as if migration or validation passed
```

Detection:

```text
verification result has failed status
projection does not include failed check literal
claim ledger contains success claim contradicted by failure output
```

Required behavior:

```text
preserve failed check literal or block dispatch
```

Operator report:

```text
failed verification source requires literal preservation
```

### Failure F004: secret value model-visible

Severity:

```text
critical
```

Description:

```text
raw secret-bearing content appears in rendered model input or summary
```

Impact:

```text
credential exposure
```

Detection:

```text
redaction classifier flags source
rendered input contains raw flagged span
summary includes raw flagged span
```

Required behavior:

```text
block dispatch and emit incident-class report
```

Operator report:

```text
secret-bearing source was prevented from model visibility
```

### Failure F005: tenant source crossing

Severity:

```text
critical
```

Description:

```text
projection includes or cites private source material from another tenant, organization, workspace, or app scope
```

Impact:

```text
cross-tenant data leak or wrong migration target
```

Detection:

```text
source tenant scope does not match current execution scope
retrieval query lacks tenant filter
claim ledger cites forbidden source id
```

Required behavior:

```text
block dispatch
```

Operator report:

```text
projection blocked due tenant-scope mismatch
```

### Failure F006: provider-native artifact treated as authority

Severity:

```text
high
```

Description:

```text
provider-native compaction artifact replaces local source packet coverage
```

Impact:

```text
operator cannot audit which durable sources shaped model input
```

Detection:

```text
rendered projection references provider artifact without local source coverage
claim ledger lacks durable source ids
operator report lacks local projection manifest
```

Required behavior:

```text
block when migration or audit scenario requires source lineage
```

Allowed behavior:

```text
record provider-native artifact as secondary provider artifact
```

### Failure F007: stale source accepted as current

Severity:

```text
high
```

Description:

```text
old docs, old local code, or old retrieved source is rendered as current fact after newer evidence exists
```

Impact:

```text
implementation may target obsolete APIs or old package behavior
```

Detection:

```text
source superseded by newer source
source exceeds staleness policy
claim has no caveat
```

Required behavior:

```text
add staleness caveat or block if current behavior is required
```

Operator report:

```text
source requires recheck before implementation
```

### Failure F008: destructive operation hidden

Severity:

```text
high
```

Description:

```text
delete, merge, or irreversible transaction operation is omitted from model-visible context
```

Impact:

```text
the model may continue without recognizing destructive migration risk
```

Detection:

```text
transaction plan includes destructive operation
projection marks it summaryAllowed without literal requirement
claim ledger lacks destructive operation claim
```

Required behavior:

```text
preserve operation type, count, target, and approval state literal or block
```

### Failure F009: old rejected option resurrected

Severity:

```text
high
```

Description:

```text
summary turns a rejected design or old plan into active guidance
```

Impact:

```text
model follows a previously rejected architecture
```

Detection:

```text
source packet marked rejected_option
summary lacks rejected marker
claim ledger validates claim as decision
```

Required behavior:

```text
mark rejected option explicitly or omit it as rejected history
```

### Failure F010: tool/action continuity lost

Severity:

```text
high
```

Description:

```text
projection loses pending tool calls, failed tool outputs, or action state needed for the next turn
```

Impact:

```text
model retries incorrectly or assumes a tool/action succeeded
```

Detection:

```text
tool call has pending/failed state
recent tool result not present
claim ledger lacks continuity claim
```

Required behavior:

```text
preserve continuity state literal or block dispatch
```

### Failure F011: budget ledger excludes tool schemas

Severity:

```text
medium
```

Description:

```text
token budget counts conversation but ignores tool schema surface
```

Impact:

```text
model input may exceed window or response reserve may collapse
```

Detection:

```text
available tool schemas have token estimate
budget ledger omits tool schema category
rendered input includes tools
```

Required behavior:

```text
record tool schema estimate and reduce tool surface if necessary
```

Blocking condition:

```text
block if response reserve or protected content becomes unsafe
```

### Failure F012: unsupported success claim

Severity:

```text
medium
```

Description:

```text
summary says operation succeeded without verification source support
```

Impact:

```text
operator or model may skip validation
```

Detection:

```text
success claim lacks verification source
claim type is fact but support level is weak or unsupported
```

Required behavior:

```text
render as unverified claim or reject from model-visible summary
```

### Failure F013: line/file anchor lost

Severity:

```text
medium
```

Description:

```text
source file or line anchor that matters for implementation disappears from projection
```

Impact:

```text
future implementation starts from vague references
```

Detection:

```text
local file source packet exists
projection summary mentions file without absolute path or anchor
```

Required behavior:

```text
preserve absolute path anchor for implementation-critical sources
```

### Failure F014: estimate error unreported

Severity:

```text
medium
```

Description:

```text
local token estimate diverges from provider usage and the divergence is not recorded
```

Impact:

```text
future budget decisions remain uncalibrated
```

Detection:

```text
provider usage is available
local estimate exists
ledger lacks estimate error
```

Required behavior:

```text
record estimate error and update calibration data
```

### Failure F015: omission reason missing

Severity:

```text
medium
```

Description:

```text
source packet is omitted without a reason
```

Impact:

```text
operator cannot distinguish safe omission from data loss
```

Detection:

```text
source packet inclusion mode is omitted
omission reason empty
```

Required behavior:

```text
record omission reason or fail validation
```

### Failure F016: projection report missing

Severity:

```text
medium
```

Description:

```text
model dispatch occurs but no projection report or trace evidence is emitted
```

Impact:

```text
operator cannot audit context selection after the fact
```

Detection:

```text
reactor executed
projection id missing
trace event missing
operator report missing
```

Required behavior:

```text
fail test suite; in production, emit incident or degraded audit status
```

### Failure F017: low-value history retained over high-value evidence

Severity:

```text
medium
```

Description:

```text
old exploratory conversation consumes budget while migration evidence is summarized or blocked
```

Impact:

```text
model sees less useful context despite available compression choices
```

Detection:

```text
budget ledger shows low-authority old history retained
high-authority source compressed or missing
```

Required behavior:

```text
selector should prefer high-authority evidence over low-value history
```

### Failure F018: report overstates validation

Severity:

```text
medium
```

Description:

```text
operator report or release note claims validation that did not occur
```

Impact:

```text
downstream users trust unverified behavior
```

Detection:

```text
report status says passed
validation evidence missing
downstream validation field absent or unknown
```

Required behavior:

```text
report exact validation status and known gaps
```

### Failure F019: duplicate source creates double-counted support

Severity:

```text
low
```

Description:

```text
same underlying source appears as multiple packets and claim support is counted multiple times
```

Impact:

```text
claim appears better supported than it is
```

Detection:

```text
same content hash
same source command/query
same timestamp and source id family
```

Required behavior:

```text
deduplicate support or label duplicate source
```

### Failure F020: summary too vague for operator use

Severity:

```text
low
```

Description:

```text
summary is technically safe but not useful enough for review
```

Impact:

```text
operator must inspect raw history too often
```

Detection:

```text
summary lacks decisions, failures, or source coverage details
manual reviewer marks insufficient
```

Required behavior:

```text
improve prompt or report format
```

### Failure response matrix

Proposed response matrix:

```text
critical: block dispatch, emit report, require review
high: block for migration/security/approval contexts, otherwise require explicit acceptance
medium: allow only with trace evidence and no safety impact
low: allow with report finding
informational: record only
```

### Test mapping

Failure modes should map to tests:

```text
F001 current user literal fixture
F002 unresolved approval fixture
F003 failed verification fixture
F004 secret-bearing output fixture
F005 tenant boundary fixture
F006 provider-native comparison fixture
F007 stale source fixture
F008 destructive transaction fixture
F009 rejected option fixture
F010 tool continuity fixture
F011 tool schema budget fixture
F012 unsupported success claim fixture
F013 local anchor fixture
F014 estimate error fixture
F015 omitted source fixture
F016 trace/report fixture
F017 selector priority fixture
F018 release report fixture
F019 duplicate source fixture
F020 manual reviewer fixture
```

### Summary

The failure catalog gives compaction a safety vocabulary.

Without severity classes, every context reduction can look like a harmless optimization.

For Ekairos, some context reductions are correctness failures.

The first implementation should treat at least these as blocking:

```text
current user instruction compressed
unresolved approval hidden
failed verification demoted
secret value model-visible
tenant source crossing
protected content cannot fit
```

## Consumer migration guide draft

Status: proposal only.

This section is a draft migration guide for future consumers of `@ekairos/events` if the projection-ledger design is approved.

No package release is approved.

No consumer update is approved.

The guide assumes breaking changes because the workspace instruction prefers non-retrocompatible changes unless explicitly asked otherwise.

### Audience

The audience is:

```text
applications using @ekairos/events context engine
applications using @ekairos/events reactors
applications reading event trace records
applications showing operator run reports
applications integrating with domain migration workflows
```

The guide is not for end users.

It is for product engineers and platform operators consuming the package.

### Migration headline

Proposed headline:

```text
@ekairos/events now treats model-facing context as an auditable projection derived from durable event history.
```

Short version:

```text
reactors should no longer assume they own context selection
model input can be blocked before provider dispatch
projection reports explain which sources were included, summarized, referenced, omitted, or blocked
```

### What changes conceptually

Old mental model:

```text
context history plus expansion becomes provider messages
```

New mental model:

```text
durable event history
-> source packets
-> projection decision
-> budget ledger
-> optional compaction artifact
-> rendered model input
-> provider dispatch only if validation passes
```

Important distinction:

```text
durable event history remains the source of truth
projection is the model-facing view for a run
```

### Primary breaking areas

Expected breaking areas:

```text
reactor params
context run trace payloads
model message construction ownership
blocked dispatch behavior
operator report data
test fixtures
possibly package exports
possibly schema entities if durable projections are approved
```

Each breaking area should have its own migration note in a future release.

### Reactor contract migration

Old assumption:

```text
reactor receives enough context events to construct model messages
```

New proposed assumption:

```text
reactor receives rendered model messages plus projection metadata
```

Consumer action:

```text
update custom reactors to read projection metadata
stop making source authority decisions inside provider code
handle blocked projection before model dispatch
record provider usage against projection id when available
```

Potential future params:

```text
contextId
runId
projectionId
messagesForModel
projectionManifest
budgetLedger
operatorReport
providerOptions
```

Do not do this in consumers:

```text
reconstruct context independently from event history after projection has already rendered
ignore blocked projection status
silently add extra source material to provider input
drop projection id from traces
```

### Blocked projection behavior

Old assumption:

```text
context engine eventually calls a reactor unless an upstream error stops it
```

New proposed assumption:

```text
context engine may stop before provider dispatch because model input is unsafe or over budget
```

Consumer action:

```text
handle blocked projection as a first-class run state
show blocked reason to operator
do not retry automatically without changing source context, budget, or approval state
record that provider dispatch did not occur
```

Example blocked reasons:

```text
current_user_instruction_cannot_fit
unresolved_approval_cannot_fit
failed_verification_cannot_fit
secret_redaction_failed
tenant_scope_mismatch
protected_context_exceeds_budget
```

Operator copy should be precise:

```text
The model was not called because protected context could not be rendered safely.
```

Do not show:

```text
model failed
provider error
conversation too long only
```

Blocked projection is not a provider failure.

It is a safety decision before provider dispatch.

### Trace and report migration

Old assumption:

```text
trace events mostly describe execution steps and provider/tool activity
```

New proposed assumption:

```text
trace events also describe projection planning, rendering, blocking, and validation
```

Consumer action:

```text
include projection trace events in run timelines
index projection id when available
show budget ledger summary
show source coverage summary
show blocked source ids
show validation status
```

Possible trace names:

```text
context_projection_planned
context_projection_rendered
context_projection_blocked
context_projection_validation_failed
context_projection_source_gap
```

Trace display should distinguish:

```text
planned
rendered
blocked
dispatched
provider_completed
provider_failed
```

### Operator UI migration

Consumers with operator UI should add or adapt:

```text
projection status
model dispatch status
blocked reason
source coverage count
budget ledger summary
compaction artifact count
redaction state
tenant-scope state
claim ledger high-risk findings
```

Minimum useful UI:

```text
status: rendered or blocked
reason: if blocked
included/summarized/referenced/omitted counts
source coverage status
model dispatch happened: yes/no
```

Target UI:

```text
source packet table
budget ledger
claim ledger
artifact references
trace timeline
manual reviewer notes
```

### Test migration

Consumers should update tests that assume:

```text
every context run calls provider
reactor constructs messages from raw event history
long context is truncated silently
provider error is the only no-response path
```

New tests should cover:

```text
successful rendered projection
blocked projection with no provider call
current user literal preservation
failed verification preservation
secret redaction
tenant-scope exclusion
tool schema budget
projection trace emission
```

Custom reactor tests should assert:

```text
reactor receives messagesForModel
reactor receives projection metadata
reactor does not dispatch on blocked projection
reactor records provider usage with projection id if available
```

### Migration scenarios

Scenario M001: consumer has no custom reactor.

Expected migration:

```text
update package version
update UI/report handling for blocked projection if exposed
update tests expecting provider dispatch
```

Scenario M002: consumer has custom reactor.

Expected migration:

```text
update reactor params
consume rendered messages
stop building context selection inside reactor
propagate projection id to traces
handle blocked status before provider call
```

Scenario M003: consumer reads trace events.

Expected migration:

```text
accept new projection trace event names
index projection id
display blocked projection as non-provider failure
```

Scenario M004: consumer performs migrations.

Expected migration:

```text
show migration projection report
preserve schema dry-run evidence
show org matrix and verification status
handle blocked projection as gate failure requiring review
```

Scenario M005: consumer uses provider-native compaction directly.

Expected migration:

```text
record provider-native artifact as secondary
retain local projection manifest as audit authority
do not use provider artifact as sole source coverage
```

### Data migration if durable projection schema is approved

If durable projection entities are approved, consumers may need:

```text
schema dry-run
query updates
retention policy update
operator report query update
data export update
```

If durable projection entities are not in the first release, consumers need only contract and trace/report updates.

The release notes must make this distinction explicit.

### Config migration

Potential future config concepts:

```text
model budget profile
response reserve
auto compaction threshold
manual compaction enabled
provider-native compaction enabled
tool surface budget
redaction policy
```

No config keys are proposed as final in this document.

Consumer migration guide should avoid invented config examples until approved.

If config is introduced, migration guide must state:

```text
required config keys
optional config keys
defaults
security impact
environment impact
test impact
```

### Provider migration

If provider-native compaction is introduced:

```text
state supported providers
state unsupported providers
state feature flags or explicit config
state provider artifact retention behavior
state local audit companion behavior
state failure behavior when native compaction is unavailable
```

Provider-native absence should not break local projection.

Local projection is the package-level contract.

Provider-native compaction is an adapter-level optimization or artifact path.

### Migration anti-patterns

Avoid:

```text
catching blocked projection and forcing provider dispatch
constructing provider messages outside the projection renderer
omitting projection trace events from operator timelines
treating provider-native compaction as source truth
assuming all long contexts can summarize safely
assuming all old context is low value
```

### Pre-upgrade checklist

Before upgrading a consumer:

```text
identify custom reactors
identify trace readers
identify operator UI surfaces
identify migration workflows
identify provider-native context usage
identify tests assuming provider dispatch
identify long-context scenarios
identify secrets in tool outputs
```

### Post-upgrade checklist

After upgrading a consumer:

```text
normal projection run passes
blocked projection run shows operator reason
provider dispatch does not happen when blocked
projection trace events visible
source coverage visible
budget ledger visible
secret redaction fixture passes
tenant boundary fixture passes
migration dry-run failure fixture passes if applicable
```

### Release-note snippet

Potential snippet:

```text
This release changes the @ekairos/events reactor contract so provider execution receives projection-rendered model input and projection metadata. Consumers with custom reactors must update to the new params and must treat blocked projection as a first-class non-provider run state.
```

Potential blocked-state snippet:

```text
A run can now stop before model dispatch when protected context cannot be rendered safely. This is expected behavior, not a provider failure.
```

Potential audit snippet:

```text
Projection reports show included, summarized, referenced, omitted, and blocked source classes so operators can inspect why the model saw a specific compact context.
```

### Summary

The consumer migration guide should be concrete and breaking.

It should not soften the contract change.

The essential migration message is:

```text
consumers must stop treating provider messages as an implementation detail hidden inside reactors
consumers must treat projection state as part of context execution
consumers must surface blocked projection as an expected safety outcome
```

## Package export surface impact appendix

Status: proposal only.

This appendix maps future context projection changes to the current public export surface of `@ekairos/events`.

Observed package version during this research pass:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\package.json:3

Observed export map starts here:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\package.json:20

```text

@ekairos/events/mcp
@ekairos/events/oidc
@ekairos/events/codex
@ekairos/events/react
@ekairos/events/instant
```

This matters because context compaction is not only an internal engine change.

Projection metadata can affect root exports, reactor exports, runtime trace behavior, React UI helpers, schema/domain exports, and downstream app contracts.

### Root entrypoint

Export entry:

```text
@ekairos/events
```

Source:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\index.ts

Relevant current anchors:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\index.ts:14

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\index.ts:91

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\index.ts:129

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\index.ts:145

Impact if projection contracts become public:

```text
root export may expose projection status types
root export may expose projection manifest types
root export may expose budget ledger types
root export may expose claim ledger types
root export may expose blocked reason constants
```

Breaking risk:

```text
high if existing ContextReactorParams changes
medium if only new projection types are exported
medium if convertItemsToModelMessages changes semantics
```

```text
should projection contracts be exported from the root entrypoint or a narrower projection entrypoint
```

```text
do not add broad public root exports until the first implementation slice proves the contract
```

Reason:

```text
root exports become the easiest consumer dependency to spread
```
