```text
instant entrypoint: only after store-level projection persistence approval
codex entrypoint: only for Codex-specific source classification after core projection exists
mcp entrypoint: only after inspection/authority model approval
oidc entrypoint: only if identity fields are exposed
```

### Summary

Projection compaction will likely be a public contract change even if implementation starts inside the engine.

The highest-risk public surfaces are:

```text
@ekairos/events
@ekairos/events/reactor
@ekairos/events/runtime
@ekairos/events/react
@ekairos/events/schema
@ekairos/events/instant
```

The first approved implementation should deliberately choose which of those surfaces changes.

Accidental export drift would turn an internal projection experiment into an unsupported consumer contract.

## Engine insertion-point risk appendix

Status: proposal only.

This appendix maps the current engine and reactor call path to safe and unsafe insertion points for context projection.

It is based on local code inspection during this research pass.

Relevant engine anchors:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\context.engine.ts:1379

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\context.engine.ts:1452

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\context.engine.ts:1497

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\context.engine.ts:1736

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\context.engine.ts:1887

Relevant reactor contract anchor:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\types.ts:42

Relevant AI SDK reactor anchors:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:153

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:173

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:190

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:320

### Current call path summary

Observed sequence:

```text
initialize context content
open reaction step
emit step/context events
run context updated hook
build system prompt
build actions/tools
build skills
expand raw events
get reactor
persist reaction parts callback is prepared
call reactor with expanded events, system prompt, actions, skills, ids, stream handles
reactor returns assistant event, action requests, messagesForModel
engine derives review requests
engine executes actions
action execute context receives messagesForModel
action results are written to stream/parts
shouldContinue runs after action results are merged
loop continues or finalizes
```

This sequence implies a key constraint:

```text
projection must happen before the reactor call if it decides what the model sees
```

It also implies a second constraint:

```text
messagesForModel returned by the reactor currently feeds action execution context
```

Therefore, a future projection-aware implementation must decide where `messagesForModel` is owned.

### Candidate insertion point A: before expandEvents

Location:

```text
before story.expandEvents
```

Benefit:

```text
can classify raw events early
could influence expansion
```

Risk:

```text
projection would miss expanded domain/retrieval sources
projection may duplicate expander policy
projection may not see the final source list used for provider input
```

Recommendation:

```text
do not make this the primary projection point
```

Use only for:

```text
pre-classification
early budget warnings
source expansion constraints
```

### Candidate insertion point B: after expandEvents, before getReactor or reactor call

Location:

```text
after expandedEvents is available
before model/provider dispatch
```

Benefit:

```text
sees expanded source context
still before provider execution
can block safely
can emit projection trace/report before reactor
can pass rendered messages to reactor
```

Risk:

```text
requires reactor contract change
requires engine to own projection policy
requires tests for blocked dispatch
```

Recommendation:

```text
primary insertion point for projection decision engine
```

Reason:

```text
it is late enough to see source expansion and early enough to prevent unsafe model calls
```

### Candidate insertion point C: inside reactor

Location:

```text
inside createAiSdkReactor or executeAiSdkReaction path
```

Benefit:

```text
minimal engine changes at first glance
provider code already builds messagesForModel
```

Risk:

```text
projection policy becomes provider-specific
blocked projection may appear as provider behavior
custom reactors can diverge
source coverage becomes harder to standardize
provider-native compaction can be confused with local audit
```

Recommendation:

```text
do not place primary projection policy inside provider reactors
```

Allowed reactor responsibility:

```text
execute provider call from approved rendered input
record provider usage
record provider artifact if adapter supports it
map provider chunks into context events
```

Not reactor responsibility:

```text
decide source authority
decide current user literal policy
decide tenant source inclusion
decide unresolved approval blocking
```

### Candidate insertion point D: after reactor call

Location:

```text
after reactionResult returns
```

Benefit:

```text
can inspect messagesForModel produced by reactor
can audit what was sent after the fact
```

Risk:

```text
too late to prevent unsafe provider dispatch
provider already saw context
blocked projection cannot be enforced
```

Recommendation:

```text
use only for post-dispatch validation and telemetry, not as primary protection
```

### Candidate insertion point E: before action execution

Location:

```text
after model response and before action execute
```

Benefit:

```text
can inspect action requests and messagesForModel
can block unsafe actions even if model call happened
```

Risk:

```text
model already received unsafe context if projection failed earlier
does not solve model input budget
does not protect provider-visible secrets
```

Recommendation:

```text
use as secondary action gate only
```

This insertion point is still valuable.

It can ensure that action execution sees:

```text
projection id
messagesForModel hash
blocked or rendered status
approval state
```

But it cannot replace pre-reactor projection.

### Candidate insertion point F: store itemsToModelMessages

Location:

```text
store.itemsToModelMessages inside AI SDK reactor path
```

Benefit:

```text
centralizes conversion from items to model messages for current AI SDK path
```

Risk:

```text
store becomes model projection policy owner
custom reactors may bypass it
projection cannot see full tool schema budget
blocked dispatch becomes awkward
source authority decisions move into persistence layer
```

Recommendation:

```text
do not make store conversion the projection policy boundary
```

Store can support:

```text
source packet reads
artifact reads
message conversion helpers
```

Store should not own:

```text
budget policy
authority policy
provider strategy
blocking decision
```

### Current action execution dependency

Observed in engine:

```text
action execute context receives messagesForModel from reactionResult
```

Implication:

```text
if projection renderer moves messagesForModel ownership to the engine, action execution can receive a stable rendered-message artifact that is independent from provider-specific reactor behavior
```

Future action execute context could receive:

```text
messages
projectionId
renderedInputHash
projectionStatus
budgetLedger
sourceCoverage
```

Approval question:

```text
should action execute context expose projection metadata to tools/actions
```

Recommendation:

```text
yes for projection id and rendered input hash
carefully review source coverage exposure because tools/actions may not need full source details
```

### Current persistReactionParts dependency

Observed engine behavior:

```text
engine prepares persistReactionParts callback before reactor invocation
reactor streams/persists output parts through that callback
```

Projection implication:

```text
input projection should be separate from output part persistence
```

Do not combine:

```text
input projection manifest
assistant output parts
action result parts
```

They are linked, but they are not the same artifact.

Recommended link fields:

```text
projectionId
renderedInputHash
eventId
executionId
stepId
iteration
```

### Current loop continuation dependency

Observed behavior:

```text
shouldContinue runs after action results have been merged into reactionEvent
```

Projection implication:

```text
each iteration may need a new projection because action results change source state
```

Therefore:

```text
projection scope should be per iteration, not only per context
```

Possible identifiers:

```text
contextId
executionId
stepId
iteration
projectionId
```

### Blocked projection state placement

If projection blocks before reactor call, engine must decide how to represent the run.

Options:

```text
execution failed
step failed
step completed with blocked projection status
new projection blocked trace and no assistant event
assistant event with engine part explaining block
```

Recommended proposal:

```text
step completes as blocked projection state, provider dispatch does not occur, trace records blocked reason, operator-visible report explains next action
```

Rationale:

```text
blocked projection is expected safety behavior, not provider failure
```

Approval needed:

```text
exact state model
whether context status remains open
whether execution status is failed, completed, or blocked
whether UI receives an assistant-like engine message
```

### Test insertion map

Tests needed for insertion point B:

```text
projection runs after expandEvents
projection receives expanded events
blocked projection prevents reactor call
reactor receives rendered messages when projection is renderable
action execute context receives rendered messages hash
shouldContinue behavior remains deterministic
step stream records projection trace/report
```

Tests needed for insertion point C if considered:

```text
custom reactor behavior does not diverge
AI SDK reactor and scripted reactor share projection policy
blocked projection does not become provider error
```

Tests needed for insertion point E:

```text
unsafe action can be blocked after model response
action approval state remains literal
messagesForModel hash matches model input
```

### Summary

The safest primary insertion point is:

```text
after expandEvents
before reactor invocation
```

The engine should own projection policy.

Reactors should execute approved rendered input.

Action execution should receive enough projection metadata to preserve audit continuity, but action execution cannot replace pre-provider projection.

## Projection manifest scenario examples

Status: proposal only.

This section gives concrete projection manifest examples for review.

They are not schema definitions.

They are not implementation contracts.

They show the level of detail needed for audit-grade compaction.

### Manifest design rules

A projection manifest should:

```text
identify the execution scope
identify the source packets considered
record budget decisions
record inclusion decisions
record validation result
record rendered input hash
record whether provider dispatch occurred
record source coverage
record blocked reasons when blocked
```

It should not:

```text
replace durable event history
store raw secrets
hide omitted source classes
claim provider-native compaction is authoritative
mix multiple iterations without lineage
```

### Common fields

Common fields:

```text
projectionId
contextId
executionId
stepId
iteration
createdAt
status
strategy
modelProfile
sourcePacketCount
budgetLedger
segments
claimLedger
validation
renderedInputHash
providerDispatch
operatorReport
```

Common status values:

```text
planned
rendered
blocked
validation_failed
provider_dispatched
superseded
```

Common segment inclusion modes:

```text
full
summary
reference
omitted
blocked
not_model_visible
```

### Manifest validation rules

General validation:

```text
every rendered source segment has sourcePacketIds
every summary segment has summaryArtifactId or explicit summary content reference
every reference segment has artifactRef or contentHash
every omitted segment has omission reason
every blocked segment has blocked reason and source ids
every provider dispatch has renderedInputHash
every blocked projection has providerDispatch.dispatched false
```

Security validation:

```text
not_model_visible segments never appear in rendered input
secret-bearing raw sources require redaction state
tenant scopes must match execution scope
```

Migration validation:

```text
schema plan status must be represented
org gate state must be represented
failed verification must be literal or blocked
destructive transaction operation must be literal or blocked
```

### Summary

Projection manifests should be small enough to inspect and structured enough to test.

They should make it obvious whether the model saw:

```text
literal source
validated summary
hash-backed reference
explicit omission
blocked protected source
```

That clarity is more important than the exact field names in these examples.

## Token accounting formulas appendix

Status: proposal only.

This appendix makes the budget math explicit.

The formulas are intentionally conservative.

The goal is to decide whether model dispatch is safe, not to perfectly predict provider billing.

### Core terms

Terms:

```text
W = model context window
R = required response reserve
S = system/developer/policy tokens
U = current user tokens
T = recent literal tail tokens
H = old history tokens retained literally
M = summary tokens
Q = retrieved source tokens
A = action/tool continuity tokens
G = tool schema tokens
P = provider overhead estimate
E = estimate error reserve
I = projected input tokens
```

Required invariant:

```text
I + R + E <= W
```

If the invariant fails, the projection must reduce nonprotected context or block.

### Projected input formula

Formula:

```text
I = S + U + T + H + M + Q + A + G + P
```

Protected subset:

```text
K = S + U + protected(T) + protected(A) + protected(Q)
```

Hard block rule:

```text
if K + R + E > W, block
```

Reason:

```text
protected content cannot be safely summarized or omitted to fit the model window
```

### Dispatch safety formula

Dispatch allowed when:

```text
I + R + E <= W
and validationStatus is accepted
and no critical failure exists
and providerDispatch.allowed is true
```

Dispatch blocked when:

```text
protected content exceeds budget
critical failure exists
validationStatus is blocked
redaction fails
tenant scope fails
unresolved approval cannot fit
```

### Estimate error reserve

Estimate error reserve can be derived from calibration:

```text
E = max(minErrorReserve, ceil(I * observedErrorRate))
```

Example:

```text
I = 50000
observedErrorRate = 0.08
minErrorReserve = 2000
E = max(2000, 4000)
E = 4000
```

If no provider/model calibration exists:

```text
use conservative default
```

Suggested initial defaults:

```text
small model window: 10 percent
medium model window: 8 percent
large model window: 5 percent
unknown tokenizer: 12 percent
```

These numbers require approval before implementation.

### Response reserve

Response reserve should depend on task type.

Suggested categories:

```text
classification or routing: small reserve
short answer: medium reserve
coding or migration planning: large reserve
tool-call planning: large reserve
report generation: large reserve
```

Formula:

```text
R = max(taskReserveFloor, ceil(W * responseReserveRatio))
```

Example:

```text
W = 128000
taskReserveFloor = 8000
responseReserveRatio = 0.10
R = max(8000, 12800)
R = 12800
```

Do not consume response reserve to include low-authority old history.

### Tool schema accounting

Tool schema budget:

```text
G = sum(tokens(toolSchema_i) for exposed tools)
```

Tool schema reduction rule:

```text
if G is large and tools are not needed, reduce exposed tool surface before summarizing protected context
```

Priority:

```text
current required tools
tools needed for unresolved action continuity
tools explicitly requested by current user
tools required by migration/report workflow
optional tools
irrelevant tools
```

Blocked condition:

```text
if required tool schema plus protected content cannot fit, block
```

Reason:

```text
removing required tools can make the model unable to complete the current turn safely
```

### Protected content formula

Protected content classes:

```text
current user instruction
system/developer/package policy
unresolved approval state
failed verification evidence
current target org/app mapping
destructive transaction plan
secret redaction state
tenant-scope guard evidence
recent tool/action continuity
```

Protected content sum:

```text
K = sum(tokens(source) for source where literalRequired is true)
```

If a protected source is too large:

```text
attempt relevant excerpt only if excerpt preserves the protected meaning
otherwise block
```

Example:

```text
failed verification output with exact count mismatch can be excerpted
current user instruction should remain literal
raw secret should not be model-visible
```

### Summary target formula

For summarizable old history:

```text
availableForSummary = W - R - E - S - U - T - Q - A - G - P
```

If:

```text
availableForSummary <= 0
```

then:

```text
no summary budget remains
```

The system should either:

```text
reference old sources
omit safe old sources
reduce tools
block
```

Summary target:

```text
M_target = min(maxSummaryTokens, max(minSummaryTokens, availableForSummary))
```

But:

```text
M_target should not be created if source coverage validation cannot pass
```

### Reference packet formula

Reference packet tokens:

```text
refTokens = metadataTokens + excerptTokens + caveatTokens
```

Reference value is high when:

```text
rawArtifactTokens >> refTokens
and artifact hash/source id is durable
and excerpt preserves decision-relevant evidence
```

Use reference when:

```text
large dataset extract
large success log
large unchanged query result
large code diff already persisted elsewhere
```

Do not use reference alone when:

```text
failed evidence needs exact diagnostic
approval state is unresolved
current user instruction is source
tenant scope is ambiguous
```

### Omission budget formula

Omission candidates:

```text
lowAuthoritySources
supersededSources
duplicateSources
irrelevantOldExploration
largeSuccessLogsWithCountsPreserved
```

Omission savings:

```text
O = sum(tokens(candidate) - tokens(omissionNote))
```

Omission is valid only when:

```text
omissionReason exists
authorityClass is safe for omission
claim ledger does not depend on omitted source
operator report records omission
```

### Worked budget example: safe summary

Inputs:

```text
W = 128000
R = 12000
S = 1500
U = 300
T = 15000
H = 0
M = 3000
Q = 6000
A = 2500
G = 8000
P = 1000
E = 5000
```

Projected input:

```text
I = 1500 + 300 + 15000 + 0 + 3000 + 6000 + 2500 + 8000 + 1000
I = 37300
```

Safety:

```text
I + R + E = 37300 + 12000 + 5000
I + R + E = 54300
54300 <= 128000
dispatch may be allowed if validation passes
```

### Worked budget example: block

Inputs:

```text
W = 32000
R = 6000
S = 1200
U = 400
protected approval = 18000
failed verification = 9000
G = 3000
E = 3000
```

Protected sum:

```text
K = 1200 + 400 + 18000 + 9000
K = 28600
```

Safety:

```text
K + R + E = 28600 + 6000 + 3000
K + R + E = 37600
37600 > 32000
block
```

This should not attempt provider dispatch.

### Worked budget example: reduce tools first

Inputs:

```text
W = 64000
R = 8000
E = 4000
protected content = 30000
tool schemas all = 18000
tool schemas relevant = 5000
old history = 12000
```

All tools:

```text
30000 + 18000 + 12000 + 8000 + 4000 = 72000
72000 > 64000
```

Relevant tools only:

```text
30000 + 5000 + 12000 + 8000 + 4000 = 59000
59000 <= 64000
```

Decision:

```text
reduce tool surface before summarizing protected content
```

### Telemetry fields

Budget telemetry should record:

```text
estimatedSystemTokens
estimatedCurrentUserTokens
estimatedLiteralTailTokens
estimatedSummaryTokens
estimatedReferenceTokens
estimatedRetrievedSourceTokens
estimatedActionContinuityTokens
estimatedToolSchemaTokens
estimatedProviderOverheadTokens
estimatedErrorReserveTokens
requiredResponseReserveTokens
projectedInputTokens
modelWindowTokens
providerPromptTokens
providerTotalTokens
estimateErrorTokens
estimateErrorRate
```

### Summary

The budget ledger should make dispatch safety mechanically reviewable.

The core invariant is simple:

```text
projected input plus response reserve plus estimate error must fit inside the model window
```

But the source priority rules matter more than the arithmetic.

Ekairos should never make protected migration or approval context disappear just because the arithmetic is inconvenient.

## Provider capability registry proposal

Status: proposal only.

Provider and model behavior should not be inferred inside projection logic.

A future implementation should read provider/model capabilities from an explicit registry approved by the technical leader.

This registry can start as a pure in-memory or test-only data structure if approved.

It does not require schema/config work in the first slice.

### Why a capability registry exists

Context projection needs to know:

```text
model window size
response reserve policy
token usage fields returned by provider
whether provider supports tool calling
whether provider supports native compaction
whether provider supports prompt caching
whether provider supports provider-managed conversation state
whether provider can return raw provider metadata
whether provider tool schema format is large or compact
whether streaming chunks can be mapped to context parts
```

If this information is scattered across adapters:

```text
projection policy becomes inconsistent
tests become provider-specific
budget estimates become unreviewable
provider-native features may become hidden behavior
```

### Registry scope

The registry should describe capabilities, not secrets.

Allowed:

```text
provider name
model family
model id pattern
context window tokens
default response reserve
estimate error policy
native compaction support
conversation state support
tool support
usage metadata mapping
provider artifact support
docs URL
docs checked at
```

Not allowed:

```text
API keys
admin tokens
tenant data
raw provider account config
```

### Candidate record

Candidate shape:

```json
{
  "provider": "example-provider",
  "modelFamily": "example-family",
  "modelIdPattern": "example/*",
  "windowTokens": 128000,
  "defaultResponseReserveTokens": 12000,
  "estimateErrorRate": 0.08,
  "supportsTools": true,
  "supportsStreaming": true,
  "supportsNativeCompaction": false,
  "supportsConversationState": false,
  "supportsPromptCaching": false,
  "usageFields": {
    "promptTokens": ["promptTokens", "inputTokens"],
    "completionTokens": ["completionTokens", "outputTokens"],
    "totalTokens": ["totalTokens"]
  },
  "providerArtifacts": [],
  "officialDocsUrl": "example provider docs URL omitted",
  "docsCheckedAt": "2026-05-02",
  "confidence": "example_only"
}
```

This JSON is illustrative only.

Do not use this illustrative provider entry as a source.

### Capability categories

Capability categories:

```text
budget
message_rendering
tools
streaming
native_compaction
conversation_state
prompt_cache
usage_telemetry
provider_artifacts
security_logging
```

Each category should have:

```text
supported
unsupported
unknown
requires_recheck
```

Unknown should not silently become supported.

### Budget capabilities

Budget capability fields:

```text
windowTokens
maxOutputTokens
defaultResponseReserveTokens
recommendedResponseReserveRatio
estimateErrorRate
tokenizerConfidence
usageMetadataAvailable
```

Budget decision rules:

```text
unknown window blocks production enablement
unknown tokenizer increases estimate error reserve
missing provider usage prevents calibration but not necessarily dispatch
known small window forces earlier projection
```

Approval questions:

```text
what model families are in scope for first implementation
what fallback window is acceptable for unknown model id
whether unknown window should block dispatch
```

Recommended default:

```text
unknown window should block production dispatch for compaction-enabled runs
```

### Message rendering capabilities

Message rendering fields:

```text
supportsSystemPrompt
supportsDeveloperPrompt
supportsMultiMessageHistory
supportsToolResults
supportsReasoningParts
supportsSourceParts
maxMessageCountKnown
```

Rendering rules:

```text
renderer should target provider-neutral messages first
adapter may transform provider-neutral messages to provider format
adapter must not drop protected segments silently
adapter must report dropped or transformed unsupported parts
```

Approval question:

```text
should unsupported message part cause block or adapter-level transformation
```

Recommended default:

```text
block protected unsupported parts; transform only low-risk display details with trace evidence
```

### Tool capabilities

Tool capability fields:

```text
supportsTools
supportsRequiredToolChoice
supportsParallelToolCalls
supportsProviderDefinedTools
toolSchemaFormat
toolCallIdStable
toolResultFormat
```

Projection relevance:

```text
tool schemas consume budget
tool availability changes model action surface
tool call ids are needed for action continuity
tool results are source packets after execution
```

Rules:

```text
tool schema tokens must be counted
tool surface reduction must be explicit
required tools must stay available or dispatch should block
```

### Streaming capabilities

Streaming capability fields:

```text
supportsStreaming
streamChunkTypesKnown
usageAvailableDuringStream
usageAvailableAfterStream
providerMetadataAvailable
```

Projection relevance:

```text
streaming output produces event parts after dispatch
usage telemetry calibrates future budget estimates
provider metadata may include cache or native artifact details
```

Rules:

```text
projection manifest is input-side
stream output parts are output-side
link them with executionId, stepId, eventId, projectionId
```

### Native compaction capabilities

Native compaction fields:

```text
supportsNativeCompaction
nativeCompactionApiKind
nativeCompactionScope
nativeCompactionArtifactAvailable
nativeCompactionArtifactReplayable
nativeCompactionCostKnown
nativeCompactionDocsUrl
nativeCompactionDocsCheckedAt
```

Possible scopes:

```text
response
conversation
provider_session
cache
unknown
```

Rules:

```text
native compaction never replaces local projection manifest
native compaction must be source-rechecked before implementation
native compaction artifact role must be secondary unless explicitly approved otherwise
```

Blocked condition:

```text
provider-native artifact is the only audit path for a migration run
```

### Conversation state capabilities

Conversation state fields:

```text
supportsProviderConversationState
stateIdReturned
stateCanBeCompacted
stateCanBeReplayInspected
stateRetentionKnown
stateTenantIsolationKnown
```

Projection relevance:

```text
provider conversation state may reduce payload size but may weaken local replay if treated as source truth
```

Rules:

```text
provider state id can be recorded as provider artifact
local durable event history remains source of truth
projection report records whether provider state was used
```

### Prompt cache capabilities

Prompt cache fields:

```text
supportsPromptCaching
cacheKeyVisible
cacheHitUsageVisible
cacheScopeKnown
cacheInvalidationKnown
```

Projection relevance:

```text
cache hit can lower cost but does not lower logical model-visible context
```

Rule:

```text
prompt caching should affect cost telemetry, not source authority
```

Do not treat cached tokens as omitted context.

### Usage telemetry mapping

Current AI SDK reactor already records usage-like fields in the reaction result path.

Relevant current anchor:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\types.ts:18

Relevant AI SDK usage mapping anchor:

@C:\ekairos-projects\workspace\ekairos-base\packages\events\src\reactors\ai-sdk.step.ts:320

Capability registry should map provider usage fields to:

```text
promptTokens
promptTokensCached
promptTokensUncached
completionTokens
totalTokens
latencyMs
rawUsage
rawProviderMetadata
```

Rules:

```text
raw usage can calibrate estimate error
raw provider metadata must be redacted if it can contain sensitive data
missing usage marks calibration unknown
```

### Security and logging capability

Security fields:

```text
providerLogsPrompts
providerLogsToolInputs
zeroDataRetentionAvailable
dataRegionKnown
rawProviderMetadataMayContainSecrets
```

Projection relevance:

```text
model-visible context may also become provider-visible context
```

Rules:

```text
secret-bearing source must be redacted before provider dispatch
provider logging caveats should be in operator report if relevant
```

### Recheck policy

Capability records should include:

```text
docsUrl
docsCheckedAt
checkedBy
sourceClass
confidence
expiresAt
```

Recheck required when:

```text
native compaction is enabled
provider adapter behavior changes
model id changes
usage telemetry fields change
provider docs expire
```

### Test strategy

Tests for capability registry:

```text
unknown provider blocks production compaction
known provider budget profile is applied
unknown tokenizer increases error reserve
tool schema budget uses provider tool capability
native compaction unsupported path skips provider-native call
native compaction supported path still requires local projection manifest
usage mapping records estimate error
```

### Summary

The provider capability registry makes provider assumptions explicit.

It should be treated as approval-controlled input to projection decisions.

Without it, provider-specific branches can quietly define policy.

With it, Ekairos can say:

```text
this model window is known
this tool behavior is known
this provider-native compaction path is available
this provider capability is unknown and blocks production enablement
```

## Operator UX copy catalog for projection states

Status: proposal only.

This catalog defines operator-facing language for projection and compaction states.

It does not implement UI.

It gives future UI and report work precise wording so compaction does not look like an invisible or arbitrary model failure.

### Copy principles

Operator copy should be:

```text
specific
factual
short
evidence-linked
clear about whether the model was called
clear about what action is needed
clear about validation status
```

Operator copy should not be:

```text
optimistic without evidence
vague about blocked reasons
provider-blaming when dispatch did not happen
silent about omitted sources
silent about redaction
silent about downstream validation gaps
```

### State: projection planned

Meaning:

```text
the system is calculating model-facing context before dispatch
```

Short copy:

```text
Planning model context.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
Ekairos is selecting source material, budget, and safety checks before calling the model.
```

Do not say:

```text
Summarizing conversation.
```

Reason:

```text
projection may not involve summarization
```

### State: projection rendered

Meaning:

```text
model-facing context was rendered and validation passed
```

Short copy:

```text
Model context ready.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
The model input was rendered from an audited projection. Source coverage and budget checks passed.
```

Required metadata:

```text
projection id
rendered input hash
included source count
summarized source count
referenced source count
omitted source count
budget status
```

Do not say:

```text
All context included.
```

Reason:

```text
rendered projection may include references, summaries, and omissions
```

### State: provider dispatched

Meaning:

```text
model call occurred after projection validation
```

Short copy:

```text
Model called.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
Provider dispatch occurred using the rendered projection.
```

Required metadata:

```text
provider
model
projection id
step id
prompt token estimate
provider prompt tokens if available
```

Do not say:

```text
Model saw full history.
```

Reason:

```text
model saw projection-rendered context, not necessarily full durable history
```

### State: blocked before provider dispatch

Meaning:

```text
projection validation stopped the run before a model call
```

Short copy:

```text
Model call blocked.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
The model was not called because protected context could not be rendered safely.
```

Required metadata:

```text
blocked reason
source ids or source count
budget ledger
recommended operator action
model dispatched: no
```

Do not say:

```text
Provider failed.
```

Reason:

```text
provider dispatch did not occur
```

### State: blocked by unresolved approval

Short copy:

```text
Approval required before model call.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
The run was blocked because an unresolved approval is protected context and could not be safely reduced.
```

Recommended action:

```text
Review the approval gate, reduce context, or split the task before retrying.
```

Do not say:

```text
Waiting for model.
```

Reason:

```text
the model is intentionally not called
```

### State: blocked by failed verification

Short copy:

```text
Verification failure must be reviewed.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
The run was blocked because failed verification evidence must remain visible and cannot fit safely.
```

Recommended action:

```text
Inspect the failed check, correct the migration state, or start a narrower follow-up run.
```

Do not say:

```text
Context too long.
```

Reason:

```text
the important fact is failed evidence, not only length
```

### State: blocked by tenant scope

Short copy:

```text
Tenant scope mismatch.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
The projection was blocked because a source did not match the current organization, workspace, app, or tenant scope.
```

Recommended action:

```text
Recheck source retrieval scope before retrying.
```

Do not say:

```text
Source unavailable.
```

Reason:

```text
source may exist but be forbidden for this scope
```

### State: blocked by redaction failure

Short copy:

```text
Secret redaction required.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
The model was not called because secret-bearing material could not be safely represented.
```

Recommended action:

```text
Review the redaction report and use an approved redacted artifact.
```

Do not show:

```text
raw secret value
```

### State: rendered with summary

Short copy:

```text
Older context summarized.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
Older source material was summarized with source coverage. Recent and protected sources remained literal.
```

Required metadata:

```text
summary artifact id
source packet count
claim coverage status
validation status
```

Do not say:

```text
Conversation compressed safely.
```

Reason:

```text
safe needs evidence; state exact validation result instead
```

### State: rendered with references

Short copy:

```text
Large artifacts referenced.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
Large artifacts were represented by hash-backed references and relevant excerpts.
```

Required metadata:

```text
artifact ref
artifact class
content hash
record count if available
redaction state
```

Do not say:

```text
Large artifacts ignored.
```

Reason:

```text
reference is an explicit inclusion mode, not omission
```

### State: omitted sources

Short copy:

```text
Some sources omitted.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
Low-authority or superseded sources were omitted with recorded reasons.
```

Required metadata:

```text
omitted count
omission reasons
authority classes
whether any omission needs review
```

Do not hide omitted source count.

Omission is acceptable only when explainable.

### State: source coverage gap

Short copy:

```text
Source coverage gap.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
A model-visible claim lacks sufficient source support.
```

Recommended action:

```text
Review the claim ledger or regenerate the projection.
```

Model dispatch:

```text
blocked if gap affects protected or high-risk claim
may continue only if gap is low-risk and approved by policy
```

### State: stale provider source

Short copy:

```text
Provider docs need recheck.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
This claim depends on provider documentation that must be rechecked before implementation.
```

Recommended action:

```text
Refresh the provider source packet and update the approval record.
```

Do not say:

```text
Provider API confirmed.
```

unless current source evidence is attached.

### State: downstream validation not performed

Short copy:

```text
Downstream validation not performed.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
Package-level checks may exist, but no downstream product scenario was validated for this change.
```

Required metadata:

```text
reason
required next step
approval owner
```

Do not say:

```text
Ready for product use.
```

unless the downstream validation packet exists.

### State: downstream validation ready

Short copy:

```text
Manual validation ready.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
A review environment, seeded data, and approved test credentials are available for manual validation.
```

Required metadata:

```text
deploy URL
test account policy
seeded data ids
scenario ids
known gaps
```

Do not include raw privileged secrets.

### State: provider-native artifact recorded

Short copy:

```text
Provider artifact recorded.
```

Detailed copy:

```text
A provider-native artifact was recorded as secondary evidence. The local projection manifest remains authoritative.
```

Do not say:

```text
Provider compaction verified the context.
```

unless local validation confirms the claim.

### Summary table

Copy table:

```text
planned: Planning model context.
rendered: Model context ready.
dispatched: Model called.
blocked: Model call blocked.
blocked_approval: Approval required before model call.
blocked_verification: Verification failure must be reviewed.
blocked_tenant: Tenant scope mismatch.
blocked_redaction: Secret redaction required.
summary: Older context summarized.
reference: Large artifacts referenced.
omission: Some sources omitted.
coverage_gap: Source coverage gap.
stale_source: Provider docs need recheck.
downstream_not_validated: Downstream validation not performed.
downstream_ready: Manual validation ready.
provider_artifact: Provider artifact recorded.
```

### Summary

Projection UX should make one fact impossible to miss:

```text
did the model see a validated projection, or was the model call blocked
```

Everything else is supporting evidence.

## Selector trace walkthroughs

Status: proposal only.

This section walks through how a future selector might classify sources, apply budgets, and produce a projection decision.

The walkthroughs are meant to make selector behavior reviewable before implementation.

### Walkthrough format

Each walkthrough uses:

```text
input source packets
classification pass
budget pass
conflict pass
decision pass
validation pass
operator report pass
```

The passes are conceptual.

Implementation may combine them, but the trace should preserve this level of explanation.

### Walkthrough W001: normal long chat

Input source packets:

```text
src_policy: package policy, 900 tokens
src_user_latest: current user, 120 tokens
src_turns_old: old exploratory chat, 30000 tokens
src_decision_old: accepted old decision, 900 tokens
src_rejected_old: rejected old option, 1200 tokens
src_recent_tail: recent assistant/user tail, 6000 tokens
src_tool_recent: recent tool output, 3500 tokens
tool_schema_all: available tools, 5000 tokens
```

Classification pass:

```text
src_policy -> policy, literalRequired
src_user_latest -> current_user, literalRequired
src_turns_old -> old_history, summaryAllowed
src_decision_old -> decision, summaryAllowed with claim required
src_rejected_old -> rejected_option, summaryAllowed with rejected marker required
src_recent_tail -> recent_history, literalPreferred
src_tool_recent -> tool_evidence, literalPreferred
tool_schema_all -> tool_surface, budgeted
```

Budget pass:

```text
full input is over budget
protected content fits
tool schemas fit
old exploratory chat is largest reducible source
```

Decision pass:

```text
policy full
current user full
recent tail full
recent tool output full
old exploratory chat summary
accepted decision summary with claim
rejected option summary with rejected marker
all required tools included
```

Validation pass:

```text
current user literal passes
source coverage passes
rejected option marker passes
budget passes
```

Operator report:

```text
rendered with summary
old exploratory history summarized
recent evidence literal
model dispatch allowed
```

### Walkthrough W002: migration dry-run failure

Input source packets:

```text
src_policy: package policy, 900 tokens
src_user_latest: current migration instruction, 180 tokens
src_schema_plan: schema dry-run output, 7000 tokens
src_schema_failure_line: failed entity/field lines, 800 tokens
src_org_matrix: org/app matrix, 2200 tokens
src_dataset_extract: dataset extract, 90000 tokens
src_transform_notes: transform plan, 4500 tokens
src_verification_failed: verification failure, 2500 tokens
tool_schema_migration: migration tools, 6500 tokens
```

Classification pass:

```text
src_policy -> policy, literalRequired
src_user_latest -> current_user, literalRequired
src_schema_plan -> schema_plan, referenceAllowed with failure literal
src_schema_failure_line -> failure_evidence, literalRequired
src_org_matrix -> org_matrix, literalRequired
src_dataset_extract -> dataset_extract, referenceAllowed
src_transform_notes -> transform_plan, summaryAllowed
src_verification_failed -> verification_result, literalRequired
tool_schema_migration -> tool_surface, required
```

Budget pass:

```text
full dataset extract cannot fit
protected schema failure plus org matrix plus verification failure can fit
migration tools can fit
transform notes need summary
```

Decision pass:

```text
current user full
schema failure lines full
schema dry-run full status plus reference to full artifact
org matrix full for current target org
dataset extract reference with hash and counts
transform notes summary
verification failure full
migration tools included
```

Validation pass:

```text
failed schema evidence literal passes
verification failure literal passes
dataset reference has hash
org scope present
budget passes
```

Operator report:

```text
rendered with migration references
failed verification visible
dataset extract reference only
model dispatch allowed if next action is diagnostic
```

Important nuance:

```text
dispatch may be allowed for diagnosis even though migration gate failed
dispatch should not imply rollout approval
```

### Walkthrough W003: unresolved approval pressure

Input source packets:

```text
src_policy: project approval policy, 1200 tokens
src_user_latest: current user asks to continue, 100 tokens
src_approval_pending: unapproved schema/config plan, 22000 tokens
src_recent_tail: recent discussion, 10000 tokens
src_tool_schema: required tools, 5000 tokens
model_window: 32000 tokens
response_reserve: 6000 tokens
estimate_error: 3000 tokens
```

Classification pass:

```text
src_policy -> policy, literalRequired
src_user_latest -> current_user, literalRequired
src_approval_pending -> approval_state, literalRequired
src_recent_tail -> recent_history, summaryAllowed except current constraints
src_tool_schema -> tool_surface, required
```

Budget pass:

```text
protected content plus required reserve exceeds window
approval state cannot be safely summarized
```

Decision pass:

```text
projection blocked
provider dispatch not allowed
operator action required
```

Validation pass:

```text
blocked reason: unresolved_approval_cannot_fit
source ids recorded
model dispatch false
```

Operator report:

```text
model call blocked
approval required before model call
split task or obtain approval
```

### Walkthrough W004: secret-bearing diagnostic

Input source packets:

```text
src_policy: secret redaction policy, 700 tokens
src_user_latest: asks to diagnose failed auth, 150 tokens
src_tool_output: command output with raw token and error code, 4000 tokens
src_redacted_output: redacted diagnostic, 800 tokens
src_recent_tail: recent chat, 2000 tokens
```

Classification pass:

```text
src_policy -> policy, literalRequired
src_user_latest -> current_user, literalRequired
src_tool_output -> secret_bearing_tool_output, notModelVisible
src_redacted_output -> tool_evidence, referenceAllowed
src_recent_tail -> recent_history, literalPreferred
```

Budget pass:

```text
budget is sufficient
raw secret is not allowed regardless of budget
```

Decision pass:

```text
policy full
current user full
redacted diagnostic reference
recent tail full
raw secret source not model visible
```

Validation pass:

```text
raw secret absent from rendered input
redaction state recorded
operator report includes redaction warning
```

Operator report:

```text
rendered with redacted reference
raw secret not sent to provider
model dispatch allowed
```

### Walkthrough W005: tenant source conflict

Input source packets:

```text
src_policy: tenant isolation policy, 900 tokens
src_user_latest: current org A request, 100 tokens
src_org_a_context: current org source, 3000 tokens
src_org_b_context: other org source, 3000 tokens
src_old_chat: old mention of org B, 2000 tokens
```

Classification pass:

```text
src_policy -> policy, literalRequired
src_user_latest -> current_user, literalRequired
src_org_a_context -> tenant_scoped_source, allowed
src_org_b_context -> tenant_scoped_source, forbidden
src_old_chat -> old_history, summaryAllowed with tenant caveat
```

Budget pass:

```text
budget is sufficient
tenant conflict is independent of budget
```

Decision pass:

```text
org A source included
org B source blocked/excluded
old chat summarized only if it does not include private org B data
```

Validation pass:

```text
tenant filter passes for included sources
forbidden source not cited by claim ledger
```

Operator report:

```text
rendered with tenant filtering
other-tenant private source excluded
```

Blocked variant:

```text
if current claim requires org B source, block instead of rendering unsupported cross-tenant claim
```

### Walkthrough W006: provider capability unknown

Input source packets:

```text
src_policy: provider recheck policy, 800 tokens
src_user_latest: asks to use new model, 100 tokens
src_provider_model: model id not in capability registry
src_context_history: moderate context, 12000 tokens
tool_schema: tools, 3000 tokens
```

Classification pass:

```text
src_policy -> policy, literalRequired
src_user_latest -> current_user, literalRequired
src_provider_model -> provider_capability, requiresRecheck
src_context_history -> history, reducible if needed
tool_schema -> tool_surface
```

Budget pass:

```text
window size unknown
estimate error unknown
```

Decision pass:

```text
block production compaction-enabled dispatch
or require explicit approved fallback profile
```

Validation pass:

```text
blocked reason: provider_capability_unknown
```

Operator report:

```text
provider docs need recheck
model call blocked until capability record is approved
```

### Trace event expectations

For each walkthrough, trace should include:

```text
projection planned
source packet count
budget ledger
decision summary
validation result
provider dispatch yes/no
```

Blocked trace should include:

```text
blocked reason
source ids
protected token estimate
required reserve
operator action
```

Rendered trace should include:

```text
rendered input hash
included count
summary count
reference count
omitted count
warnings
```

### Summary

Selector traces make compaction debuggable.

The useful audit question is:

```text
given these sources and budget, why did this source become full, summary, reference, omitted, or blocked
```

If the trace cannot answer that question, the selector is not ready for migration-grade use.

## Cross-agent pattern mapping to Ekairos proposals

Status: proposal only.

This section maps observed patterns from other agents and frameworks into Ekairos-specific design choices.

The goal is not to copy any one system.

The goal is to extract the durable patterns that fit `@ekairos/events`.

### Pattern: automatic threshold compaction

Seen in:

```text
Claude Code style context-window management
Cline auto compact
OpenCode overflow and compaction paths
```

Generic idea:

```text
monitor context growth and compact before the model window fails
```

Ekairos adaptation:

```text
monitor projected input budget before provider dispatch
calculate protected content first
compact only allowed old/history segments
block if protected content cannot fit
record projection trace
```

Not adopted directly:

```text
silent summarization as an internal convenience
```

Reason:

```text
Ekairos needs migration audit and technical-leader reviewability
```

Implementation proposal:

```text
projection decision engine plus budget ledger
```

### Pattern: provider-native compaction

Seen in:

```text
Anthropic API compaction
OpenAI Responses compact endpoint
provider-managed conversation state patterns
```

Generic idea:

```text
provider helps compress or carry conversation state
```

Ekairos adaptation:

```text
provider-native artifact may be recorded as secondary evidence
local projection manifest remains audit authority
source packet ledger remains required
```

Not adopted directly:

```text
provider artifact as sole source of truth
```

Reason:

```text
provider state is not enough for migration-source lineage and tenant-scoped audit
```

Implementation proposal:

```text
provider capability registry plus provider adapter acceptance checklist
```

### Pattern: explicit context files

Seen in:

```text
Hermes context files
Gemini CLI context files
Goose hints
Cursor rules
Windsurf memories
```

Generic idea:

```text
let users or projects provide persistent context outside chat history
```

Ekairos adaptation:

```text
model persistent instructions as rule/source packets with authority and staleness
keep rules separate from compaction artifacts
record activation reason
```

Not adopted directly:

```text
auto-memory as first implementation slice
```

Reason:

```text
persistent memory can become stale or cross-tenant unless source-scoped and approved
```

Implementation proposal:

```text
rule activation plane proposal
auto-memory delayed design
source packet classification
```

### Pattern: retrieval-first context

Seen in:

```text
Cursor codebase context
Continue context providers
Aider repo map
Windsurf codemaps
Zed agent panel context
```

Generic idea:

```text
select relevant codebase/project sources instead of sending all history
```

Ekairos adaptation:

```text
retrieval providers produce source packets
source packets carry tenant scope, authority, staleness, and token estimates
retrieved sources enter projection budget like any other source
```

Not adopted directly:

```text
retrieval result as unverified current fact
```

Reason:

```text
retrieved sources can be stale, low-authority, or wrong-tenant
```

Implementation proposal:

```text
retrieval provider API proposal
stale-source invalidation rules
claim ledger validation
```

### Pattern: repo maps and structural summaries

Seen in:

```text
Aider repo map
Windsurf codemaps
IDE codebase indexes
```

Generic idea:

```text
represent large codebases through structural maps
```

Ekairos adaptation:

```text
structural context can be a source packet class
repo map claims need source links to files or symbols
edited files and failing lines remain literal when needed
```

Not adopted directly:

```text
repo map as substitute for exact implementation anchors
```

Reason:

```text
implementation work needs exact local anchors and current file state
```

Implementation proposal:

```text
source packet format catalog
claim ledger reviewer examples
local file anchor preservation rules
```

### Pattern: visible compaction steps

Seen in:

```text
Cline compaction surfaced as a tool-like event
agent systems that expose context operations
```

Generic idea:

```text
make context reduction visible to the user/operator
```

Ekairos adaptation:

```text
emit projection trace events
show operator report
show blocked reason
show source coverage
show budget ledger
```

Not adopted directly:

```text
single generic compaction message
```

Reason:

```text
Ekairos operators need to know what was included, summarized, referenced, omitted, or blocked
```

Implementation proposal:

```text
operator report examples
operator UX copy catalog
projection failure mode catalog
```

### Pattern: checkpoint and restore around compaction

Seen in:

```text
Cline checkpoint behavior
durable agent workflow patterns
```

Generic idea:

```text
maintain recoverability around context state changes
```

Ekairos adaptation:

```text
never mutate raw event_parts for compaction
projection artifacts are derived and link back to durable sources
blocked or rendered projection can be regenerated if sources remain
```

Not adopted directly:

```text
rewrite transcript as the checkpoint
```

Reason:

```text
event history is audit source of truth
```

Implementation proposal:

```text
recursive compaction lineage
projection lifecycle state machine
storage and retention sizing considerations
```

### Pattern: model capability aware compaction

Seen in:

```text
Cline model-specific context behavior
provider docs with different model windows
framework memory systems with configurable model contexts
```

Generic idea:

```text
context strategy depends on model capabilities
```

Ekairos adaptation:

```text
capability registry defines model window, tool support, usage telemetry, and native compaction support
projection engine uses registry for budget and provider strategy
unknown capabilities block production enablement or require approval
```

Not adopted directly:

```text
adapter-specific hidden defaults
```

Reason:

```text
capability assumptions affect safety and must be reviewable
```

Implementation proposal:

```text
provider capability registry proposal
model-window budget profiles
usage telemetry calibration loop
```

### Pattern: long-term memory

Seen in:

```text
LangGraph memory
LlamaIndex memory
AutoGen memory
Windsurf memories
```

Generic idea:

```text
retain user/project facts beyond one conversation
```

Ekairos adaptation:

```text
defer memory until compaction and rule activation are safe
if memory is later added, classify it as source with scope, authority, and staleness
memory claims require source lineage or explicit owner
```

Not adopted directly:

```text
memory as automatic policy
```

Reason:

```text
memory can pollute migration decisions if stale or cross-tenant
```

Implementation proposal:

```text
auto-memory caution and delayed design proposal
source reliability and recheck policy
tenant-scope rules
```

### Pattern: tool/action state preservation

Seen in:

```text
coding agents with tool calls
OpenCode processor loop
Claude Code agent loop
Codex agent loop
AI SDK tool call flows
```

Generic idea:

```text
tool/action continuity must survive context reduction
```

Ekairos adaptation:

```text
action requests and results are protected source classes when unresolved or recent
tool schema budget is counted separately
action execute context receives projection metadata
```

Not adopted directly:

```text
summarize pending action state as ordinary chat
```

Reason:

```text
tool/action state controls external effects
```

Implementation proposal:

```text
tool and action approval gate interaction
tool-schema budget and action surface control
engine insertion-point risk appendix
```

### Pattern: claim-preserving summaries

Seen in:

```text
academic context compression research
agent memory summaries
coding-agent compaction prompts
```

Generic idea:

```text
summaries should preserve decisions, facts, open tasks, and constraints
```

Ekairos adaptation:

```text
summary claims must be ledgered
claims must link to source packets
unsupported claims are rejected or blocked
source conflicts and stale claims are surfaced
```

Not adopted directly:

```text
freeform summary without evidence links
```

Reason:

```text
migration decisions need reconstructable evidence
```

Implementation proposal:

```text
source-link validation and claim ledger algorithm
claim ledger reviewer examples
context precision and recall supplement
```

### Mapping summary

Condensed mapping:

```text
automatic threshold compaction -> projection decision engine
provider-native compaction -> secondary provider artifact
context files/rules/memories -> source packet plus rule activation
retrieval-first IDE context -> retrieval provider source packets
repo maps -> structural source packets with anchors
visible compaction -> projection trace and operator report
checkpoint/restore -> immutable raw events plus derived projection lineage
model capability awareness -> provider capability registry
long-term memory -> delayed, scoped source plane
tool continuity -> protected action state and tool budget
claim-preserving summaries -> claim ledger
```

### Summary

The state-of-the-art pattern is not one mechanism.

It is a stack:

```text
retrieve relevant source
classify authority and scope
budget before dispatch
summarize only safe history
preserve tool/action continuity
surface compaction visibly
calibrate by provider capability
keep source lineage audit-ready
```

Ekairos should implement the stack through projection-ledger architecture, not through hidden chat summarization.

## Projection retention class matrix

Status: proposal only.

Projection and compaction artifacts have different retention needs.

Keeping everything forever is expensive and may be unsafe.

Deleting everything quickly breaks audit and migration reports.

This section proposes retention classes that can be reviewed before any schema or storage work is approved.

### Retention principles

Principles:

```text
raw durable event history remains the source of truth
projection artifacts are derived
source hashes can outlive model-visible text
secret-bearing raw material should not be duplicated into projection storage
migration evidence needs stronger retention than ordinary old chat summaries
blocked projection reports should remain inspectable
provider-native artifacts are secondary and may have provider retention limits
```

Retention should be decided by artifact class, source authority, tenant policy, and operational value.

### Retention class names

Proposed classes:

```text
ephemeral
short_lived
run_audit
migration_audit
incident_audit
source_reference_only
not_persisted
```

These names are proposal labels only.

### Class: ephemeral

Purpose:

```text
temporary calculation artifacts needed only during a projection attempt
```

Examples:

```text
intermediate token estimates
candidate ranking arrays
temporary selector scores
draft summary before validation
```

Retention:

```text
discard after projection attempt completes or fails
```

Model-visible:

```text
no
```

Audit-visible:

```text
only if promoted into a report field
```

Use for:

```text
implementation internals
```

Do not use for:

```text
blocked reason
source coverage
claim ledger
rendered input hash
```

### Class: short_lived

Purpose:

```text
debug artifacts useful for recent runs but not required long-term
```

Examples:

```text
raw rendered model input preview
temporary provider request metadata
debug-only selector traces
```

Retention:

```text
hours or days, depending on approved policy
```

Risks:

```text
may contain model-visible sensitive context
may duplicate source material
may increase storage cost
```

Approval required:

```text
whether this class exists at all
whether raw rendered input can be stored
whether redaction is mandatory before storage
```

Recommended default:

```text
avoid storing raw rendered input until a redaction and retention policy is approved
```

### Class: run_audit

Purpose:

```text
retain enough projection evidence to explain a normal run
```

Examples:

```text
projection id
status
budget ledger summary
source inclusion counts
rendered input hash
provider dispatch status
validation status
warnings
```

Retention:

```text
same as normal run trace retention
```

Model-visible:

```text
no, unless report text is rendered to the model in a later run
```

Audit-visible:

```text
yes
```

Use for:

```text
normal rendered projection
normal blocked projection
operator timeline
provider usage calibration
```

### Class: migration_audit

Purpose:

```text
retain projection evidence needed for migration reports and rollout decisions
```

Examples:

```text
schema plan source reference
org matrix source reference
dataset extract hash
transaction plan hash
verification result source reference
approval gate state
blocked migration projection report
```

Retention:

```text
longer than normal run traces, according to migration policy
```

Model-visible:

```text
only redacted summaries or references
```

Audit-visible:

```text
yes, with tenant-scoped access controls
```

Use for:

```text
domain/schema migrations
org-scoped rollout
canary expansion
migration incident review
```

Do not use for:

```text
raw secrets
full raw dataset duplication without approved storage policy
```

### Class: incident_audit

Purpose:

```text
retain evidence for projection failure, data exposure, or unsafe dispatch investigation
```

Examples:

```text
secret redaction failure report
tenant scope mismatch report
provider dispatch after blocked status if it ever occurs
source coverage gap
operator correction
```

Retention:

```text
incident policy, often longer and more restricted than normal traces
```

Access:

```text
restricted to authorized operators
```

Model-visible:

```text
no raw incident evidence by default
```

Use for:

```text
security review
post-incident analysis
audit report
```

### Class: source_reference_only

Purpose:

```text
retain references to large or sensitive source material without duplicating content
```

Examples:

```text
artifact id
content hash
record count
query metadata
source command
tenant scope
redaction state
storage pointer if approved
```

Retention:

```text
same as referenced source or migration audit report
```

Model-visible:

```text
reference packet only
```

Use for:

```text
large dataset extract
large command log
large unchanged query result
provider-native artifact pointer
```

Risk:

```text
reference without source availability can become useless
```

Required:

```text
source availability status
hash verification policy
```

### Class: not_persisted

Purpose:

```text
prevent persistence of content that should not be stored as projection artifact
```

Examples:

```text
raw credential
raw admin token
raw provider key
raw cookie
raw private key
unredacted secret-bearing output
```

Retention:

```text
none in projection storage
```

Model-visible:

```text
no
```

Audit-visible:

```text
only redaction event and safe metadata
```

Use for:

```text
secret-bearing raw material
```

### Retention matrix

Matrix:

```text
draft summary before validation: ephemeral
validated summary for normal run: run_audit
validated summary for migration run: migration_audit
blocked projection reason: run_audit or migration_audit
blocked projection with security concern: incident_audit
rendered input hash: run_audit
raw rendered input: short_lived only if approved
dataset extract hash: migration_audit or source_reference_only
raw dataset extract: source storage, not projection storage by default
redacted secret report: incident_audit or run_audit
raw secret-bearing output: not_persisted
provider-native compaction artifact id: source_reference_only
provider-native artifact payload: short_lived or source_reference_only only if approved
claim ledger for normal run: run_audit
claim ledger for migration run: migration_audit
```

### Access controls

Retention class should drive access:

```text
ephemeral: process-local
short_lived: restricted debug/operator
run_audit: run viewers with correct tenant scope
migration_audit: migration operators and technical leaders
incident_audit: restricted incident reviewers
source_reference_only: same as source artifact
not_persisted: no projection access
```

### Deletion rules

Deletion rules should define:

```text
when derived projection artifacts can be deleted
whether source hashes remain
whether operator reports remain
whether incident audit is exempt
whether migration audit has separate retention
```

Deleting a projection artifact should not delete durable raw event history unless a separate retention policy says so.

Deleting a raw source should mark projection references as unavailable.

### Schema implications

If retention becomes schema-backed, fields may include:

```text
retentionClass
expiresAt
sourceAvailability
redactionState
accessScope
contentHash
artifactRef
```

Schema work requires explicit approval.

Trace-only first slice can still record retention class in trace payload examples without adding new entities.

### Summary

Retention class is part of compaction safety.

The important question is not only:

```text
what did the model see
```

It is also:

```text
what evidence remains later
who can inspect it
what was intentionally not persisted
what source reference can still be resolved
```

## Approval gate matrix by workstream

Status: proposal only.

This matrix exists because the workspace rules require technical-leader approval for architecture, schema, config, infra, provider, release, and downstream validation decisions.

It is a control document, not an implementation plan.

### Gate categories

Gate categories:

```text
docs_only
orchestration_code
public_contract
schema
store
provider_adapter
config
runtime_workflow
ui
release
downstream_validation
```

Each workstream should name which gates it touches.

No workstream should start until its gate owner approves it.

### Gate: docs_only

Allowed without further implementation approval when user has asked for research:

```text
Markdown research
proposal matrices
source summaries
approval templates
future implementation ticket drafts
```

Not allowed:

```text
editing package source
editing schema
editing config
running release
deploying
provisioning credentials
```

```text
artifact path
audit scan
git status showing docs-only file
```
