### Workstream gate matrix

Matrix:

```text
projection contracts: public_contract, orchestration_code
source packet extraction: orchestration_code, store if persistent/query changes
budget ledger: orchestration_code, provider_adapter for usage calibration
decision engine: orchestration_code, public_contract
renderer: orchestration_code, provider_adapter, public_contract
trace-only reports: orchestration_code, runtime_workflow
manual summary artifact: orchestration_code, provider_adapter if model-generated
durable projection schema: schema, store, public_contract
operator report UI: ui, runtime_workflow
provider-native compaction: provider_adapter, config, provider source recheck
auto compaction: orchestration_code, config, runtime_workflow
release: release
downstream product validation: downstream_validation
```

### Approval packet format

Each proposed implementation slice should state:

```text
workstream
gate categories
files affected
entrypoints affected
schema impact
config impact
provider impact
runtime impact
ui impact
release impact
validation evidence
explicit out-of-scope gates
```

### Summary

The gate matrix prevents compaction from becoming an unbounded refactor.

The recommended discipline:

```text
approve one workstream
approve its gates
implement only inside those gates
stop when another gate is needed
return evidence
```

This matches the project rule that technical leadership owns architecture, config, schema, infra, and release decisions.

## Projection audit query recipes

Status: proposal only.

This section describes future audit questions and the data needed to answer them.

It does not define final schema.

It does not execute queries.

It gives reviewers a concrete checklist for deciding whether trace-only reports are enough or first-class projection entities are needed.

### Recipe format

Each recipe includes:

```text
audit question
required source data
expected answer shape
blocking interpretation
schema implication
```

### Recipe Q001: did the model get called

Audit question:

```text
did provider dispatch occur for this execution and iteration
```

Required source data:

```text
context id
execution id
step id
iteration
projection id
provider dispatch status
provider trace event if dispatched
```

Expected answer:

```text
yes with provider/model and usage
no because projection blocked
no because run failed before projection
unknown due missing trace
```

Blocking interpretation:

```text
if projection status is blocked and provider dispatch is yes, incident review is required
```

Schema implication:

```text
trace-only can answer if projection trace and provider trace share executionId/stepId/iteration
first-class projection entity makes answer faster and safer
```

### Recipe Q002: why was dispatch blocked

Audit question:

```text
which protected source blocked provider dispatch
```

Required source data:

```text
projection status
blocked reason
blocked source packet ids
source authority class
token estimate
operator report
```

Expected answer:

```text
blocked reason
source ids
source classes
budget fields
recommended operator action
```

Blocking interpretation:

```text
missing blocked source id means blocked report is not audit-grade
```

Schema implication:

```text
blocked source ids should be persisted or trace-recorded in structured form
```

### Recipe Q003: what did the model see

Audit question:

```text
which durable sources shaped the rendered model input
```

Required source data:

```text
projection manifest
rendered input hash
segment list
source packet ids
inclusion modes
summary artifact ids
reference artifact ids
```

Expected answer:

```text
full sources
summary sources
reference sources
omitted sources
not model-visible sources
rendered input hash
```

Blocking interpretation:

```text
if rendered input exists without source coverage, projection validation should fail
```

Schema implication:

```text
trace-only answer is possible but may be large
first-class segment/source entities improve queryability
```

### Recipe Q004: did current user remain literal

Audit question:

```text
was the newest controlling user instruction included literally
```

Required source data:

```text
current user source packet
segment inclusion mode
rendered span or rendered hash proof
validation result
```

Expected answer:

```text
literal included
literal not included and blocked
literal missing due validation failure
```

Blocking interpretation:

```text
current user not literal and dispatch occurred is critical failure
```

Schema implication:

```text
source packet authority class and validation flags need structured storage or trace fields
```

### Recipe Q005: did failed verification remain visible

Audit question:

```text
was failed migration verification evidence preserved
```

Required source data:

```text
verification result source packet
failure status
failed check name
expected count
actual count
segment inclusion mode
claim ledger entry
```

Expected answer:

```text
failed verification literal
failed verification blocked
failed verification summarized with sufficient exact fields
failure evidence missing
```

Blocking interpretation:

```text
failure evidence missing and dispatch occurred is critical failure
```

Schema implication:

```text
migration_audit retention class may be required
```

### Recipe Q006: was a secret exposed

Audit question:

```text
did raw secret-bearing content become model-visible or projection-persisted
```

Required source data:

```text
redaction classifier result
source packet redaction state
segment model visibility
rendered input scan result
projection retention class
```

Expected answer:

```text
raw secret not model-visible
redacted reference model-visible
raw secret blocked
raw secret exposure suspected
```

Blocking interpretation:

```text
raw secret exposure suspected requires incident audit
```

Schema implication:

```text
redaction state and not_persisted retention class should be structured
```

### Recipe Q007: were tenant boundaries respected

Audit question:

```text
did every included source match the execution tenant scope
```

Required source data:

```text
execution tenant scope
source packet tenant scope
retrieval query scope
claim ledger source ids
segment inclusion modes
```

Expected answer:

```text
all included sources match
forbidden sources excluded
tenant mismatch blocked
tenant scope unknown
```

Blocking interpretation:

```text
tenant scope unknown for private source should block migration/product runs
```

Schema implication:

```text
tenant scope belongs on source packets or source references
```

### Recipe Q008: did summary claims have evidence

Audit question:

```text
does each model-visible summary claim link to source evidence
```

Required source data:

```text
summary artifact
claim ledger
source packet ids
support level
validation status
```

Expected answer:

```text
all claims accepted
some claims accepted with caveat
unsupported claims rejected
blocked due unsupported high-risk claim
```

Blocking interpretation:

```text
unsupported high-risk claim in rendered input should block dispatch
```

Schema implication:

```text
claim ledger may need first-class persistence for audit-heavy workflows
```

### Recipe Q009: why was a source omitted

Audit question:

```text
which sources were omitted and why
```

Required source data:

```text
source packet list
inclusion mode
omission reason
authority class
claim dependency
```

Expected answer:

```text
safe low-authority omission
superseded source omitted
duplicate source omitted
omission needs manual review
invalid omission
```

Blocking interpretation:

```text
missing omission reason fails validation
```

Schema implication:

```text
omission reason should be structured on segment decision
```

### Recipe Q010: did provider-native compaction affect audit

Audit question:

```text
was a provider-native artifact used and what role did it play
```

Required source data:

```text
provider capability record
provider artifact id
local projection id
local source coverage
adapter trace
```

Expected answer:

```text
no provider-native artifact
provider artifact recorded as secondary
provider artifact unavailable
provider artifact incorrectly treated as primary
```

Blocking interpretation:

```text
provider artifact primary without local source coverage blocks migration audit
```

Schema implication:

```text
provider artifacts can be references linked to projection id
```

### Recipe Q011: which projection superseded another

Audit question:

```text
what is the lineage of projection artifacts across iterations
```

Required source data:

```text
projection id
iteration
superseded by
superseded reason
rendered input hash
action result source packet
```

Expected answer:

```text
linear lineage
branch or retry lineage
missing successor
orphan projection
```

Blocking interpretation:

```text
orphan projection is not necessarily unsafe, but migration report should not cite superseded projection as current
```

Schema implication:

```text
projection lineage benefits from first-class projection records
```

### Recipe Q012: what changed after provider usage calibration

Audit question:

```text
did provider usage telemetry update future budget estimates
```

Required source data:

```text
local token estimate
provider prompt tokens
provider total tokens
cached prompt tokens
uncached prompt tokens
model profile
estimate error
```

Expected answer:

```text
estimate error recorded
calibration bucket updated
usage missing
usage redacted or unavailable
```

Blocking interpretation:

```text
missing usage does not block dispatch by itself, but repeated unknown usage should raise calibration warning
```

Schema implication:

```text
usage telemetry can remain in trace or llm fields unless long-term calibration is required
```

### Recipe Q013: was release validation honest

Audit question:

```text
do release notes match actual validation evidence
```

Required source data:

```text
test command results
schema dry-run evidence
provider recheck packet
downstream validation packet
known gaps
release note draft
```

Expected answer:

```text
release notes match evidence
release notes overstate validation
release notes omit known gap
release notes omit breaking behavior
```

Blocking interpretation:

```text
release notes overstate validation should block release
```

Schema implication:

```text
not a package schema issue, but release artifacts should reference validation evidence
```

### Trace-only feasibility

Trace-only can answer:

```text
did projection block
did provider dispatch
what reason blocked
basic budget ledger
basic source counts
basic validation status
```

Trace-only struggles with:

```text
large segment/source queryability
claim ledger review across many runs
recursive projection lineage
migration audit joins
retention policies by artifact
```

This supports a staged approach:

```text
first trace-only reports
then first-class projection entities if audit queries prove valuable
```

### Summary

The audit recipes define what "auditable compaction" means in practice.

An implementation is not audit-grade merely because it stores a summary.

It is audit-grade when an operator can answer:

```text
what was included
what was reduced
what was excluded
why the model was or was not called
which source evidence supports each important claim
```

## Redaction classifier policy table

Status: proposal only.

Compaction cannot be safe if redaction is vague.

This table defines how a future projection system should classify secret-bearing or sensitive content before model rendering.

It does not implement detection.

It defines expected behavior for review.

### Classifier goals

The classifier should decide:

```text
can this source be model-visible
can this source be summarized
can this source be referenced
can this source be stored as projection artifact
does this source require incident handling
```

The classifier should not decide:

```text
whether provider dispatch is useful
whether a migration should continue
whether a credential is valid
```

Those decisions belong to projection validation and operator approval.

### Redaction states

Proposed redaction states:

```text
none_detected
suspected_secret
confirmed_secret
redacted
redaction_failed
not_model_visible
not_persisted
manual_review_required
```

State transitions:

```text
none_detected -> redacted only if later classifier finds sensitive span
suspected_secret -> redacted or manual_review_required
confirmed_secret -> redacted or not_model_visible
redaction_failed -> blocked
not_persisted -> safe metadata only
```

### Sensitive source classes

Source classes:

```text
api_key
admin_token
session_cookie
private_key
oauth_token
database_url
webhook_secret
personal_access_token
provider_credential
clerk_secret
instant_admin_token
raw_auth_header
tenant_private_record
personal_data
commercial_sensitive_data
unknown_sensitive_blob
```

Each class should have:

```text
modelVisibility
summaryAllowed
referenceAllowed
persistRawAllowed
requiresIncidentIfRendered
```

### Policy: API key

Model visibility:

```text
no raw value
```

Summary allowed:

```text
only as redacted fact
```

Reference allowed:

```text
yes, with redacted hash or safe artifact id
```

Persist raw projection artifact:

```text
no
```

If raw value appears in rendered input:

```text
critical incident
```

Allowed rendering:

```text
An API key-like value was present and redacted.
```

### Policy: admin token

Model visibility:

```text
no raw value
```

Summary allowed:

```text
only status and scope, never value
```

Reference allowed:

```text
yes, safe metadata only
```

Persist raw projection artifact:

```text
no
```

Allowed rendering:

```text
Admin runtime resolved for the current app; token value is not model-visible.
```

Blocked rendering:

```text
any raw admin token
```

### Policy: session cookie

Model visibility:

```text
no raw value
```

Summary allowed:

```text
yes, as redacted diagnostic only
```

Reference allowed:

```text
yes, with source id and redaction status
```

Persist raw projection artifact:

```text
no
```

If required for debugging:

```text
operator must inspect secure source outside model context
```

### Policy: private key

Model visibility:

```text
no
```

Summary allowed:

```text
only state that private key material was detected
```

Reference allowed:

```text
safe metadata only
```

Persist raw projection artifact:

```text
no
```

Dispatch rule:

```text
block if redaction cannot prove raw key material is absent from rendered input
```

### Policy: database URL

Model visibility:

```text
no raw credential-bearing URL
```

Summary allowed:

```text
redacted host/classification only if approved
```

Reference allowed:

```text
yes, with redacted form
```

Persist raw projection artifact:

```text
no
```

Allowed rendering:

```text
Database connection string was detected and redacted.
```

### Policy: tenant private record

Model visibility:

```text
only if tenant scope matches and data is needed
```

Summary allowed:

```text
only within matching tenant scope
```

Reference allowed:

```text
yes, tenant-scoped source reference
```

Persist raw projection artifact:

```text
only according to tenant data retention policy
```

Blocked condition:

```text
tenant scope unknown or mismatched
```

### Policy: personal data

Model visibility:

```text
only if approved by product/security policy and required for the task
```

Summary allowed:

```text
prefer aggregate or redacted summary
```

Reference allowed:

```text
yes, with access controls
```

Persist raw projection artifact:

```text
only under approved retention class
```

Operator report:

```text
state that personal data was included, redacted, referenced, or excluded
```

### Policy: unknown sensitive blob

Model visibility:

```text
no until classified
```

Summary allowed:

```text
no
```

Reference allowed:

```text
metadata only
```

Persist raw projection artifact:

```text
no
```

Dispatch rule:

```text
block if blob is relevant and cannot be classified safely
```

### Redaction validation checks

Validation checks:

```text
raw flagged spans absent from rendered input
raw flagged spans absent from summary text
raw flagged spans absent from operator copy
raw flagged spans absent from persisted projection artifact
redaction state present on source packet
reference packet states redacted or not_model_visible
claim ledger does not cite raw secret as model-visible evidence
```

### Redaction trace fields

Trace/report fields:

```text
redactionState
redactionClass
sourcePacketId
rawModelVisible
rawPersisted
redactedArtifactRef
classifierConfidence
manualReviewRequired
incidentRequired
```

Do not log:

```text
raw secret span
raw credential value
full sensitive payload
```

### Redaction and summaries

Summary prompt should receive:

```text
redacted source text
redaction metadata
allowed diagnostic facts
forbidden raw spans removed before model call
```

Summary prompt should not receive:

```text
raw secret plus instruction to hide it
```

Reason:

```text
the model must not see the raw secret at all
```

### Redaction and references

Reference packet should include:

```text
source id
artifact class
redaction state
safe hash if approved
safe diagnostic excerpt
model visibility status
```

Reference packet should not include:

```text
raw secret
raw secret-derived substring that can reconstruct the value
```

### Redaction and blocked projection

Block when:

```text
redaction failed
classifier is uncertain for relevant sensitive source
raw secret appears in rendered input
tenant-private source scope is unknown
manual review is required and not complete
```

Allowed to proceed when:

```text
raw sensitive source is excluded
redacted reference is safe
validation scan passes
operator report records redaction state
```

### Summary

The redaction policy is simple:

```text
never ask the model to keep a raw secret secret
```

Redact before projection rendering, validate after rendering, and block if validation cannot prove the raw sensitive content stayed out.

## Technical-leader sign-off sequence

Status: proposal only.

This section turns the approval templates and gate matrix into a review sequence.

It is designed for a technical leader who wants to approve or reject implementation slices without letting the research document make architectural decisions by itself.

### Sign-off principle

The sign-off sequence should approve:

```text
one architectural decision
one implementation slice
one gate set
one validation packet
```

It should not approve:

```text
general compaction
provider-native behavior broadly
schema changes by implication
config changes by implication
release by implication
downstream validation by implication
```

### Step 1: choose proposal family

Decision:

```text
projection-ledger architecture
provider-native-first architecture
retrieval-only architecture
manual-summary-only architecture
no implementation
```

Recommended selection from this research:

```text
projection-ledger architecture
```

Why:

```text
it matches durable events, migration audit, source links, and blocked safety behavior
```

Sign-off output:

```text
accepted proposal family
rejected proposal families
reason for rejection
```

### Step 2: choose first slice

Candidate first slices:

```text
contracts only
source packet extractor
budget ledger
decision engine
trace-only report
manual summary artifact
durable schema
provider-native adapter
```

Recommended first slice:

```text
contracts plus source packet classification plus budget ledger tests
```

Rationale:

```text
it establishes policy vocabulary before changing provider dispatch
```

Sign-off output:

```text
slice name
files allowed
files forbidden
tests required
schema impact
provider impact
config impact
```

### Step 3: decide public contract break

Questions:

```text
will ContextReactorParams change in the first approved slice
will projection types be public
which entrypoint exports them
will old reactor params be removed rather than bridged
```

Recommended direction:

```text
approve explicit breaking contract when reactor integration slice begins
keep first contracts slice internal or clearly experimental if no reactor behavior changes
```

Sign-off output:

```text
contract break approved yes/no
entrypoints affected
migration guide required yes/no
release note required yes/no
```

### Step 4: decide blocked projection semantics

Questions:

```text
is blocked projection a run state
is blocked projection a step state
does execution fail or complete with blocked state
does UI show an engine message
does provider dispatch remain impossible after blocked validation
```

Recommended direction:

```text
blocked projection is a first-class non-provider state
provider dispatch does not occur
operator report explains blocked reason
```

Sign-off output:

```text
blocked state model
trace event names
UI copy requirement
test fixture requirement
```

### Step 5: decide schema timing

Questions:

```text
should first implementation be trace-only
should projection entities be added immediately
which retention classes are required
is claim ledger first-class
is source packet first-class
```

Recommended direction:

```text
first implementation trace-only unless the technical leader wants durable queryability immediately
```

Sign-off output:

```text
schema change approved yes/no
planSchemaPush required yes/no
migration report required yes/no
entities approved
entities rejected
```

### Step 6: decide provider-native timing

Questions:

```text
is provider-native compaction in scope
which providers
which models
what source recheck is required
what role does provider artifact play
```

Recommended direction:

```text
exclude provider-native compaction from the first implementation
evaluate provider-native artifacts only after local projection ledger works
```

Sign-off output:

```text
provider-native in scope yes/no
provider recheck packet required
capability records required
adapter acceptance checklist required
```

### Step 7: decide auto compaction timing

Questions:

```text
manual only or automatic
threshold
cooldown
blocked cases
operator override
```

Recommended direction:

```text
manual or deterministic projection first
auto trigger only after blocked/report/summary validation passes
```

Sign-off output:

```text
auto compaction in scope yes/no
threshold approved if yes
manual trigger behavior
test fixtures required
```

### Step 8: decide tool schema budget behavior

Questions:

```text
are tool schemas counted in first budget ledger
can tool surface be reduced
which tools are required
does required tool omission block
```

Recommended direction:

```text
count tool schemas from first budget ledger
reduce only optional tool surface
block if required tool plus protected context cannot fit
```

Sign-off output:

```text
tool schema budget required yes/no
tool reduction policy
required tool policy
```

### Step 9: decide migration evidence policy

Questions:

```text
which migration artifacts are protected
which artifacts may be referenced
which verification failures must remain literal
which retention class applies
```

Recommended direction:

```text
protect schema dry-run status, org matrix, failed verification, destructive transaction plan, and approval gate
reference large dataset extracts by hash
```

Sign-off output:

```text
protected artifact classes
reference artifact classes
blocked artifact classes
retention classes
```

### Step 10: decide redaction policy

Questions:

```text
which detector/classifier is acceptable
what classes block dispatch
what can be redacted
what cannot be persisted
what incident evidence is required
```

Recommended direction:

```text
raw secrets are never model-visible
redaction failure blocks dispatch
not_persisted class for raw credential values
```

Sign-off output:

```text
redaction classes
blocked states
retention policy
incident path
```

### Step 11: decide UI/report scope

Questions:

```text
is operator report required in first slice
is React UI changed
which copy strings are approved
how blocked projection appears
```

Recommended direction:

```text
report fixture required before UI
UI changes only after report shape stabilizes
```

Sign-off output:

```text
operator report required yes/no
UI files allowed yes/no
copy approved
screenshot/manual QA required if UI changes
```

### Step 12: decide release and downstream validation

Questions:

```text
is package release intended
which channel
is downstream validation mandatory
will test credentials be provisioned
will deploy be inspected
```

Recommended direction:

```text
no release until implementation and tests are complete
downstream validation packet required for product-facing behavior
```

Sign-off output:

```text
release approved yes/no
release channel
downstream validation required yes/no
credentials policy
deploy inspection policy
```

### One-page sign-off record

A final sign-off record should contain:

```text
approved proposal family
approved first slice
approved files
forbidden files
public contract impact
schema impact
provider impact
config impact
runtime impact
ui impact
test requirements
release status
downstream validation status
```

### Example sign-off for smallest slice

Example:

```text
proposal family: projection-ledger
first slice: projection contracts plus source packet classifier plus budget ledger tests
files allowed: contract/projection helper files only
files forbidden: schema, provider adapters, runtime workflow, React UI, package config
public contract: no root export until reviewed
schema impact: none
provider impact: none
config impact: none
runtime impact: none
tests: unit fixtures for source classes and budget decisions
release: no
downstream validation: no
```

### Example sign-off for reactor integration slice

Example:

```text
proposal family: projection-ledger
slice: engine projection before reactor invocation
files allowed: context engine, reactor types, scripted reactor tests, AI SDK reactor tests
public contract: ContextReactorParams breaking change approved
schema impact: none
provider impact: AI SDK reactor consumes rendered projection input
config impact: none
runtime impact: blocked projection trace
tests: blocked projection prevents reactor call, rendered projection reaches reactor
release: no until migration guide and release notes are approved
downstream validation: not yet
```

### Summary

The sign-off sequence turns a large architecture proposal into small approvals.

The key control is:

```text
no slice may silently cross into a gate the technical leader did not approve
```

The first approved slice should not need every test group.

It should need the groups that match its gates:

```text
contracts slice -> contract, source packet, budget tests
engine slice -> decision, renderer, engine insertion, scripted reactor tests
provider slice -> AI SDK reactor and provider capability tests
schema slice -> schema/store tests plus migration report
UI slice -> React/operator state tests
```

## Terminology distinction matrix

Status: proposal only.

This matrix separates terms that are often blended in agent systems.

Ekairos should keep them distinct because each mechanism has different audit, safety, and implementation implications.

### Term: projection

Definition:

```text
the model-facing view derived from durable context and source packets for one run or iteration
```

Primary question:

```text
what should the model see now
```

Ekairos role:

```text
core architecture concept
```

Can include:

```text
literal source
summary
reference
omission note
blocked source
budget ledger
claim ledger
```

Must record:

```text
source coverage
inclusion mode
validation status
rendered input hash
```

Should not:

```text
mutate durable event history
replace source records
```

### Term: compaction

Definition:

```text
reducing context size while preserving task-relevant information
```

Primary question:

```text
how can model-visible context fit within budget
```

Ekairos role:

```text
one mechanism inside projection
```

Can include:

```text
summary
reference packet
tool surface reduction
safe omission
```

Must record:

```text
what was reduced
why it was reduced
source links
validation result
```

Should not:

```text
hide approvals
hide verification failures
delete durable event parts
```

### Term: summarization

Definition:

```text
producing shorter text that represents source material
```

Primary question:

```text
what claims survive from the source
```

Ekairos role:

```text
allowed only for summaryAllowed sources after validation
```

Can include:

```text
decisions
constraints
open questions
rejected options
recent progress
```

Must record:

```text
summary artifact id
source packet ids
claim ledger
validation status
prompt version if model-generated
```

Should not:

```text
summarize current user instruction
summarize raw secrets
summarize unresolved approval as ordinary history
```

### Term: pruning

Definition:

```text
dropping source material from model-visible context
```

Primary question:

```text
what can be safely omitted
```

Ekairos role:

```text
allowed only with explicit omission reason
```

Can include:

```text
duplicate sources
superseded old exploration
low-authority irrelevant context
large success logs with counts preserved elsewhere
```

Must record:

```text
omitted source id
omission reason
authority class
whether claim ledger depends on source
```

Should not:

```text
drop high-risk evidence
drop current user instruction
drop failed verification
drop unresolved action state
```

### Term: retrieval

Definition:

```text
fetching or selecting external/local source material relevant to the current task
```

Primary question:

```text
what source should be considered
```

Ekairos role:

```text
input to projection, not a replacement for projection
```

Can include:

```text
local file anchors
domain records
schema docs
provider docs
repo maps
codemaps
```

Must record:

```text
retrieval scope
tenant scope
source timestamp
staleness state
authority class
```

Should not:

```text
treat retrieved source as current fact without validation
cross tenant boundaries
```

### Term: memory

Definition:

```text
persistent facts or preferences retained beyond one run
```

Primary question:

```text
what should the system remember later
```

Ekairos role:

```text
out of first compaction slice unless separately approved
```

Can include:

```text
user preference
project rule
long-term fact
organization policy
```

Must record if added:

```text
scope
owner
source
staleness
authority
revocation path
```

Should not:

```text
be silently created from summaries
override current user instruction
cross tenant boundaries
```

### Term: rule activation

Definition:

```text
selecting which instructions or policies apply to the current run
```

Primary question:

```text
which rules are active now and why
```

Ekairos role:

```text
separate plane from compaction
```

Can include:

```text
workspace rule
project rule
technical-leader constraint
domain migration policy
provider recheck policy
```

Must record:

```text
rule id
activation reason
source
priority
scope
```

Should not:

```text
be buried inside a summary
```

### Term: caching

Definition:

```text
reusing previously computed or provider-cached input/output for cost or latency
```

Primary question:

```text
can repeated context be reused efficiently
```

Ekairos role:

```text
performance/cost feature, not source authority
```

Can include:

```text
prompt cache
projection artifact cache
retrieval cache
provider cache metadata
```

Must record:

```text
cache key
cache scope
cache hit/miss if available
invalidated state
```

Should not:

```text
treat cache hit as validation
override source staleness
```

### Term: provider conversation state

Definition:

```text
state stored or referenced by a provider across calls
```

Primary question:

```text
what context does the provider carry forward
```

Ekairos role:

```text
secondary provider artifact only unless explicitly approved
```

Can include:

```text
response id
conversation id
compacted provider state
provider cache state
```

Must record:

```text
provider
artifact id
scope
retention caveat
local projection id
```

Should not:

```text
replace durable event history
replace local projection manifest
```

### Term: source packet

Definition:

```text
classified source unit considered by projection
```

Primary question:

```text
what is this source and what authority does it have
```

Ekairos role:

```text
core input to projection
```

Can represent:

```text
event part
trace event
tool output
retrieved file
dataset artifact
provider docs
approval state
```

Must record:

```text
source id
authority class
tenant scope
visibility
token estimate
redaction state
staleness
```

Should not:

```text
be untyped raw text
```

### Term: artifact reference

Definition:

```text
compact pointer to large or restricted source material
```

Primary question:

```text
where is the durable evidence and how can it be verified
```

Ekairos role:

```text
preferred representation for large migration/data artifacts
```

Can include:

```text
artifact id
content hash
record count
redaction state
source command
tenant scope
```

Must record:

```text
hash policy
source availability
retention class
model visibility
```

Should not:

```text
be vague placeholder text
```

### Distinction table

Matrix:

```text
projection: selects model-facing view
compaction: reduces size inside projection
summarization: creates shorter text
pruning: omits source with reason
retrieval: adds candidate source
memory: persists facts for future
rule activation: selects active instructions
caching: reuses computation or provider state
provider conversation state: provider-held continuation artifact
source packet: classified source input
artifact reference: compact pointer to durable evidence
```

### Common confusion cases

Confusion:

```text
retrieval is not compaction
```

Correction:

```text
retrieval increases candidate source set; projection then budgets/selects
```

Confusion:

```text
summary is not memory
```

Correction:

```text
summary helps current projection; memory persists future facts with separate approval
```

Confusion:

```text
provider cache is not omission
```

Correction:

```text
cached context can still be model-visible; it only changes cost/latency
```

Confusion:

```text
provider conversation state is not audit source
```

Correction:

```text
local durable events and projection manifest remain authority
```

### Summary

Keeping these terms separate prevents design drift.

Ekairos should talk in this order:

```text
source packets are gathered
rules are activated
projection selects model-visible view
compaction reduces safe parts if needed
summaries and references are validated
provider dispatch happens only if projection passes
memory and caching remain separate mechanisms
```

## Future implementation code review checklist

Status: proposal only.

This checklist is for a future implementation PR.

It should be used in code-review mode, where findings lead and summaries are secondary.

No implementation exists in this research artifact.

### Review stance

Review should prioritize:

```text
incorrect model-visible context
unsafe dispatch
source lineage gaps
tenant leaks
secret exposure
approval gate bypass
contract breaks not documented
missing tests for touched behavior
```

Review should not focus first on:

```text
minor naming preferences
formatting style if formatter handles it
unrelated refactors
future features outside approved slice
```

### Scope check

Ask first:

```text
does the diff stay inside approved files
does the diff touch schema
does the diff touch config
does the diff touch provider adapters
does the diff touch runtime workflow
does the diff touch UI
does the diff touch release metadata
```

Finding if scope is wrong:

```text
implementation crosses an unapproved gate
```

Severity:

```text
high or critical depending on gate
```

### Contract review

Check:

```text
ContextReactorParams changes are deliberate
public entrypoint exports match approval
old contract is removed if breaking change approved
no hidden adapter layer preserves old behavior without approval
type tests cover new contract
consumer migration guide matches actual break
```

Potential findings:

```text
custom reactors can compile but receive no projection metadata
blocked projection state cannot be represented in public types
root export leaks unstable internal type
release notes omit public contract break
```

### Engine insertion review

Check:

```text
projection runs after expandEvents
projection runs before reactor invocation
blocked projection prevents reactor call
projection validation result is checked before dispatch
projection id flows to trace/report
action execution receives correct rendered message hash if approved
```

Potential findings:

```text
reactor still rebuilds model messages from raw events
projection validates after provider dispatch
blocked state still calls provider
expanded sources bypass projection
```

### Source packet review

Check:

```text
source packets include source ids
authority class is assigned
tenant scope is assigned where relevant
redaction state is assigned
staleness is assigned for external/retrieved sources
token estimate exists or unknown estimate blocks as approved
```

Potential findings:

```text
current user source is not literalRequired
failed verification source is summaryAllowed without literal requirement
tenant source has unknown scope but is included
retrieved provider docs lack recheck metadata
```

### Budget review

Check:

```text
response reserve is counted
estimate error reserve is counted
tool schema budget is counted
protected content is calculated separately
unknown model window blocks or uses approved fallback
budget ledger is emitted
```

Potential findings:

```text
tool schemas omitted from budget
response reserve consumed by old history
unknown model treated as unlimited
estimate error not recorded after provider usage
```

### Renderer review

Check:

```text
current user remains literal
protected sources remain literal or block
summary sources include source links
reference packets include hash/artifact metadata
not_model_visible sources are excluded
rendered input hash is stable
```

Potential findings:

```text
summary includes raw secret
reference packet has no source id
omitted source has no reason
rendered messages include source from wrong tenant
```

### Claim ledger review

Check:

```text
model-visible claims have source ids
unsupported claims are rejected or blocked
contradicted claims are labeled
stale claims have caveats
rejected options remain rejected
```

Potential findings:

```text
summary claim has no evidence
old rejected design becomes active decision
latest failure contradicted by old success note but old success wins
```

### Redaction review

Check:

```text
redaction classification happens before rendering
raw secret is not sent to model
raw secret is not persisted as projection artifact
redacted reference is safe
redaction failure blocks dispatch
```

Potential findings:

```text
model receives raw sensitive source and is asked to ignore it
operator report includes raw secret
redaction failure logs raw payload
```

### Tenant-scope review

Check:

```text
source packet tenant scope exists
retrieval queries include tenant filters
claim ledger source ids match execution scope
other-tenant source is excluded or blocks
```

Potential findings:

```text
projection includes another org source
tenant scope unknown but source included
summary merges same-named projects across orgs
```

### Provider adapter review

Check:

```text
adapter consumes approved rendered messages
adapter does not own projection policy
provider-native artifact is secondary
usage telemetry maps to projection id
provider capability record is used
```

Potential findings:

```text
adapter silently truncates messages
adapter calls native compaction without local projection manifest
provider artifact replaces source coverage
usage telemetry cannot calibrate estimates
```

### Runtime and trace review

Check:

```text
projection planned/rendered/blocked trace is emitted
blocked state is not provider failure
step/execution status matches approved state model
stream timeline is coherent
operator report can be reconstructed
```

Potential findings:

```text
blocked projection appears as model error
projection trace missing when provider dispatch occurs
stream says model called when dispatch did not happen
```

### UI review

Only if UI gate approved.

Check:

```text
blocked reason visible
model dispatched yes/no visible
source coverage counts visible
operator copy matches approved catalog
text does not imply full history was sent
```

Potential findings:

```text
UI says provider failed for blocked projection
UI hides source omissions
UI omits redaction warning
```

### Schema/store review

Only if schema/store gates approved.

Check:

```text
planSchemaPush evidence exists
entities match approved data model
retention classes represented
tenant-scoped queries exist
source/segment/claim joins are possible
```

Potential findings:

```text
projection entity stores raw secret
source segments cannot be queried by context
claim ledger lacks source relation
retention class missing
```

### Test review

Check tests for:

```text
current user literal
unresolved approval block
failed verification literal
secret redaction
tenant mismatch
tool schema budget
provider dispatch false when blocked
source coverage required
claim ledger unsupported claim
rejected option preservation
```

Finding if missing:

```text
approved behavior lacks regression coverage
```

Severity:

```text
high for safety behavior
medium for reporting behavior
```

### Release review

Only if release gate approved.

Check:

```text
release notes state breaking changes
known gaps are explicit
test commands are listed
provider recheck status is current
downstream validation status is honest
```

Potential findings:

```text
release notes say validated without downstream packet
provider docs stale but provider feature claimed current
schema changes omitted from notes
```

### Review output format

Findings should be written as:

```text
severity
file and line
observed behavior
risk
required correction or decision
```

Example:

```text
High: Reactor dispatch still occurs when projection validation returns blocked. This violates the blocked projection contract and can send protected unresolved approval context to the provider. The engine should return blocked state before reactor invocation or the technical leader must reject blocked-state semantics.
```

### Summary

Future implementation review should ask:

```text
did the code preserve operational truth under context pressure
```

If the answer is uncertain, the PR is not ready.

## Projection metrics field dictionary

Status: proposal only.

This dictionary defines metrics and fields that should exist in traces, reports, or dashboards if implementation is approved.

It does not define final telemetry schema.

It makes field meanings explicit before instrumentation is added.

### Metric naming principles

Metric names should be:

```text
specific
stable
provider-neutral when possible
linked to projection id
safe to aggregate
clear about estimate versus reported usage
```

Metric names should not:

```text
hide provider-specific behavior
mix input and output artifacts
store raw prompt text
store raw secrets
```

### Identity fields

Fields:

```text
projectionId
contextId
executionId
stepId
iteration
eventId
modelProvider
modelId
modelProfileId
```

Purpose:

```text
join projection records, provider traces, stream events, and operator reports
```

Rules:

```text
projectionId should be present on projection trace/report events
executionId and stepId should be present when available
modelId should not imply capability unless registry confirms it
```

### Projection status fields

Fields:

```text
projectionStatus
projectionStrategy
validationStatus
blockedReason
providerDispatchAllowed
providerDispatched
```

Allowed status examples:

```text
planned
rendered
blocked
validation_failed
provider_dispatched
superseded
```

Purpose:

```text
distinguish safe rendered projections from blocked or failed projections
```

Rules:

```text
providerDispatched must be false when projectionStatus is blocked
blockedReason required when blocked
```

### Source count fields

Fields:

```text
sourcePacketCount
includedSourceCount
fullSourceCount
summarySourceCount
referenceSourceCount
omittedSourceCount
blockedSourceCount
notModelVisibleSourceCount
secretSourceCount
tenantScopedSourceCount
staleSourceCount
```

Purpose:

```text
show what happened to source material
```

Rules:

```text
counts should sum to sourcePacketCount or explain multi-class overlap
secretSourceCount should not reveal raw secret content
```

### Budget fields

Fields:

```text
modelWindowTokens
projectedInputTokens
requiredResponseReserveTokens
estimateErrorReserveTokens
estimatedSystemTokens
estimatedCurrentUserTokens
estimatedLiteralTailTokens
estimatedSummaryTokens
estimatedReferenceTokens
estimatedRetrievedSourceTokens
estimatedActionContinuityTokens
estimatedToolSchemaTokens
estimatedProviderOverheadTokens
```

Purpose:

```text
make projection budget decisions reviewable
```

Rules:

```text
estimated fields should be labeled as estimates
unknown estimates should be explicit
tool schema tokens should not be hidden inside history tokens
```

### Provider usage fields

Fields:

```text
providerPromptTokens
providerPromptTokensCached
providerPromptTokensUncached
providerCompletionTokens
providerTotalTokens
providerLatencyMs
rawUsagePresent
rawProviderMetadataPresent
```

Purpose:

```text
calibrate local estimates and track provider behavior
```

Rules:

```text
raw provider metadata should be redacted or omitted if sensitive
missing usage should be recorded as unavailable, not zero
```

### Estimate calibration fields

Fields:

```text
estimateErrorTokens
estimateErrorRate
calibrationBucket
calibrationSampleCount
calibrationUpdated
```

Purpose:

```text
improve future budget estimates
```

Rules:

```text
estimateErrorTokens = providerPromptTokens - projectedInputTokens when comparable
do not calculate error if provider usage is unavailable or incomparable
```

### Summary quality fields

Fields:

```text
summaryArtifactCount
summaryPromptVersion
summarySourceCount
summaryClaimCount
summaryUnsupportedClaimCount
summaryContradictedClaimCount
summaryValidationStatus
```

Purpose:

```text
detect summary drift and unsupported claims
```

Rules:

```text
unsupported high-risk claims should block
summaryPromptVersion required for model-generated summaries
```

### Claim ledger fields

Fields:

```text
claimCount
acceptedClaimCount
acceptedWithCaveatClaimCount
rejectedClaimCount
blockedClaimCount
unsupportedClaimCount
contradictedClaimCount
staleClaimCount
manualReviewClaimCount
```

Purpose:

```text
surface claim quality without exposing raw source content
```

Rules:

```text
claim counts are not enough for high-risk review; source ids remain needed
```

### Redaction fields

Fields:

```text
redactionSourceCount
redactionWarningCount
redactionFailureCount
rawSecretModelVisible
rawSecretPersisted
manualRedactionReviewRequired
```

Purpose:

```text
prove secret-bearing sources were handled safely
```

Rules:

```text
rawSecretModelVisible true is critical incident
rawSecretPersisted true is critical incident unless explicitly approved secure storage outside projection
```

### Tenant fields

Fields:

```text
executionTenantScope
sourceTenantScopeCount
tenantMismatchCount
tenantScopeUnknownCount
crossTenantSourceBlocked
```

Purpose:

```text
detect tenant boundary failures
```

Rules:

```text
tenantMismatchCount greater than zero should block when private source is involved
```

### Tool/action fields

Fields:

```text
availableToolCount
exposedToolCount
omittedToolCount
requiredToolCount
toolSchemaTokenEstimate
actionRequestCount
pendingActionCount
failedActionCount
approvalRequiredActionCount
```

Purpose:

```text
make tool surface and action continuity visible
```

Rules:

```text
required tool omission should block
approvalRequiredActionCount should affect protected source budget
```

### Provider artifact fields

Fields:

```text
providerArtifactCount
providerNativeCompactionUsed
providerArtifactRole
providerArtifactIdPresent
providerArtifactReplayable
providerArtifactRetained
```

Purpose:

```text
track provider-native compaction or provider conversation state without making it authority
```

Rules:

```text
providerArtifactRole should be secondary unless separately approved
```

### Operator report fields

Fields:

```text
operatorReportPresent
operatorReportVersion
operatorActionRequired
operatorActionKind
manualReviewRequired
knownGapCount
```

Purpose:

```text
make operator readiness measurable
```

Rules:

```text
blocked projection should have operatorActionRequired true
known gaps should be explicit for release/deploy review
```

### Dashboard slices

Potential dashboard dimensions:

```text
provider
model
projectionStatus
blockedReason
tenantScope
workflow type
source authority class
retention class
summary prompt version
release version
```

Potential dashboard questions:

```text
how often does projection block
which blocked reasons dominate
how often are secrets detected
how often are tenant mismatches blocked
which models have high estimate error
how often provider-native artifacts are recorded
how many migration runs reference dataset extracts
```

### Alert candidates

Alert on:

```text
rawSecretModelVisible true
tenantMismatchCount greater than zero with providerDispatchAllowed true
blocked projection followed by provider dispatch
unsupported high-risk claim rendered
estimate error above approved threshold repeatedly
provider-native artifact primary without local source coverage
```

### Summary

Metrics should make projection behavior observable without leaking sensitive content.

The minimum useful dashboard answers:

```text
how often did projection render
how often did it block
why did it block
how accurate were token estimates
did any high-risk validation fail
```

## Rollout gate decision table

Status: proposal only.

This table defines rollout gates for a future approved implementation and release.

It does not approve release, branch creation, push, deploy, downstream validation, or credentials.

### Rollout stages

Proposed stages:

```text
research
implementation slice
package test
schema dry-run if schema changed
beta package release
consumer update
preview validation
canary organization
expanded canary
production rollout
post-rollout audit
```

Only research is happening in this task.

### Stage: research

Gate objective:

```text
produce source-backed proposals and approval material
```

Required evidence:

```text
research artifact
source catalog
local code anchors
proposal set
approval gates
timer satisfied
artifact audit clean
```

Blocked if:

```text
five-hour goal not satisfied
artifact audit fails
technical-leader asks to stop
```

Current status:

```text
active
```

### Stage: implementation slice

Gate objective:

```text
make one approved code change inside approved gates
```

Required evidence:

```text
technical-leader sign-off
approved files
approved out-of-scope gates
tests for touched behavior
diff review
```

Blocked if:

```text
approval missing
implementation touches unapproved schema/config/provider/UI/release gate
tests for safety behavior missing
```

### Stage: package test

Gate objective:

```text
prove package-level behavior
```

Required evidence:

```text
typecheck
typecheck tests
unit tests
reactor tests if touched
workflow tests if touched
real provider tests only if approved and required
```

Blocked if:

```text
critical fixture fails
blocked projection still dispatches provider
secret or tenant test fails
```

### Stage: schema dry-run

Applies when:

```text
schema gate approved and schema file changed
```

Gate objective:

```text
prove proposed domain/schema changes can be planned safely
```

Required evidence:

```text
planSchemaPush output
entity diff
index/relation diff
migration report
tenant query examples
rollback or forward-fix plan
```

Blocked if:

```text
schema dry-run missing
tenant scope query not demonstrated
retention fields missing for durable projection entities
```

### Stage: beta package release

Gate objective:

```text
publish approved package version for downstream validation
```

Required evidence:

```text
release approval
version strategy
test results
known gaps
release notes
consumer migration guide
```

Blocked if:

```text
release notes omit breaking changes
provider docs stale for claimed provider features
downstream validation implied but not performed
```

### Stage: consumer update

Gate objective:

```text
update downstream consumer to approved package version
```

Required evidence:

```text
consumer approval
package version
consumer diff
consumer tests
known consumer contract changes
```

Potential consumer workspace:

@C:\ek

Blocked if:

```text
consumer update not approved
package version unavailable
consumer tests fail on context contract
```

### Stage: preview validation

Gate objective:

```text
prove product behavior in a review environment
```

Required evidence:

```text
deploy URL
test credentials policy
seeded data ids
normal projection scenario
blocked projection scenario
secret scenario if relevant
tenant scenario if relevant
manual reviewer result
```

Blocked if:

```text
credentials unavailable
seeded data missing
blocked projection not observable
provider dispatch status unknown
```

### Stage: canary organization

Gate objective:

```text
enable behavior for one scoped organization or workspace
```

Required evidence:

```text
canary org id
feature/config approval if needed
tenant scope verification
operator report visibility
rollback/disable mechanism
```

Blocked if:

```text
org scope ambiguous
tenant filtering unverified
disable path unavailable
```

### Stage: expanded canary

Gate objective:

```text
expand after first canary has clean evidence
```

Required evidence:

```text
first canary pass
no critical incidents
blocked projection rate understood
operator feedback reviewed
usage estimate error within threshold
```

Blocked if:

```text
critical risk open
operator reports unclear
estimate error high and unmitigated
```

### Stage: production rollout

Gate objective:

```text
make behavior generally available for approved scope
```

Required evidence:

```text
release approval
canary evidence
known gaps accepted
incident response path
dashboard/metric readiness
support notes
```

Blocked if:

```text
source coverage gaps remain
secret/tenant risks unresolved
release notes inaccurate
downstream validation absent when required
```

### Stage: post-rollout audit

Gate objective:

```text
verify production behavior after rollout
```

Required evidence:

```text
projection render/block rates
blocked reason distribution
secret detection count
tenant mismatch count
provider estimate error
operator feedback
incident count
```

Blocked if:

```text
metrics unavailable
provider dispatch after blocked state appears
raw secret exposure appears
tenant mismatch included source appears
```

### Gate status values

Recommended status values:

```text
not_started
ready_for_review
approved
blocked
passed
failed
not_applicable
```

Avoid:

```text
good
fine
probably
ready-ish
```

### Summary

Rollout gates should make evidence explicit:

```text
package tests are not downstream validation
preview deployed is not manual validation
manual validation is not production rollout
canary pass is not global rollout
provider feature exists is not audit sufficiency
```

Each gate should say what was proven and what remains unproven.

It does not yet create:

The minimal first slice should answer:

It should not yet answer:

```text
can Ekairos rewrite provider input in production
```

That second question belongs to a later approved slice.

```text
reactor contract break approved or explicitly deferred
```

### Goal

Goal:

```text
insert projection planning after expanded source context exists and before provider dispatch can happen
```

This slice should prove:

```text
projection can block before reactor call
rendered projection can reach reactor
projection traces can be emitted
engine behavior remains deterministic across iterations
```

### In scope

In scope:

```text
engine insertion after expandEvents
projection builder call
blocked projection return path
projection trace event emission
rendered messages passed to reactor if contract break approved
scripted reactor test coverage
AI SDK reactor test coverage if params change
```

### Out of scope

Out of scope:

```text
schema changes
provider-native compaction
auto compaction
React UI changes
release
downstream validation
long-term memory
durable projection entities
```

### Insertion rule

Required insertion point:

```text
after story.expandEvents
before story.getReactor or before reactor invocation
```

Reason:

```text
projection sees expanded context and can block before provider call
```

Forbidden insertion point:

```text
inside provider adapter as primary projection policy
after provider dispatch
inside store.itemsToModelMessages as policy owner
```

### Blocked behavior

When projection blocks:

```text
reactor is not called
provider dispatch does not occur
projection trace records blocked reason
operator report can be built from trace/report payload
step/execution state follows approved blocked semantics
```

Must not happen:

```text
AI SDK streamText call
provider-native compact call
action execution from blocked model response
provider usage trace claiming dispatch
```

### Rendered behavior

When projection renders:

```text
reactor receives rendered messages or approved projection-aware params
projection id flows with reactor params
rendered input hash is available
messagesForModel returned by reactor matches rendered projection or is derived deterministically
```

If reactor still returns messagesForModel:

```text
engine should verify or trust according to approved contract
```

Recommended:

```text
engine owns rendered messages and reactor echoes or reports them
```

### Action execution behavior

Action execution currently receives messagesForModel from reactionResult.

Future behavior should define whether actions receive:

```text
messages
projectionId
renderedInputHash
projectionStatus
sourceCoverageSummary
```

Recommended minimum:

```text
projectionId
renderedInputHash
messages
```

Reason:

```text
action execution should preserve audit continuity with the model input that produced the action request
```

Minimum trace payload:

```text
executionId

iteration
projectionStatus
strategy
projectedInputTokens
modelWindowTokens

providerDispatchAllowed
```

Blocked trace:

```text
operatorActionRequired
```

Rendered trace:

```text

summarySourceCount
referenceSourceCount
omittedSourceCount
warnings
```

### Required tests

Required tests:

```text
projection runs after expandEvents
blocked projection prevents reactor call
blocked projection emits trace/report
rendered projection calls reactor once
rendered projection params include projection id
action execution context preserves messages/projection hash if approved
shouldContinue still runs only after valid action results
```

Suggested fixtures:

```text
blocked_unresolved_approval_no_reactor
rendered_short_context_reactor_called
rendered_summary_context_reactor_called
blocked_secret_redaction_no_reactor
blocked_tenant_scope_no_reactor
```

### Regression tests

Regression risks:

```text
double assistant message rendering
step stream close behavior changes
reaction parts persistence changes
shouldContinue loop changes
action results fail to merge into parts
```

Tests should inspect:

```text
step stream event order
reactionEvent status
step status
persisted parts
action request extraction
loop continuation
```

### Acceptance criteria

Pass when:

```text
blocked projection stops before reactor
rendered projection invokes reactor with approved params
trace/report evidence exists
no schema/config/UI/release changes
tests pass
```

Fail when:

```text
blocked state still calls provider
reactor can bypass projection
projection trace missing
provider adapter owns source authority policy
action execution receives messages unrelated to rendered input
```

### Review questions

Before implementation, technical leader should answer:

```text
what exact blocked state shape is approved
does ContextReactorParams break now
does scripted reactor change in same slice
does AI SDK reactor change in same slice
what trace event names are approved
what tests are mandatory before merge
```

### Summary

The runtime integration slice is where projection stops being a pure policy object and starts controlling provider dispatch.

That is why it should only happen after the minimal first slice proves the policy vocabulary and the technical leader approves blocked-state semantics.

## Runtime dispatch gate trace taxonomy

Status: proposal only.

This section specifies a candidate trace and stream vocabulary for the runtime dispatch gate described in the previous slice.

It is not approved.

It does not authorize code, schema, config, provider, or runtime changes.

The purpose is to make the runtime slice reviewable before implementation by naming the evidence that must exist when projection either blocks provider dispatch or allows provider dispatch.

### Existing runtime facts

Current facts from the local package:

```text
the engine expands events before it calls the reactor
the reactor call is the provider dispatch boundary for AI SDK reactors
the AI SDK reactor rebuilds messagesForModel from context items
the engine later passes messagesForModel to tool execution context
the loop asks shouldContinue only after action results are merged
context trace writes currently use a closed TraceEventKind union
context trace writes support an arbitrary payload field
AI SDK usage is written as context.llm after provider execution
```

### Core trace principle

The dispatch gate has one non-negotiable audit principle:

```text
provider dispatch evidence must be impossible to confuse with projection evidence
```

If projection blocks, the trace must prove:

```text
projection ran
source packets were classified
budget was evaluated
protected material was not summarized away
dispatch was denied
reactor was not called
context.llm was not emitted for that blocked attempt
action execution did not run from a blocked model result
```

If projection renders, the trace must prove:

```text
projection ran
source packets were classified
budget was evaluated
rendered input was produced
dispatch was allowed
reactor was called once
context.llm, if emitted, corresponds to the allowed rendered input
action execution context can be linked to the rendered input
```

The current `context.llm` event must remain provider usage evidence.

It should not be overloaded to mean projection planning.

Projection planning can happen without an LLM call.

Projection blocking must happen without an LLM call.

Therefore projection evidence needs a separate event identity.

### Event kind strategy

The local trace contract currently exposes these trace kinds:

```text
workflow.run
workflow.step
context.run
context.lifecycle
context.execution
context.item
context.review
context.step
context.part
context.llm
```

The low-blast-radius runtime slice should not expand that union unless the technical leader explicitly approves a schema/type break.

For the runtime slice that avoids schema changes, the candidate mapping is:

```text
projection planning eventKind: context.step
projection blocked eventKind: context.step
projection rendered eventKind: context.step
projection dispatch allowed eventKind: context.step
projection dispatch denied eventKind: context.step
provider usage eventKind: context.llm
action binding eventKind: context.step
loop decision eventKind: context.step
```

The precise projection event name can live in payload:

```text
payload.projectionEventName
```

Candidate names:

```text
context.projection.plan.started
context.projection.plan.completed
context.projection.rendered
context.projection.blocked
context.projection.dispatch.allowed
context.projection.dispatch.denied
context.projection.action.bound
context.projection.loop.input_bound
```

If the technical leader approves a trace contract break later, the target union could add explicit projection kinds:

```text
context.projection
context.projection.dispatch
```

That later contract break is cleaner for analytics, but it should be reviewed separately from the first runtime insertion.

### Stream event strategy

There are two audiences:

```text
operator-visible stream events
durable trace events
```

Operator-visible stream events should be small.

They should answer:

```text
is projection running
did projection block
did projection render
is provider dispatch allowed
```

Durable trace events should be complete enough for migration audit.

They should answer:

```text
what sources were considered
what was included
what was summarized
what was referenced
what was omitted
what blocked dispatch
what rendered input hash was used
what provider call, if any, consumed that input
```

Candidate stream event types:

```text
projection.started
projection.rendered
projection.blocked
projection.dispatch_allowed
projection.dispatch_denied
```

Candidate durable trace payload field:

```text
projectionEventName
```

The stream event should not include source text.

The durable trace should not include secrets or raw protected data.

The durable trace should include ids, hashes, counts, classifications, and reviewer-facing reasons.

### Required event sequence for rendered dispatch

Rendered dispatch should produce this logical sequence:

```text
step.created
context.content_updated
context.projection.plan.started
context.projection.plan.completed
context.projection.rendered
context.projection.dispatch.allowed
context.llm
part.created
step.updated
context.projection.action.bound if action requests exist
action result chunk events if actions execute
context.projection.loop.input_bound
shouldContinue decision
step.completed or step.updated
execution.completed if loop ends
```

The important boundary is:

```text
context.projection.dispatch.allowed must occur before reactor invocation
context.llm can occur only after provider execution
```

The trace must allow a reviewer to ask:

```text
which projection allowed this provider call
what input hash did the provider call consume
which source packets shaped the rendered input
which budget profile was used
which protected packets were passed by reference instead of summarized
```

The answer should not require reading the full raw transcript.

The answer should be available from trace payload and projection manifest.

### Required event sequence for blocked dispatch

Blocked dispatch should produce this logical sequence:

```text
step.created
context.content_updated
context.projection.plan.started
context.projection.plan.completed
context.projection.blocked
context.projection.dispatch.denied
step.updated or step.completed with approved blocked semantics
execution status according to approved blocked semantics
```

Blocked dispatch must not produce:

```text
context.llm for that attempt
part.created from provider output
action request extraction from provider output
action execution from provider output
shouldContinue based on provider output
```

If a blocked projection creates an engine-owned assistant event for UI explanation, that event must be clearly marked as engine-owned.

It must not look like model output.

Candidate engine-owned part marker:

```text
partType: engine.projection_blocked
source: engine
projectionId: projection identifier
providerDispatchAllowed: false
```

This marker is a proposal only.

The current part contract would need review before any implementation writes such a part.

### Projection identifiers

Every projection attempt should have an identifier even when it blocks.

Candidate deterministic id input:

```text
contextId
executionId
stepId
iteration
sourceWindowHash
projectionPolicyVersion
```

Candidate id format:

```text
projection:<executionId>:<stepId>:<iteration>:<shortHash>
```

The short hash should be a display aid only.

The trace should retain the full hash.

The id must be stable for deterministic replay of the same source window and policy version.

The id must change when:

```text
source event set changes
source packet content hash changes
projection policy version changes
model-window profile changes
redaction policy version changes
protected source classification changes
```

The id should not change when:

```text
operator opens the same report again
stream subscriber reconnects
trace upload is retried
```


### Context.llm correlation

The current AI SDK trace writes provider usage after the provider stream completes.

That is correct for usage.

A future projection-aware provider call should correlate `context.llm` to projection evidence through payload fields.

Candidate additional `context.llm` payload fields:

```text
projectionId
renderedInputHash
projectionPolicyVersion
sourceWindowHash
providerDispatchAllowed
```

Rules:

```text
context.llm without projectionId is allowed only before the runtime slice is enabled
context.llm with providerDispatchAllowed false is invalid
context.llm with a renderedInputHash that has no rendered projection event is invalid
context.llm for a blocked projection is invalid
```

For a breaking runtime slice, the cleaner rule is stricter:

```text
all context.llm events produced by projection-aware engines must carry projectionId and renderedInputHash
```

That stricter rule should be part of the runtime contract review.

### Action execution correlation

The current engine passes `messagesForModel` into action execution context after the model returns action requests.

That means projection must preserve audit continuity past the provider call.

Future action execution context should know which model input produced the action request.

Candidate action context additions:

```text
projectionId
renderedInputHash
projectionStatus
sourceCoverageSummary
```

Candidate trace event:

```text
projectionEventName: context.projection.action.bound
```

Minimum payload:

```text
projectionId
renderedInputHash
toolCallId
actionName
autoApproval
requiresReview
sourceCoverageSummaryHash
```

Rules:

```text
action execution must not occur without a valid rendered projection
manual review requests should include projection id
manual approval should not mutate rendered input hash
action result parts should remain linked to the same projection id
```

This does not mean action code receives raw source packets.

Action code should receive only the approved execution context.

The trace should hold the audit link.

### Loop continuation correlation

The loop calls `shouldContinue` after action results are merged into persisted reaction parts.

Projection changes the evidence that `shouldContinue` can rely on.

If `shouldContinue` keeps inspecting `reactionEvent.content.parts`, it may not know whether those parts came from:

```text
raw event replay
projection-rendered messages
provider output
engine-owned blocked explanation
action result merge
```

Candidate trace event:

```text
projectionEventName: context.projection.loop.input_bound
```

Minimum payload:

```text
projectionId
renderedInputHash if rendered
projectionStatus
reactionEventId
stepId
actionResultCount
shouldContinueInputHash
```

Rules:

```text
shouldContinue must not run after blocked provider dispatch unless the blocked-state semantics explicitly require it
if shouldContinue runs, its input hash should bind to the post-action reaction event
if shouldContinue ends the execution, final status must preserve the projection id
```

### Failure taxonomy

Projection gate failures should be separate from provider failures.

Candidate failure classes:

```text
projection_source_read_failed
projection_classification_failed
projection_budget_overflow
projection_redaction_failed
projection_secret_detected
projection_tenant_scope_violation
projection_summary_validation_failed
projection_render_failed
projection_trace_write_failed
projection_unknown_failure
```

Provider failures remain provider failures.

Action failures remain action failures.

Loop-decision failures remain loop failures.

This distinction matters because retry policy differs:

```text
source read failure may retry after store recovery
budget overflow may require task splitting
secret detection may require operator review
tenant violation must block
summary validation failure may use include-by-reference or split
render failure is a projection bug
provider failure may retry provider dispatch
action failure may retry or surface to operator
```

### Blocked-state decision points

The runtime slice cannot implement blocked state without technical-leader approval.

Open decisions:

```text
does blocked projection mark step failed or completed
does blocked projection mark execution failed or keep it executing
does blocked projection close context or leave it open_idle
does blocked projection create an output item
does blocked projection create event_parts
does blocked projection emit operator-visible stream chunks
does blocked projection call shouldContinue
does blocked projection trigger onEnd hooks
```

Recommendation for review:

```text
blocked projection should be a first-class terminal state for the step
provider dispatch should not occur
model output should not be fabricated
operator-facing explanation should be engine-owned
trace/report evidence should explain the block
```

Exact state values must be approved before code changes.

### Trace persistence caveat

The current trace writer is designed so tracing does not break workflows by default, with strict behavior controlled by trace configuration.

Projection audit creates a sharper requirement:

```text
blocked dispatch evidence must not be lost silently
```

Therefore the runtime slice needs a separate approval decision:

```text
is projection-block trace failure terminal
```

Two candidate policies:

```text
policy A: trace write failure blocks provider dispatch and returns projection_trace_write_failed
policy B: trace write failure allows local persisted report but blocks remote trace upload only
```

Policy A is stronger for migration audit.

Policy B reduces operational interruption but requires a durable local report.

Because the current trace writer can continue when trace persistence fails, projection gate evidence should not rely only on remote trace upload.

The minimal safe runtime rule:

```text
before provider dispatch, projection evidence must be durably available in at least one approved local artifact
```

That artifact can be:

```text
event_trace_events row
event_parts engine-owned report
future projection entity
```

The exact approved artifact depends on the slice boundary.

If the slice excludes schema changes and excludes engine-owned parts, then the runtime gate needs a reviewed choice before implementation.

### Test fixtures

Trace taxonomy tests should be scenario-first.

Candidate fixture names:

```text
projection_trace_rendered_before_reactor
projection_trace_blocked_no_reactor
projection_trace_blocked_no_context_llm
projection_trace_rendered_context_llm_correlated
projection_trace_action_bound_to_projection
projection_trace_loop_bound_after_action_merge
projection_trace_write_failure_blocks_when_strict
projection_trace_write_failure_uses_local_report_when_approved
```

Each test should assert ordering.

Rendered ordering assertions:

```text
projection.plan.started before projection.plan.completed
projection.plan.completed before projection.rendered
projection.rendered before projection.dispatch.allowed
projection.dispatch.allowed before reactor call
reactor call before context.llm trace
context.llm trace carries projection id if runtime slice requires it
```

Blocked ordering assertions:

```text
projection.plan.started before projection.plan.completed
projection.plan.completed before projection.blocked
projection.blocked before projection.dispatch.denied
projection.dispatch.denied before terminal step state
reactor call count is zero
context.llm trace count is zero
action execution count is zero
```

Correlation assertions:

```text
projectionId is stable across projection events for one attempt
renderedInputHash is present only when rendered
context.llm renderedInputHash equals projection.rendered renderedInputHash
action.bound projectionId equals context.llm projectionId
loop.input_bound projectionId equals action.bound projectionId when actions exist
```

### Reviewer queries

A reviewer should be able to answer these questions from traces and reports:

```text
show all blocked projections for execution id X
show provider calls whose projection id is missing
show provider calls whose rendered input hash has no rendered projection event
show action executions whose projection id differs from provider call projection id
show blocked projections that emitted context.llm
show projection budget overflows by model profile
show tenant-scope violations by org id
show trace failures before provider dispatch
```

Suggested derived checks:

```text
blocked projection with context.llm count greater than zero is critical
rendered projection with no context.llm may be valid only if reactor failed before provider dispatch
context.llm with no projection id after runtime slice is critical
action execution with no projection id after runtime slice is critical
loop continuation with mismatched projection id is critical
```

### Review packet

Before implementation, the technical leader should approve:

```text
trace event naming
payload field names
blocked-state step/execution/context semantics
whether context.llm must carry projection id immediately
whether trace write failure blocks provider dispatch
whether blocked projection writes an output item
whether engine-owned parts are allowed in this slice
which tests are mandatory
```

If any of those decisions is missing, runtime implementation should not start.

### Summary

The dispatch gate is an audit boundary, not only a token-budget function.

The most important trace rule is simple:

```text
blocked projection must leave durable evidence and must not leave provider evidence
rendered projection must leave durable evidence that can be matched to provider evidence
```

That distinction is what lets Ekairos use compaction in migration sessions without losing proof of what the model saw, what it did not see, and why provider dispatch was allowed.
