### Cross-example invariant matrix

Invariant checklist:

```text
blocked examples have no context.llm
blocked examples have no provider-originated part.created
blocked examples have no action execution from provider output
rendered examples have renderedInputHash
rendered examples have dispatch.allowed before context.llm
action examples bind action context to projection id
loop examples bind shouldContinue input to post-action reaction hash
trace write failure blocks if durable evidence is required
provider failure is not projection.blocked
manual approval denial is not projection.blocked
summary validation failure is projection.blocked
```

### Future fixture conversion

If the technical leader approves the runtime trace slice, these examples can become fixture cases.

Suggested fixture mapping:

```text
Example A -> rendered_migration_action_trace_order
Example B -> blocked_tenant_scope_no_provider_trace
Example C -> blocked_budget_overflow_split_required
Example D -> rendered_provider_failure_not_projection_block
Example E -> trace_write_failure_denies_dispatch_when_required
Example F -> rendered_no_actions_completion_trace
Example G -> rendered_manual_approval_denied_trace
Example H -> blocked_summary_validation_failed_trace
```

Fixture assertions should not depend on wall-clock timestamps except for monotonic ordering.

Fixture assertions should depend on:

```text
event names
projection id correlation
rendered input hash correlation
provider dispatch marker
absence of context.llm on blocked attempts
absence of action execution on blocked attempts
step/execution terminal state after approval of blocked semantics
```

### Summary

The worked examples clarify that projection has three different outcomes:

```text
rendered and dispatched
blocked before dispatch
rendered but provider/action later fails
```

Only the second outcome is compaction blocking provider dispatch.

The third outcome still needs projection evidence because the provider input existed and may be relevant to retry, audit, and migration reports.

Status: proposal only.

It does not approve implementation.

It does not create files.

It names the test surfaces that should be reviewed before any runtime change is made.

### Harness principle

The dispatch gate should be tested before real provider dispatch is needed.

The first runtime tests should use deterministic reactors and explicit spies.

Only after deterministic ordering is proven should AI SDK mock and real-provider tests be added.

Test tiers:

```text
tier 1 pure selector unit tests
tier 2 engine integration with scripted reactor
tier 3 Instant-backed trace and event_parts tests
tier 4 AI SDK mock model correlation tests
tier 5 real provider smoke test gated by env
```

Tier 1 belongs to the minimal first slice.

Tiers 2 and 3 belong to the runtime dispatch gate slice.

Tier 4 belongs to AI SDK reactor integration after the runtime contract is approved.

Tier 5 is release evidence, not a substitute for deterministic tests.

### Tier 1: pure selector tests

Pure selector tests should not start workflows.

They should call projection planning functions directly once those functions exist.

They should prove:

```text
source packet classification is deterministic
protected packets are not summarized
budget overflow blocks
tenant-scope violation blocks
summary candidate selection is stable
omitted packets keep reasons
rendered input hash is deterministic
policy version participates in hashes
model profile participates in budget decisions
```

Candidate test names:

```text
classifies_source_packets_by_authority
blocks_cross_tenant_source_window
blocks_when_protected_tokens_exceed_window
renders_when_budget_allows_reference_packets
keeps_summary_claims_linked_to_source_packet_ids
changes_projection_hash_when_policy_version_changes
```

These tests can run without InstantDB.

They should not know about provider adapters.

### Tier 2: scripted reactor dispatch gate tests

Scripted reactor tests are the best first runtime harness because the reactor can be replaced with a spy.

The future test should build a context with:

```text
expander that adds source packets
projection policy configured to render or block
reactor spy that records calls
action tool spy that records executions
shouldContinue spy that records inputs
```

Rendered case assertions:

```text
projection builder called after expandEvents
reactor spy called exactly once
reactor params carry rendered projection contract if approved
projection dispatch allowed trace exists before reactor call
provider-neutral assistant event is persisted
event_parts rows are persisted
action spy executes only if reactor returns action request
shouldContinue sees post-action reaction event
```

Blocked case assertions:

```text
projection builder called after expandEvents
reactor spy call count is zero
action spy call count is zero
shouldContinue call count follows approved blocked semantics
dispatch denied trace exists
context.llm trace count is zero
provider-originated part rows are absent
blocked report or engine-owned blocked artifact exists if approved
```

The blocked case is the most important test in the runtime slice.

If blocked dispatch still reaches a reactor, the feature fails.

### Tier 3: Instant trace and event_parts tests

Instant-backed tests should verify durable artifacts.

They should query:

```text
event_trace_events
event_trace_runs
event_steps
event_items
event_parts
step stream chunks if stream is enabled
```

Rendered durable checks:

```text
projection events share one projectionId
projection.rendered has renderedInputHash
projection.dispatch.allowed appears before context.llm by createdAt or seq
context.llm payload projectionId matches rendered projection
event_parts rows belong to the reaction step
action result parts retain the same step boundary
```

Blocked durable checks:

```text
projection.blocked exists
projection.dispatch.denied exists
context.llm does not exist for execution and step
event_parts either absent or contain only approved engine-owned blocked artifact
step status follows approved blocked semantics
execution status follows approved blocked semantics
```

Trace rows should be parsed by payload, not by string search over JSON.

The helper should expose functions like:

```text
findProjectionEvents
findProjectionEventByName
assertProjectionOrder
assertNoContextLlmForStep
assertRenderedInputHashCorrelation
```

Those helper names are proposals only.

### Tier 4: AI SDK mock model tests

AI SDK mock tests should verify provider adapter correlation after the engine dispatch gate is proven.

They should not be the first proof of blocking.

Rendered AI SDK assertions:

```text
AI SDK streamText receives rendered messages if the reactor contract break is approved
context.llm trace includes projectionId
context.llm trace includes renderedInputHash
messagesForModel returned by reactor matches rendered projection or approved echo contract
tool calls extracted from provider output bind to projection id
```

Blocked AI SDK assertions:

```text
AI SDK streamText is not called
store.itemsToModelMessages is not used for provider dispatch after a blocked projection
context.llm trace is absent
no provider chunks are emitted
```

If the approved runtime design keeps `itemsToModelMessages` inside the AI SDK reactor, then the engine must pass already projected events.

If the approved runtime design moves message rendering to the engine, then AI SDK tests should assert that the reactor uses provided rendered messages.

Those are different contracts.

The test suite should make the chosen contract explicit.

### Tier 5: real provider smoke test

Real provider tests should be narrow.

They should not test every projection policy.

They should prove:

```text
rendered projection can reach a real provider
context.llm usage is captured
projectionId and renderedInputHash correlate with usage trace
provider response persists as event_parts
no secrets or raw protected payloads are written into traces
```

They should be skipped unless required environment is present.

They should not run as the main proof that blocked dispatch works.

Blocked dispatch is better proven with deterministic spies.

### Type contract tests

If the technical leader approves a reactor contract break, the public type test should be changed deliberately.

Candidate new assertions:

```text
ContextReactorParams exposes projection
ContextReactorParams exposes renderedMessages or projectionInput according to approved name
ContextReactorParams exposes projectionId
ContextReactorParams exposes renderedInputHash when dispatch is allowed
ContextReactorParams does not expose raw protected source packets directly to provider adapters
ContextReactionResult no longer owns model input authority if engine owns rendering
```

If the technical leader defers the reactor contract break, the type test should instead assert:

```text
reactor params events are projection-filtered events
reaction result messagesForModel is treated as reactor echo
engine verifies reaction result messagesForModel hash if approved
```

The type test should not preserve both contracts.

The approved contract should be singular.

### Trace assertion helpers

Future trace assertion helper behavior:

```text
load trace events by workflowRunId or executionId
group by stepId
extract projection events from payload.projectionEventName
sort by seq first and eventAt second
fail on duplicate projection.dispatch.allowed for one projectionId
fail on dispatch.allowed after context.llm
fail on context.llm without projectionId when projection-aware mode is enabled
fail on blocked projection with context.llm
```

Candidate helper outputs:

```text
projectionEvents
llmEvents
actionBoundEvents
loopBoundEvents
blockedEvents
dispatchAllowedEvents
dispatchDeniedEvents
```

The helper should not hide failed invariants behind snapshots.

Assertions should be explicit so reviewer failures are readable.

### Reactor spy helper

Future reactor spy helper:

```text
records params.events length
records params.projectionId if approved
records params.renderedInputHash if approved
records params.messages if approved
returns scripted assistant event
returns scripted action requests
returns messagesForModel according to approved contract
increments call count only when invoked
```

Blocked tests assert:

```text
call count equals zero
```

Rendered tests assert:

```text
call count equals one
```

Multi-iteration tests assert:

```text
call count equals number of rendered iterations
blocked iteration does not increment call count
```

### Multi-iteration tests

The context engine can run several iterations.

Projection must be per iteration.

Candidate scenario:

```text
iteration 0 renders and requests an action
action executes and shouldContinue returns true
iteration 1 blocks because new action result introduced protected overflow
execution stops or enters approved blocked state
```

Assertions:

```text
iteration 0 has projection id A
iteration 0 has context.llm
iteration 1 has projection id B
iteration 1 has no context.llm
reactor call count is one
action execution count is one
blocked state belongs to iteration 1
```

This scenario prevents a subtle failure:

```text
a previous rendered projection must not authorize a later blocked iteration
```

### Stream tests

If the runtime slice emits operator-visible projection stream events, stream tests should verify:

```text
projection.started appears after step.created
projection.rendered appears before provider chunks
projection.blocked appears without provider chunks
projection.dispatch_denied appears before terminal state
projection events do not include raw source text
projection events include projection id and high-level reason only
```

If the runtime slice does not emit stream events, this section should stay out of scope.

The technical leader should decide whether stream UX is part of the slice.

### Benchmark and report checks

The current benchmark helper groups context, reactor, and loop stages.

Projection should add measurable stages only after approval.

Candidate stage names:

```text
react.iteration.N.projectionPlanMs
react.iteration.N.projectionRenderMs
react.iteration.N.projectionTraceMs
```

Benchmark assertions should not be brittle on duration.

They should assert that stage names exist for rendered and blocked attempts.

Reports should include:

```text
projection status
projected token estimate
actual prompt tokens if provider ran
overflow tokens if blocked
trace event count
reactor call count
action execution count
```

### Negative tests

Negative tests are required because dispatch gating is a safety feature.

Required negative cases:

```text
blocked projection still calls reactor
blocked projection emits context.llm
blocked projection executes action
rendered projection lacks renderedInputHash
context.llm renderedInputHash differs from projection.rendered
action.bound projectionId differs from context.llm projectionId
loop.input_bound projectionId differs from action.bound projectionId
summary validation failure still dispatches provider
tenant violation still dispatches provider
```

Each negative test should fail on one invariant.

Do not combine many violations into one broad failure.

### Approval checklist for test harness

Before implementation, technical leader should approve:

```text
which future test files are allowed
whether runtime slice uses scripted reactor tests first
whether AI SDK mock tests are in the same slice or later
whether real provider smoke is required before merge
which blocked status semantics tests must assert
whether stream event tests are in scope
whether ContextReactorParams breaks in this slice
which trace payload names are final for tests
```

If those questions are not answered, only pure selector docs and proposal work should continue.

### Summary

The runtime dispatch gate test harness should prove one thing with zero ambiguity:

```text
projection is the last authority before provider dispatch
```

The most valuable tests are not the real-provider tests.

The most valuable tests are deterministic blocked-dispatch tests that prove the provider path cannot run when projection denies it.

### Claude Code context window recheck

Current Claude Code context-window docs emphasize context inspection and compaction behavior.

Observed survival behavior after `/compact`:

```text
system prompt and output style remain unchanged
project-root CLAUDE.md and unscoped rules are re-injected from disk
auto memory is re-injected from disk
rules with paths frontmatter are lost until a matching file is read again
nested CLAUDE.md files are lost until a file in that subdirectory is read again
invoked skill bodies are re-injected with token caps
```

Observed skill caps:

```text
5000 tokens per skill
25000 tokens total across skills
oldest skill bodies dropped first
```

Source interpretation for Ekairos:

```text
not all context is conversation history

path-scoped rules need activation evidence
skill bodies need independent token budgets
compaction should not pretend every instruction survives equally
```

Ekairos proposal impact:

```text
rule activation plane remains necessary
source packet authority should distinguish durable disk rules from prior chat text
projection report should list instructions reloaded from source
projection report should list path-scoped rules that were inactive
skill/context package budget should be a separate budget line
```

### Hermes recheck

Current Hermes documentation still describes a pluggable context engine and two compression layers.

Observed architecture:

```text
ContextEngine abstraction
default ContextCompressor
plugin engines can replace the default engine when explicitly configured
gateway session hygiene at 85 percent of context
agent ContextCompressor at 50 percent by default
gateway layer is a safety net before agent processing
agent layer runs inside the agent loop with API-reported tokens
```

Observed config and budget details:

```text
compression.enabled default true
compression.threshold default 0.50
compression.target_ratio default 0.20
compression.protect_last_n default 20
protect_first_n hardcoded as 3
tail budget at defaults for 200000 context is 20000 tokens
maximum summary tokens use the smaller of 5 percent of context or 12000
summary minimum is 2000 tokens
```

Observed algorithm features:

```text
old tool results outside protected tail can be cleared before LLM summarization
tail is selected by walking backward through recent messages by token budget
tool call and tool result groups are kept aligned
summary model is called with a structured template
previous summary is carried into later compactions for iterative recompression
prompt caching strategy separates stable system prompt cache from compressed regions
intermediate context-pressure warnings were removed because they made models stop too early on complex tasks
```

Risk observed in Hermes docs:

```text
if the summary model cannot fit the content, the compressor can return no summary and drop middle turns
```

Source interpretation for Ekairos:

```text
two-layer pressure management is useful
cheap pruning and LLM summary are separate mechanisms
protected head and protected tail are useful defaults for chat agents
summary failure must not result in silent loss for migrations
Ekairos should block or split instead of dropping protected middle context
```

Ekairos proposal impact:

```text
projection selector should separate cheap elision from summary generation
projection selector should have protected head/tail concepts only as one proposal, not as the whole policy
summary generation failure should be projection blocked for migration sessions
prompt cache interaction should be modeled in the budget ledger
operator pressure warnings should be carefully designed to avoid causing premature task abandonment
```

```text
OpenCode's tool-output pruning reinforces the need to classify tool output as a separate segment type

OpenCode's source does not provide Ekairos migration-grade source validation by itself
```

Ekairos proposal impact:

```text
Ekairos summary templates should be fixed enough for validation

```

### Recheck-based adjustments to proposal emphasis

This recheck strengthens five points already present in the artifact:

```text
1. Provider-native compaction is an adapter capability, not Ekairos policy.
2. Durable rules and source artifacts must be re-resolved, not trusted from summary memory.
3. Cheap pruning, retrieval, summary generation, provider compaction, and prompt caching are separate controls.
4. Summary failure in migration workflows should block or split; it should not drop source material.
5. Runtime trace evidence must distinguish projection, provider usage, action execution, and loop continuation.
```

No proposal should be weakened toward hidden transcript summarization after this recheck.

The source drift points toward more explicit projection evidence, not less.

## Provider-native compaction adapter contract examples

Status: proposal only.

This section converts the late-run provider recheck into adapter contract examples.

It does not approve implementation.

It does not choose a provider.

It does not allow provider-native compaction to own Ekairos policy.

Core rule:

```text
provider-native compaction is an operation behind the projection ledger
```

The provider adapter may compact.

The Ekairos projection layer must still decide:

```text
which source packets can be sent
which source packets are protected
which summaries can be trusted
which rendered input can reach provider dispatch
which trace evidence proves the operation
```

### Adapter contract shape

Candidate provider-native compaction adapter interface, expressed as documentation:

```text
operationName
provider
providerModel
sourceWindowHash
inputPacketRefs
inputMessageHash
operationRequestHash
operationResponseHash
providerCompactionArtifactKind
providerCompactionArtifactHash
validationStatus
sourceCoverageSummary
usageEstimate
actualUsage if reported
traceEventIds
```

The adapter should not return an unqualified string summary.

It should return a structured artifact candidate:

```text
artifactKind
artifactId
provider
providerOperation
sourceWindowHash
contentHash
summaryTextHash
sourcePacketRefs
claimLedgerRefs
validationStatus
blockedReason if invalid
```

The adapter output becomes eligible for projection only after validation.

### Claude API adapter example

Observed provider operation:

```text
normal Messages API request with context_management.edits
beta header compact-2026-01-12
edit type compact_20260112
optional trigger input_tokens value
optional pause_after_compaction
optional instructions replacing default summarization prompt
provider returns compaction content block when compaction occurs
later requests pass compaction block back
provider ignores content before compaction block
```

Candidate Ekairos adapter metadata:

```text
provider: anthropic
operationName: messages.create.context_management.compact
betaHeader: compact-2026-01-12
editType: compact_20260112
artifactKind: anthropic.compaction_block
triggerType: input_tokens
triggerValue: provider or policy value
pauseAfterCompaction: true or false
instructionsHash: sha256 of custom instructions if any
```

Candidate request trace payload:

```json
{
  "provider": "anthropic",
  "operationName": "messages.create.context_management.compact",
  "betaHeader": "compact-2026-01-12",
  "editType": "compact_20260112",
  "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
  "sourceWindowHash": "sha256:source-window-claude",
  "inputMessageHash": "sha256:messages-before-provider-compact",
  "trigger": {
    "type": "input_tokens",
    "value": 150000
  },
  "pauseAfterCompaction": true,
  "projectionId": "projection:exec:step:0:claude"
}
```

Candidate response trace payload:

```json
{
  "provider": "anthropic",
  "operationName": "messages.create.context_management.compact",
  "artifactKind": "anthropic.compaction_block",
  "artifactId": "provider-summary:anthropic:exec:step:0",
  "sourceWindowHash": "sha256:source-window-claude",
  "operationResponseHash": "sha256:anthropic-response",
  "providerCompactionArtifactHash": "sha256:anthropic-compaction-block",
  "validationStatus": "pending",
  "projectionId": "projection:exec:step:0:claude"
}
```

Claude-specific validation checks:

```text
compaction block exists before any provider text continuation is trusted as compacted context
compaction block hash is recorded
source window hash matches the request
custom instructions hash matches the approved Ekairos prompt pack
provider block is not treated as migration truth until claim validation passes
pause_after_compaction behavior is represented in trace if used
```

Claude-specific rejection cases:

```text
provider returns text without expected compaction block when compaction was required
provider compaction summary includes source claims with no source packet link
provider compaction summary refers to protected raw data that was not allowed into provider input
provider request omits required beta header
provider request uses edit type that does not match approved capability registry entry
```

### OpenAI Responses compact adapter example

Observed provider operation:

```text
POST /responses/compact
explicit operation that compacts a conversation
returns a compacted response object
model is provided as part of request
input conversation is provided as request body content
```

Candidate Ekairos adapter metadata:

```json
}
```

Candidate response trace payload:

```json
{

  "operationResponseHash": "sha256:openai-compact-response",
```

OpenAI-specific validation checks:

```text
request path is the approved compact operation
model is allowed by provider capability registry

```

```text

operation is used as a substitute for local projection planning
```

### Local validated summary adapter example

Provider-native compaction is not the only adapter.

Ekairos should also support a local validated summary operation in the target design.

Candidate operation:

```text
provider: ekairos
operationName: projection.summary.local_validated
artifactKind: ekairos.validated_summary
```

This operation can still use an LLM internally if approved, but the operation owner is Ekairos projection policy.

Candidate artifact metadata:

```json
{
  "provider": "ekairos",
  "operationName": "projection.summary.local_validated",
  "artifactKind": "ekairos.validated_summary",
  "artifactId": "summary:local:exec:step:0",
  "sourceWindowHash": "sha256:source-window-local",
  "summaryHash": "sha256:summary-local",
  "claimLedgerHash": "sha256:claim-ledger-local",
  "validationStatus": "passed",
  "projectionId": "projection:exec:step:0:local"
}
```

The local validated summary should be the default target for migration workflows.

Provider-native compaction can be an optimization or provider-specific feature after the local ledger proves the source.

### Adapter capability registry fields

Provider capability registry should represent these fields:

```text
provider
operationName
operationKind
supportedModels
requiresHeader
requiresEditType
supportsPauseAfterCompaction
supportsCustomInstructions
returnsCompactionBlock
returnsCompactedResponseObject
supportsStreamingCompactionEvents
supportsUsage
zdrEligible if documented
maxTriggerTokens
minTriggerTokens
defaultTriggerTokens
cacheInteractionNotes
sourceValidationRequired
approvedForMigration
```

Candidate operation kinds:

```text
task_model_dispatch
provider_native_compaction
local_validated_summary
retrieval
tool_execution
```

Rules:

```text
provider_native_compaction output cannot enter projection as trusted until validationStatus is passed
provider_native_compaction cannot summarize protected source packets unless policy marks them summarizable
provider_native_compaction cannot replace source packet ledger
provider_native_compaction usage must be traced separately from task model usage
```

### Dispatch ordering with provider-native compaction

If provider-native compaction is used before task dispatch, candidate ordering is:

```text
source packet selection
source packet protection classification
provider-native compaction allowed or denied
provider-native compaction operation
provider compaction artifact validation
projection render using validated artifact
task provider dispatch
context.llm for task provider dispatch
```

If provider-native compaction happens inside a task provider call, candidate ordering is:

```text
projection render
task provider dispatch allowed
provider returns compaction block
projection records compaction block
provider continuation handling according to adapter
validation before future use of compaction block as source material
```

The second ordering is harder to audit because compaction and task response share provider flow.

Therefore the recommended migration-safe path is:

```text
local validated summary first
provider-native compaction only after explicit adapter approval
```

### Security rules

Provider-native adapters must respect these rules:

```text
no raw secrets in compact request
no cross-org source window in compact request
no protected migration artifacts in compact request unless approved
no provider summary trusted without source validation
no provider compact output stored without hash
no provider compact operation without trace id
no compact operation hidden behind normal task dispatch
```

Validation should fail closed when:

```text
sourceWindowHash cannot be recomputed
inputPacketRefs are missing
provider artifact hash cannot be computed
claim ledger validation fails
tenant-scope validation fails
redaction validation fails
```

### Migration-specific adapter approval

For migration sessions, a provider-native compaction adapter should require explicit approval for:

```text
provider
model family
operationName
source classes allowed into provider compact request
custom summary instructions
validation rule set
retention class for compact artifact
trace fields
canary org scope
rollback behavior
```

Default migration stance:

```text
not approved until reviewed
```

Reason:

```text
schema migration and production data migration decisions need source proof beyond provider summary text
```

### Adapter test expectations

Provider-native compaction adapter tests should verify:

```text
capability registry exposes current provider names and operations
request hash changes when source window changes
request hash changes when custom instructions change
response hash is stable for same provider artifact
validation blocks claims without source links
protected packet ids are absent from provider compact request when reference-only
provider compact trace is separate from task context.llm trace
```

OpenAI adapter tests:

```text
operationName is responses.compact
path is /responses/compact
compacted response object hash is required
validationStatus starts pending
```

Claude adapter tests:

```text
beta header is compact-2026-01-12
edit type is compact_20260112
compaction block hash is required
pause_after_compaction is represented when enabled
```

### Summary

Provider-native compaction is valuable because it can reduce integration burden and align with provider-specific context behavior.

It is risky for Ekairos migrations if it becomes invisible policy.

The adapter contract should make every provider-native compaction call auditable:

```text
what was sent
why it was allowed
what provider artifact came back
how it was validated
whether it can be used in a migration projection
```

## Migration source-class compaction strategy matrix

Status: proposal only.

This section maps migration source classes to compaction strategy.

It is intentionally strict.

Migration work is different from generic chat continuation because source loss can produce incorrect production data changes.

Core rule:

```text
source authority determines compaction strategy
```

Token pressure alone must not decide whether a source can be summarized.

### Strategy vocabulary

Allowed strategy labels:

```text
include_exact
include_redacted
include_reference
summarize_validated
summarize_low_authority
omit_with_reason
block_and_split
block_for_review
```

Definitions:

```text
include_exact: render the exact allowed content into model input
include_redacted: render redacted content with redaction evidence
include_reference: render ids, hashes, and retrieval handles, not raw content
summarize_validated: render a summary that passed source-link validation
summarize_low_authority: render a summary for non-critical chat or exploratory content
omit_with_reason: exclude from model input and record the reason
block_and_split: deny dispatch and require task split
block_for_review: deny dispatch until operator approval or source cleanup
```

Strategy labels should be stable because they appear in traces, reports, tests, and reviewer worksheets.

### Matrix: operator instruction

Source class:

```text
operator instruction in the current turn
```

Default strategy:

```text
include_exact
```

Reason:

```text
current operator intent is high-authority context
```

Compaction rules:

```text
do not summarize current turn
do not replace approval or denial language with a paraphrase
if the instruction contains a secret, include_redacted and block_for_review if redaction would change task meaning
```

Block conditions:

```text
instruction conflicts with technical-leader approval gate
instruction requires code/config/infra execution without approval
instruction requests cross-org data mixing without explicit approval
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: operator_instruction
strategy: include_exact
authority: high
requiresApprovalGate: true when applicable
```

### Matrix: project governance instruction

Source class:

```text
AGENTS.md, workspace identity, release rules, approval constraints
```

Default strategy:

```text
include_exact for active constraints
include_reference for long stable background
```

Reason:

```text
governance instructions define allowed work and cannot be safely inferred from chat summary
```

Compaction rules:

```text
approval constraints stay exact
branch/push/release constraints stay exact
path formatting constraints stay exact
long strategic positioning can be summarized only when not driving an immediate decision
```

Block conditions:

```text
projection cannot determine whether a governance rule applies
governance rules conflict and technical-leader decision is missing
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: governance_instruction
strategy: include_exact or include_reference
authority: highest
sourcePath
sourceHash
```

### Matrix: schema definition

Source class:

```text
domain schema, Instant schema, package contracts, migration target schema
```

Default strategy:

```text
include_exact for active diff surface
include_reference for unchanged background
summarize_validated only for explanatory context
```

Reason:

```text
schema fields, links, indexes, and optionality are exact technical facts
```

Compaction rules:

```text
active source and target schema snippets stay exact
schema dry-run output stays exact for changed entities
summary may describe unchanged entities only with source links
schema hashes must be recorded
```

Block conditions:

```text
active schema diff exceeds model budget after protected reserves
schema source hash cannot be computed
schema version is ambiguous
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: schema_definition
strategy: include_exact
schemaHash
changedEntityCount
unchangedEntityCount
```

### Matrix: migration plan

Source class:

```text
operator-approved migration plan, transaction plan, staged rollout plan
```

Default strategy:

```text
include_exact
```

Reason:

```text
approved plan is executable intent
```

Compaction rules:

```text
do not summarize active approved steps
do not collapse transaction order
do not omit rollback gates
old draft plans can be summarize_validated only if marked superseded
```

Block conditions:

```text
multiple active plans conflict
approved plan cannot fit and no task split exists
transaction order is unknown
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: migration_plan
strategy: include_exact
approvalId
planHash
supersedes
```

### Matrix: Clerk organization matrix

Source class:

```text
org id, app id, admin token mapping, environment routing, canary org list
```

Default strategy:

```text
include_reference
include_redacted for non-secret identifiers when needed
```

Reason:

```text
org routing is sensitive and high authority; tokens must never be rendered
```

Compaction rules:

```text
never render admin tokens
render org ids only when needed and allowed
hash or alias sensitive route data when possible
include canary gate as exact policy
```

Block conditions:

```text
cross-org source packets appear in one projection without approval
admin token would be required in model input
org mapping cannot be verified
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: clerk_org_matrix
strategy: include_reference or include_redacted
orgCount
canaryOrgCount
tokenVisible: false
```

### Matrix: production dataset extract

Source class:

```text
dataset extracted through domain endpoint or Instant admin query
```

Default strategy:

```text
include_reference
summarize_validated for aggregate facts
block_and_split for large protected raw rows
```

Reason:

```text
raw production data can be large, sensitive, and org-scoped
```

Compaction rules:

```text
raw rows should usually stay out of provider input
aggregates can be summarized when deterministic transform records source hashes
row-level examples require redaction and approval
dataset extract id and hash must be preserved
```

Block conditions:

```text
dataset includes multiple orgs
redaction cannot prove removal of secrets or personal data
aggregate summary has no deterministic source query
row-level evidence is needed but cannot fit
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: production_dataset_extract
strategy: include_reference
extractId
queryHash
rowCount
orgScope
redactionStatus
```

### Matrix: deterministic transform script

Source class:

```text
Python or TypeScript transform logic for migration
```

Default strategy:

```text
include_exact for active transform logic
include_reference for unchanged library code
```

Reason:

```text
transform code defines how data changes
```

Compaction rules:

```text
active transformation functions should be exact
test fixture expectations should be exact
large helper modules can be referenced with symbol names and hashes
```

Block conditions:

```text
active transform does not fit and cannot be split
transform source path/hash cannot be verified
transform depends on unreviewed runtime config
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: transform_script
strategy: include_exact
sourcePath
sourceHash
testFixtureRefs
```

### Matrix: transaction application plan

Source class:

```text
idempotent transaction plan for target schema
```

Default strategy:

```text
include_exact
```

Reason:

```text
transaction operation order and idempotency keys are execution-critical
```

Compaction rules:

```text
operation order stays exact
idempotency keys stay exact unless secret-like
target entity names stay exact
large value payloads can be referenced by artifact hash
```

Block conditions:

```text
operation order cannot fit
idempotency keys are missing
transaction payload contains unredacted secrets
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: transaction_plan
strategy: include_exact
operationCount
idempotencyKeyCount
transactionPlanHash
```

### Matrix: verification query

Source class:

```text
post-migration verification query and expected result
```

Default strategy:

```text
include_exact for active verification
summarize_validated for historical verification runs
```

Reason:

```text
verification query semantics determine whether migration passed
```

Compaction rules:

```text
current verification query is exact
expected pass/fail criteria are exact
old run output can be summarized with source links
```

Block conditions:

```text
verification criteria conflict
expected result is missing
query output is too large and no aggregate exists
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: verification_query
strategy: include_exact
queryHash
expectedResultHash
lastRunStatus
```

### Matrix: model output

Source class:

```text
prior assistant/model output
```

Default strategy:

```text
summarize_low_authority for old exploratory output
include_exact for recent action requests and approved decisions
```

Reason:

```text
model output is not source truth unless approved or materialized into an artifact
```

Compaction rules:

```text
do not treat model prose as source data
do not preserve hallucinated claims without source links
preserve action requests exactly until resolved
preserve approved decisions exactly
```

Block conditions:

```text
model output contains unresolved claim used for migration decision
model output conflicts with source artifact
model output is the only source for production data fact
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: model_output
strategy: summarize_low_authority or include_exact
authority: low unless approved
claimValidationStatus
```

### Matrix: tool output

Source class:

```text
tool output, terminal output, query output, provider tool result
```

Default strategy:

```text
include_exact for short active outputs
include_reference for large outputs
summarize_validated for old outputs with stable source artifacts
```

Reason:

```text
tool output can be high value but often verbose
```

Compaction rules:

```text
preserve command/query and exit status
preserve errors exactly when active
large stdout should be hashed and referenced
old successful verbose output can be summarized if source artifact remains available
```

Block conditions:

```text
active error output cannot fit
large output is needed but not stored elsewhere
tool output includes secrets
tool output source cannot be retrieved
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: tool_output
strategy: include_exact or include_reference
commandHash
exitStatus
outputHash
truncated: true or false
```

### Matrix: source code

Source class:

```text
source files, package entrypoints, local package contracts
```

Default strategy:

```text
include_exact for edited or decision-relevant snippets
include_reference for unchanged files
summarize_validated for architecture explanation
```

Reason:

```text
code behavior depends on exact identifiers, function signatures, and control flow
```

Compaction rules:

```text
active edited function stays exact
public exported type stays exact
large unchanged files can be referenced by path, symbol, and hash
architecture summaries need file refs
```

Block conditions:

```text
needed code path cannot be inspected
symbol resolution is ambiguous
source path changed since projection
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: source_code
strategy: include_exact or include_reference
sourcePath
sourceHash
symbolNames
lineAnchorRefs
```

### Matrix: provider compaction artifact

Source class:

```text
Claude compaction block, OpenAI compacted response object, other provider summary
```

Default strategy:

```text
include_reference until validated
summarize_validated only after claim ledger passes
```

Reason:

```text
provider summary is compressed model output, not primary source
```

Compaction rules:

```text
hash provider artifact
validate claims against source packets
record provider operation metadata
record source window hash
never let provider summary erase protected source obligations
```

Block conditions:

```text
provider artifact lacks source coverage
provider artifact includes unsupported claims
provider operation sourceWindowHash cannot be verified
provider artifact attempts to summarize reference-only material
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: provider_compaction_artifact
strategy: include_reference or summarize_validated
provider
operationName
artifactHash
validationStatus
```

### Matrix: human approval artifact

Source class:

```text
technical-leader approval, manual tool approval, migration gate decision
```

Default strategy:

```text
include_exact
```

Reason:

```text
approval controls authority to execute
```

Compaction rules:

```text
approval status stays exact
approval scope stays exact
approval timestamp/id stays exact
approval comment stays exact unless redaction required
```

Block conditions:

```text
approval scope is ambiguous
approval conflicts with governance instruction
approval artifact cannot be retrieved
```

Trace fields:

```text
sourceClass: human_approval_artifact
strategy: include_exact
approvalId
approvalScope
approvedBy
approvalHash
```

### Source-class conflict policy

When source classes conflict, choose the higher authority source.

Authority order for migration decisions:

```text
governance instruction
technical-leader approval
current operator instruction within approval scope
schema and migration artifacts
Clerk org matrix and runtime access policy
production dataset extract
deterministic transform and transaction plan
verification query/result
tool output
source code
provider compaction artifact
model output
old chat discussion
```

Conflict handling:

```text
same-authority conflict -> block_for_review
lower-authority claim conflicts with higher authority -> omit lower claim with reason
provider summary conflicts with source artifact -> block provider summary
model output conflicts with source artifact -> ignore model output and record reason
operator instruction conflicts with governance -> block_for_review
```

### Source-class report shape

Every projection report should include a source-class summary:

```text
sourceClass
totalPackets
includedExact
includedRedacted
includedReference
summarizedValidated
summarizedLowAuthority
omittedWithReason
blocked
protected
estimatedTokens
actualRenderedTokens if known
```

Example:

```text
sourceClass: production_dataset_extract
totalPackets: 6
includedExact: 0
includedRedacted: 0
includedReference: 6
summarizedValidated: 1
summarizedLowAuthority: 0
omittedWithReason: 0
blocked: 0
protected: 6
estimatedTokens: 840
```

### Summary

The migration source-class matrix prevents a common failure:

```text
treating every old token as equally summarizable
```

For Ekairos, old does not mean low authority.

An old approved transaction plan, an old schema diff, or an old org gate can still be higher authority than a recent model paragraph.

Compaction must follow source authority, not recency alone.

## Blocked-reason operator action catalog

Status: proposal only.

This catalog maps projection block reasons to operator actions.

It is intended for migration compaction sessions, where a blocked projection should lead to a precise next step.

Core rule:

```text
every blocked projection needs a machine-readable reason and a human-readable next action
```

Without this catalog, blocked projection can become a vague failure.

With this catalog, the engine can tell an operator whether to split the task, approve a scope, clean source data, refresh artifacts, or change model profile.

### Catalog entry shape

Each blocked reason should define:

```text
blockedReason
category
severity
providerDispatchAllowed
reactorInvoked
defaultStepStatus
defaultExecutionStatus
operatorActionRequired
allowedNextActions
forbiddenNextActions
requiredEvidence
reportFields
testFixture
```

Status fields require technical-leader approval before implementation.

Until that approval exists, this catalog is descriptive only.

### Reason: projection_tenant_scope_violation

Meaning:

```text
source packets include multiple org scopes or ambiguous org ownership
```

Severity:

```text
critical
```

Provider dispatch:

```text
providerDispatchAllowed: false
reactorInvoked: false
```

Operator action:

```text
split execution by organization or provide explicit approved org matrix
```

Allowed next actions:

```text
rerun projection with one org
attach approved org matrix
remove cross-org source packets
create separate migration sessions per org
```

Forbidden next actions:

```text
summarize cross-org data into one prompt
send mixed-org dataset to provider
choose an org by inference
ignore ambiguous org ownership
```

Required evidence:

```text
blockedSourcePacketIds
detectedOrgIds
expectedOrgScope
orgMatrixSourceHash
```

Test fixture:

```text
blocked_tenant_scope_no_provider_trace
```

### Reason: projection_budget_overflow

Meaning:

```text
required protected context, tool schema budget, and response reserve exceed the model window
```

Severity:

```text
high
```

Provider dispatch:

```text
providerDispatchAllowed: false
reactorInvoked: false
```

Operator action:

```text
split the task or approve a narrower source window
```

Allowed next actions:

```text
split planning from verification
split by org
split by schema entity
split by migration stage
choose a larger approved model profile
reduce action surface if approved
```

Forbidden next actions:

```text
drop protected source packets
summarize exact approval artifacts
omit response reserve
hide tool schema budget
```

Required evidence:

```text
modelWindowTokens
estimatedSystemTokens
estimatedToolSchemaTokens
estimatedProtectedSourceTokens
minimumResponseReserveTokens
estimatedOverflowTokens
```

Test fixture:

```text
blocked_budget_overflow_split_required
```

### Reason: projection_secret_detected

Meaning:

```text
source packets contain token-like, key-like, credential-like, or private runtime material
```

Severity:

```text
critical
```

Provider dispatch:

```text
providerDispatchAllowed: false until redaction passes
reactorInvoked: false
```

Operator action:

```text
redact or replace the secret-bearing source packet with an approved reference
```

Allowed next actions:

```text
redact source packet
replace raw secret with secret handle
include hash only
request operator approval for reference-only handling
rerun redaction scan
```

Forbidden next actions:

```text
send secret to provider
summarize secret value
store secret in trace payload
store secret in provider compaction artifact
```

Required evidence:

```text
secretDetectorId
sourcePacketId
redactionStatus
redactedHash
operatorApprovalId if required
```

Test fixture:

```text
blocked_secret_redaction_no_reactor
```

### Reason: projection_summary_validation_failed

Meaning:

```text
summary candidate contains claims that cannot be linked to source packet ids
```

Severity:

```text
high
```

Provider dispatch:

```text
providerDispatchAllowed: false
reactorInvoked: false
```

Operator action:

```text
review failed claims, restore exact source packets, or split the task
```

Allowed next actions:

```text
rerun summary with stricter prompt
include exact source packets
convert summary to reference-only
split the source window
delete unsupported claims
```

Forbidden next actions:

```text
trust unsupported summary claims
send failed summary as migration context
promote provider summary to source truth
```

Required evidence:

```text
summaryArtifactId
failedClaimIds
sourcePacketCoverage
validationRuleSet
```

Test fixture:

```text
blocked_summary_validation_failed_trace
```

### Reason: projection_approval_missing

Meaning:

```text
requested source class, action surface, provider operation, or runtime behavior needs technical-leader approval
```

Severity:

```text
high
```

Provider dispatch:

```text
providerDispatchAllowed: false
reactorInvoked: false
```

Operator action:

```text
collect explicit approval or reduce scope to an approved slice
```

Allowed next actions:

```text
ask for approval
document exact decision needed
switch to docs-only proposal
remove unapproved provider-native compaction operation
remove unapproved schema/config/runtime change
```

Forbidden next actions:

```text
infer approval from ambiguous text
execute framework/config/infra change
create branch without confirmation
push without approved branch workflow
```

Required evidence:

```text
approvalRequiredFor
missingApprovalType
requestedOperation
currentApprovalArtifacts
```

Test fixture:

```text
blocked_missing_approval_no_provider
```

### Reason: projection_stale_source_hash

Meaning:

```text
source packet hash does not match current source or artifact changed after projection
```

Severity:

```text
medium to high depending on source class
```

Provider dispatch:

```text
providerDispatchAllowed: false for high-authority source classes
reactorInvoked: false when blocked
```

Operator action:

```text
refresh source packet and rerun projection
```

Allowed next actions:

```text
reload source file or artifact
rerun query
recompute hash
refresh line anchors
mark old packet superseded
```

Forbidden next actions:

```text
use stale schema hash
use stale dataset extract for migration decision
silently keep old line anchors
```

Required evidence:

```text
sourcePacketId
oldHash
newHash
sourceClass
stalenessDetectedAt
```

Test fixture:

```text
blocked_stale_source_hash_refresh_required
```

### Reason: projection_trace_write_failed

Meaning:

```text
required durable projection evidence could not be written before provider dispatch
```

Severity:

```text
high for migration sessions
```

Provider dispatch:

```text
providerDispatchAllowed: false if durable evidence is required
reactorInvoked: false
```

Operator action:

```text
restore trace persistence or approve a local durable report path
```

Allowed next actions:

```text
retry trace write
write approved local projection report
pause provider dispatch
inspect trace runtime configuration
```

Forbidden next actions:

```text
send provider request without projection evidence
drop trace payload
mark projection rendered without durable proof
```

Required evidence:

```text
projectionId
traceWriteTarget
errorClass
localReportId if available
providerDispatchAllowed
```

Test fixture:

```text
trace_write_failure_denies_dispatch_when_required
```

### Reason: projection_action_surface_too_large

Meaning:

```text
tool schema/action surface consumes too much model input budget or exposes actions not needed for the current stage
```

Severity:

```text
medium to high
```

Provider dispatch:

```text
providerDispatchAllowed: false when required source context cannot fit with action surface
reactorInvoked: false when blocked
```

Operator action:

```text
approve a narrower action set for the stage
```

Allowed next actions:

```text
restrict tools to current migration stage
split planning from execution
disable write actions during analysis stage
select smaller approved action schemas
```

Forbidden next actions:

```text
drop migration source to keep broad action surface
expose write actions before approval
hide action schema token cost
```

Required evidence:

```text
totalActionSchemaTokens
selectedActionNames
omittedActionNames
stageName
reasonForEachAction
```

Test fixture:

```text
blocked_action_surface_budget_no_provider
```

### Reason: projection_model_profile_missing

Meaning:

```text
projection cannot determine model window, reserve policy, provider capability, or compaction support
```

Severity:

```text
medium
```

Provider dispatch:

```text
providerDispatchAllowed: false for compaction-aware execution
reactorInvoked: false when blocked
```

Operator action:

```text
provide or approve model profile in capability registry
```

Allowed next actions:

```text
select approved model profile
refresh capability registry
disable provider-native compaction for that model
use local validated summary if model is unsupported
```

Forbidden next actions:

```text

assume provider-native compaction exists

```

Required evidence:

```text
requestedProvider
requestedModel

```

Test fixture:


### Reason: projection_provider_artifact_invalid

Meaning:

```text
provider-native compaction artifact failed validation
```

Severity:

```text
high
```

Provider dispatch:

```text
providerDispatchAllowed: false for downstream use of that artifact
reactorInvoked: false for task dispatch that would rely on it
```

Operator action:

```text
discard provider artifact, use local validated summary, or include exact source packets
```

Allowed next actions:

```text
rerun provider compact with approved instructions
run local validated summary
restore exact source packets
split source window
mark provider artifact invalid
```

Forbidden next actions:

```text
use invalid provider summary as source truth
merge invalid artifact into projection manifest
hide validation failure from operator report
```

Required evidence:

```text
provider
operationName
artifactHash
validationErrors
failedClaimIds
sourceWindowHash
```

Test fixture:

```text
blocked_provider_artifact_invalid_no_task_dispatch
```

### Reason: projection_unresolved_conflict

Meaning:

```text
two high-authority sources conflict and no approval resolves the conflict
```

Severity:

```text
high
```

Provider dispatch:

```text
providerDispatchAllowed: false
reactorInvoked: false
```

Operator action:

```text
resolve the conflict explicitly
```

Allowed next actions:

```text
ask technical leader which source wins
mark one source superseded
update migration plan
refresh source packets after decision
```

Forbidden next actions:

```text
let model choose between conflicting high-authority sources
summarize both as equally valid
omit one side without reason
```

Required evidence:

```text
conflictingSourcePacketIds
sourceClasses
authorityLevels
conflictDescription
requiredDecision
```

Test fixture:

```text
blocked_unresolved_high_authority_conflict
```

### Operator report grouping

Blocked reasons should be grouped for operators:

```text
scope and authority
security and redaction
budget and model profile
source freshness
summary validation
trace evidence
provider artifact validation
```

Example report:

```text
projectionStatus: blocked
blockedReason: projection_budget_overflow
category: budget and model profile
providerDispatchAllowed: false
operatorActionRequired: split planning and verification into separate executions
estimatedOverflowTokens: 8500
requiredEvidence: modelWindowTokens, estimatedProtectedSourceTokens, estimatedToolSchemaTokens
nextAllowedAction: split_by_stage
```

### Catalog-level invariants

Invariants:

```text
critical blocked reasons never dispatch provider
blocked reasons are machine-readable
operator actions are human-readable
forbidden next actions are explicit
required evidence is listed
test fixture exists or is proposed
```

Reviewers should reject a blocked reason if:

```text
it has no operator action
it has no required evidence
it allows provider dispatch without explaining why
it can be confused with provider failure
it can be confused with manual approval denial
```

### Summary

Blocked projection is not a dead end.

It is a controlled stop with an action.

For migration compaction, that action is usually one of:

```text
split the task
refresh source
redact source
resolve authority conflict
approve scope
change model profile
validate summary
restore trace evidence
```

That is the difference between a safe compaction gate and a vague runtime failure.

## Org-scoped migration compaction walkthrough

Status: proposal only.

This walkthrough ties together:

```text
source packet classes
projection strategy
provider adapter boundaries
trace events
blocked reasons
operator report
future test assertions
```

It is written as a review scenario for technical-leader approval.

It does not approve implementation.

### Scenario

An operator asks Ekairos to prepare a canary migration for one organization.

The task needs:

```text
current domain schema
target domain schema
Clerk organization matrix
admin runtime resolution
schema dry-run plan
dataset extract
deterministic transform outline
transaction plan draft
verification query set
previous discussion and decisions
```

The context is long enough that raw replay would exceed the target model window after tool schemas and response reserve are included.

The projection system must decide what to include, summarize, reference, omit, or block.

### Source packet inventory

Candidate source packets:

```text
packet:operator-current-turn
packet:governance-workspace-rules
packet:events-current-schema
packet:consumer-target-schema
packet:org-matrix-canary
packet:schema-dry-run-plan
packet:domain-extract-summary
packet:domain-extract-raw
packet:transform-script-draft
packet:transaction-plan-draft
packet:verification-query-list
packet:previous-model-discussion
packet:previous-provider-summary
packet:tool-output-large-query
```

Authority classification:

```text
operator-current-turn: high
governance-workspace-rules: highest
events-current-schema: high
consumer-target-schema: high
org-matrix-canary: high and sensitive
schema-dry-run-plan: high
domain-extract-summary: medium if deterministic
domain-extract-raw: high and sensitive
transform-script-draft: high if active
transaction-plan-draft: high if active
verification-query-list: high
previous-model-discussion: low unless approved
previous-provider-summary: low until validated
tool-output-large-query: medium to high depending on source
```

### First projection plan

The projection builder computes:

```text
modelWindowTokens: 128000
systemTokens: 4300
toolSchemaTokens: 14600
responseReserveTokens: 12000
availableSourceTokens: 97100
protectedSourceEstimate: 81000
summarizableSourceEstimate: 42000
```

The protected source fits only if the projection references raw dataset rows instead of including them exactly.

Strategy plan:

```text
operator-current-turn: include_exact
governance-workspace-rules: include_exact for active constraints
events-current-schema: include_exact for changed entities
consumer-target-schema: include_exact for changed entities
org-matrix-canary: include_reference and include_redacted org ids if approved
schema-dry-run-plan: include_exact
domain-extract-summary: summarize_validated
domain-extract-raw: include_reference
transform-script-draft: include_exact for active function
transaction-plan-draft: include_exact
verification-query-list: include_exact
previous-model-discussion: summarize_low_authority
previous-provider-summary: include_reference until validation
tool-output-large-query: include_reference with output hash
```

Projection status:

```text
renderable if org scope validates
blocked if org scope is ambiguous
blocked if provider summary validation is required but not passed
blocked if exact transaction plan cannot fit
```

### Green path: render and dispatch

Green path prerequisites:

```text
all source packets belong to one canary org
admin token is not rendered
domain extract raw data is reference-only
provider summary is not used as trusted source
transaction plan draft fits exactly
verification queries fit exactly
tool schema budget fits
```

Rendered projection should contain:

```text
current operator instruction
active governance constraints
changed schema snippets
canary org alias and reference id
dry-run plan
validated aggregate extract summary
active transform snippet
transaction plan draft
verification query list
low-authority prior discussion summary
references to raw extract and large query output
```

Rendered projection should not contain:

```text
admin token values
raw full dataset rows
unvalidated provider summary claims
old model guesses as source truth
large query stdout without need
cross-org data
```

Trace sequence:

```text
context.projection.plan.started
context.projection.plan.completed
context.projection.rendered
context.projection.dispatch.allowed
context.llm
context.projection.action.bound if action requested
context.projection.loop.input_bound if loop continues after action
```

Operator report summary:

```text
projectionStatus: rendered
providerDispatchAllowed: true
orgScope: canary org only
protectedSourcePackets: org matrix, raw extract, transaction plan, verification queries
referenceOnlyPackets: raw extract, large query output, provider summary
validatedSummaries: domain extract aggregate
lowAuthoritySummaries: previous model discussion
omittedPackets: obsolete chat chatter
```

Review questions:

```text
does the report show why raw extract was reference-only
does the report show that admin token was absent
does context.llm correlate to renderedInputHash
does the action request bind to projectionId
does shouldContinue input bind to post-action reaction hash
```

### Blocked path: tenant scope violation

Blocked path trigger:

```text
domain-extract-raw contains rows from canary org and production org
org-matrix-canary only approves canary org
```

Projection status:

```text
blocked
```

Blocked reason:

```text
projection_tenant_scope_violation
```

Trace sequence:

```text
context.projection.plan.started
context.projection.plan.completed
context.projection.blocked
context.projection.dispatch.denied
```

Forbidden events:

```text
context.llm
context.projection.rendered
context.projection.dispatch.allowed
provider stream chunks
action execution
```

Operator action:

```text
split execution by organization or attach approved org matrix
```

Operator report:

```text
projectionStatus: blocked
blockedReason: projection_tenant_scope_violation
providerDispatchAllowed: false
reactorInvoked: false
blockedSourcePacketIds: packet:domain-extract-raw, packet:org-matrix-canary
detectedOrgIds: canary org, production org
expectedOrgScope: canary org
operatorActionRequired: split execution by organization
```

Review questions:

```text
did the engine avoid provider dispatch
did the report list ids instead of raw rows
does the operator have one clear next action
does the trace distinguish this from provider failure
```

### Blocked path: provider summary invalid

Blocked path trigger:

```text
previous provider summary says a target field is optional
current target schema says the field is required
summary has no source link for the optional-field claim
```

Projection status:

```text
blocked if the summary is needed for the rendered plan
include_reference if the summary can be ignored
```

Recommended behavior:

```text
ignore invalid provider summary when source schema is sufficient
block only if the operator explicitly asked to rely on that summary or the source schema is missing
```

Blocked reason if blocked:

```text
projection_provider_artifact_invalid
```

Operator action:

```text
discard provider artifact and use source schema, or refresh provider summary with validation
```

Report:

```text
projectionStatus: blocked or rendered_with_invalid_provider_summary_ignored
providerArtifactValidation: failed
failedClaimIds: claim:target-field-optional
higherAuthoritySource: packet:consumer-target-schema
operatorActionRequired: discard provider artifact or refresh validation
```

Review questions:

```text
does higher authority schema override provider summary
does trace show provider artifact remained untrusted
does projection avoid sending invalid claim as source truth
```

### Blocked path: budget overflow

Blocked path trigger:

```text
operator asks for planning, transformation, transaction generation, and verification in one provider call
protected source plus action schemas exceed model window
```

Blocked reason:

```text
projection_budget_overflow
```

Operator action:

```text
split planning and verification into separate executions
```

Recommended split:

```text
execution A: schema dry-run plan and transform outline
execution B: transaction plan with canary org extract
execution C: verification query and report
```

Report:

```text
projectionStatus: blocked
blockedReason: projection_budget_overflow
modelWindowTokens: 128000
estimatedRequiredTokens: 136500
estimatedOverflowTokens: 8500
operatorActionRequired: split planning and verification into separate executions
```

Review questions:

```text
does report expose tool schema budget
does report expose protected source budget
does report avoid dropping protected artifacts
does split preserve source packet lineage
```

### Re-entry after split

After operator chooses a split, each new execution should carry:

```text
parentProjectionId
splitReason
sourcePacketRefs
excludedPacketRefs
newStageName
newBudgetProfile
```

Example:

```text
parentProjectionId: projection:exec_001:step_002:1:budget_block
splitReason: projection_budget_overflow
newStageName: schema_dry_run_plan
sourcePacketRefs: schema, org matrix reference, dry-run plan
excludedPacketRefs: raw extract rows, verification output
newBudgetProfile: planning_only
```

Re-entry trace:

```text
context.projection.plan.started
context.projection.reentry.from_blocked_parent
context.projection.plan.completed
context.projection.rendered
context.projection.dispatch.allowed
```

Candidate re-entry event payload:

```json
{
  "projectionEventName": "context.projection.reentry.from_blocked_parent",
  "parentProjectionId": "projection:exec_001:step_002:1:budget_block",
  "splitReason": "projection_budget_overflow",
  "newStageName": "schema_dry_run_plan",
  "newBudgetProfile": "planning_only"
}
```

### Walkthrough acceptance criteria

The walkthrough passes review when:

```text
green path has source-class strategy for every packet
blocked paths deny provider dispatch
blocked paths have operator actions
trace sequences distinguish projection, provider, action, and loop events
reports use ids and hashes instead of raw sensitive data
re-entry carries parent projection lineage
```

The walkthrough fails review when:

```text
provider summary becomes source truth without validation
cross-org source is summarized instead of blocked
budget overflow drops protected source silently
admin token enters model input
action execution lacks projection id
re-entry loses parent projection id
```

### Summary

This scenario shows why Ekairos compaction should be a projection and audit subsystem.

The same long context can safely produce three outcomes:

```text
rendered provider dispatch
blocked tenant scope with split action
blocked budget overflow with staged re-entry
```

The design is useful only if all three outcomes are explicit, traceable, and reviewable.

```text
context.projection.plan.started
```

## Current source-to-design evidence map

Status: synthesis appendix.

This map connects researched systems to concrete Ekairos design consequences.

It is not a source catalog replacement.

It is a review aid showing why the proposed architecture has the shape it has.

### Claude API compaction -> provider adapter, not policy owner

Observed source behavior:

```text
server-side compaction summarizes older context
compaction block becomes the continuation anchor
content before compaction block is ignored by the API
pause_after_compaction can separate summary generation from continuation
prompt caching can interact with compaction blocks
```

Ekairos consequence:

```text
provider-native compaction can be useful after projection approves source input
provider compaction block must be recorded as provider artifact
provider summary needs validation before migration use
projection manifest must preserve source packet lineage outside provider block
```

Design pressure:

```text
do not let provider-native compaction replace Ekairos source ledger
```

### OpenAI Responses compact -> operation-level trace

Observed source behavior:

```text
compact is exposed as POST /responses/compact
operation returns a compacted response object
model and conversation input are explicit request fields
```

Ekairos consequence:

```text
provider compact should be represented as a separate provider operation
request hash and response hash should be traced
compacted response object should start validationStatus pending
task model dispatch trace should remain separate from compact operation trace
```

Design pressure:

```text
operation-level audit is cleaner than hiding compaction inside reactor internals
```

### Claude Code context window -> re-resolve durable context

Observed source behavior:

```text
/compact replaces conversation with structured summary
system prompt remains outside message history
project-root instructions and auto memory can be re-injected
path-scoped rules may be absent until relevant file context appears
skills have token caps and oldest skill bodies can be dropped
```

Ekairos consequence:

```text
instructions are not all one class
governance and source rules should be re-resolved from source
path-scoped rules need activation evidence
skill or context package bodies need separate budget lines
summary cannot prove which external rules were active
```

Design pressure:

```text
rule activation plane must remain distinct from transcript compaction
```

### Hermes -> two-layer pressure management

Observed source behavior:

```text
gateway session hygiene acts as a high-threshold safety net
agent compressor runs in-loop at lower threshold
cheap tool-output pruning is separate from LLM summary
head and tail protection are explicit
summary model limitations can degrade compaction quality
prompt caching design matters after compression
```

Ekairos consequence:

```text
pressure detection and compaction generation are separate functions
cheap elision should not be confused with summary
protected source classes must survive budget pressure
summary failure should block or split in migration sessions
cache impact belongs in budget ledger
```

Design pressure:

```text
Ekairos needs block-and-split behavior instead of lossy middle-drop behavior for migrations
```

### OpenCode -> explicit compaction messages and structured summaries

Observed source behavior:

```text
compaction has concrete prune and tail constants
summary template has fixed sections
previous summary can be updated
tool output pruning is separate
plugins can add context or prompt material
auto continue can create synthetic user message after compaction
```

Ekairos consequence:

```text
structured summary sections help validation and review
tool output should be its own segment/source class
previous summaries need lineage and drift control
plugin or provider context injection needs source packet ids
auto continuation should be disabled for migration sessions unless approved
```

Design pressure:

```text
summary shape should be fixed enough to validate, not free-form prose only
```

### Cline -> visible compaction and restore thinking

Observed source behavior:

```text
auto compaction is visible as a tool-like step
context pressure and cost are operator-visible
task state is carried through dedicated mechanisms
checkpoints can restore before or after summarization
```

Ekairos consequence:

```text
projection should be visible in traces and operator reports
compaction cost should be measured
task state should not rely only on summary text
raw event replay remains necessary
```

Design pressure:

```text
hidden summarization is unacceptable for migration audit
```

### Cursor and Windsurf -> retrieval and rules are separate controls

Observed source behavior:

```text
rules and memory are durable or semi-durable instruction/context sources
retrieval systems select relevant code and context
fast context or code maps reduce active prompt pollution
activation modes decide when context enters the prompt
```

Ekairos consequence:

```text
retrieval provider API is distinct from compaction
rule activation plane is distinct from memory
source packet authority must track whether context came from rule, retrieval, memory, or transcript
```

Design pressure:

```text
do not build one generic memory table and call it compaction
```

### Framework memory systems -> memory is not migration proof

Observed source behavior:

```text
frameworks provide short-term context and long-term memory abstractions
memory can be semantic, episodic, or procedural
agents can retrieve memory into future turns
```

Ekairos consequence:

```text
memory can assist retrieval but cannot replace migration artifacts
memory entries need authority labels
auto memory should be lower authority than approved source
```

Design pressure:

```text
first implementation should delay auto-memory and focus on projection authority
```

### Local @ekairos/events -> projection fits the durable loop

Observed local behavior:

```text
event_parts is source of truth for persisted parts
context engine expands events before reactor call
reactor returns messagesForModel
action execution receives messagesForModel
shouldContinue runs after action results are merged
trace writer can persist context.llm usage
```

Ekairos consequence:

```text
projection insertion point is after expandEvents and before reactor invocation
renderedInputHash should bind reactor input, action execution, and loop continuation
blocked projection must prevent reactor invocation
context.llm must remain provider usage evidence
```

Design pressure:

```text
runtime dispatch gate must be an engine-level boundary, not provider adapter policy only
```

### Evidence map summary

The researched systems point to a combined design:

```text
provider-native compaction as optional adapter operation
local projection ledger as authority
source-class strategy before token strategy
visible trace and operator report
deterministic blocked dispatch tests
delayed auto-memory
validated summaries with source links
```

No single external system provides the full Ekairos requirement.

The target design is a synthesis tailored to:

```text
domain/schema migration
org-scoped production data
admin runtime actions
auditable provider dispatch
technical-leader approval gates
```
